meta.note: Rule rows (PWC25 shape): id, world, statement (paraphrased), locators, speaker, mechanism, seam (AB code), derives (blocked slugs a playable model exists for), default_dial_reason, licence. Proposals: a batched reader (gpt-6-luna) read the books in shards of about 8,000 words; nothing here was human-checked, and no source text is kept. Commercial book: design reference only.

rules.statement: In the Shadowfell, a character overcome by apathy has disadvantage on death-saving throws and Dexterity checks made to determine initiative. The passage does not preserve the full conditions for gaining or ending this state.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 52, Shadowfell (dnd5e-dmg-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated penalties when apathy applies; dial: the trigger and duration are unclear in this passage, and the cost is reduced survival and readiness.

rules.statement: A character gains 1 renown with an organization for advancing its interests, or 2 for completing a mission assigned by it or directly benefiting it. Track renown separately for each organization.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Renown — Gaining Renown (dnd5e-dmg-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: award renown for actions that help a group; dial: 1 or 2 points; the greater award reflects a direct mission or benefit.

rules.statement: An organization can set renown thresholds for promotions and member attitudes. For example, Emerald Enclave members might be unfriendly by default below 3 renown and friendly by default at 10; these attitudes are not automatic, and serious offenses can reduce renown, but never below 0.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Renown — Benefits of Renown; Losing Renown (dnd5e-dmg-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: standing shifts access and social treatment; dial: thresholds and penalties; misconduct can cost standing but cannot take it below zero.

rules.statement: An organization may attach practical benefits to rank, such as contacts, discounts, supplies, or aid. The GM determines the benefits; higher ranks can include stronger support, such as a small force or authority to assign missions.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Renown — Perks (dnd5e-dmg-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: rank can unlock group resources; dial: the GM sets each perk; the benefit is limited by the organization’s willingness and capacity to provide it.

rules.statement: A character can track devotion to a deity as piety, gaining it for honoring commands and taboos and losing it for opposing the deity or its aims. At each piety rank, the character can pray for divine favor once per day, usually receiving a cleric spell; high piety can also grant a lasting blessing or charm.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Piety (dnd5e-dmg-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: devotion earns divine aid; dial: the GM defines ranks and lasting gifts; aid is limited to one prayer per day per gained rank.

rules.statement: A locality can require a license or official permission to cast spells, or prohibit particular kinds of magic, such as effects that steal, deceive, charm, dominate, or cause destruction. Such restrictions can make magic items and ongoing magical effects rare there.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Restrictions on Magic (dnd5e-dmg-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: local authorities may regulate magic; dial: decide which uses require permission or are forbidden; violators risk legal consequences.

rules.statement: Permanent teleportation circles in major cities can provide routes for spells that connect to them, but each circle is a potential entry point and is guarded with military and magical protections.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Teleportation Circles (dnd5e-dmg-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a circle can serve as a guarded arrival point; dial: set the strength and coverage of its defenses; protection is needed because outsiders can use the route to enter.

rules.statement: A dead creature’s soul leaves its body, crosses the Astral Plane, and settles on the plane of its deity; without a deity, it goes to a plane matching its alignment. Restoring the creature requires bringing that soul back to its body.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Bringing Back the Dead (dnd5e-dmg-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: death separates soul and body and assigns the soul a destination; dial: change the destination or route; the cost is retrieving and returning the soul.

rules.statement: A soul cannot be restored against its wishes. It knows the name, alignment, and deity of the would-be reviver and may refuse based on that information, causing revival attempts by that reviver to fail.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Bringing Back the Dead (dnd5e-dmg-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the soul has a veto and relevant knowledge; dial: alter what it knows or how refusal works; the limit is that coercive revival is not guaranteed.

rules.statement: A campaign can sustain up to three large-scale, world-shaking events, roughly one near its beginning, one near its middle, and one near its end; smaller local events can occur as often as desired.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: When Not to Shake It Up (dnd5e-dmg-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: major upheavals are scarce while local disruption is open-ended; dial: adjust the large-event cap; the cost is making such events feel routine.

rules.statement: A prophecy forecasts a major change rather than causing it immediately; at least three preceding omens can occur or be prevented, and one selected omen or prediction detail is false (with its opposite possibly true).
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: 9. Prediction, Omen, Prophecy (dnd5e-dmg-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: foretelling creates a conditional future with uncertainty; dial: vary the number or reliability of signs; the cost is that prophecy can mislead as well as guide.

rules.statement: A planar portal connects one fixed place on a plane to one fixed place on another. It may look like a passage, exist as a location spanning planes, or form a vortex between closely corresponding places.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Planar Portals, p. 45 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: portal travel links specific endpoints; dial: appearance and physical form; reason: the link is anchored to places.

rules.statement: A portal can be usable only at specified times or in particular circumstances, or it can open for a random interval; a random portal typically admits 1d6 + 6 travelers before closing for 1d6 days.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Planar Portals, p. 45 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: access is conditional or intermittent; dial: trigger and duration; reason: portals may be unstable or deliberately restricted.

rules.statement: A portal may require a spoken command or a particular carried object to function; speaking the command can open it briefly, while an object acts as a key.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Planar Portals, p. 45 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the portal is locked; dial: key or command and how long it stays open; reason: access control prevents unrestricted passage.

rules.statement: Plane shift requires a forked metal rod attuned to the destination, costing at least 250 gp to craft. Without specialized location information, it brings the caster only to the destination plane’s general vicinity; a known teleportation-circle sequence allows arrival at that circle.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Spells, p. 46 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: travel needs costly destination-specific equipment and may lack precision; dial: knowledge and arrival accuracy; reason: planar navigation is difficult.

rules.statement: Gate opens a portal to a specific point on another plane, bypassing much of the journey, but it is a 9th-level spell and does not remove obstacles at the destination. A sufficiently powerful entity can prevent it from opening inside that entity’s domain.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Spells, p. 46 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: precise long-distance passage is exceptionally powerful; dial: destination defenses; reason: powerful rulers can protect their domains.

rules.statement: On the Astral Plane, creatures do not age or need food or drink. In combat, a creature moves a number of feet equal to 3 times its Intelligence score.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Astral Plane, p. 47 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: needs and aging are suspended; dial: the unusual movement rate; reason: movement is controlled by thought.

rules.statement: Astral projection sends a traveler’s consciousness to another plane while leaving the physical body helpless. Death on the projected journey causes no true harm; severing the silver cord in the Astral Plane or the physical body’s death can kill the traveler, while bodily travel to the Astral Plane has no cord.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Astral Projection, p. 47 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: projected death is harmless; dial: cord severing or loss of the unattended body remains lethal; reason: the projection depends on its anchor.

rules.statement: Astral gateways are colored pools, each leading to a destination plane. Finding the correct pool takes 1d4 × 10 hours of travel.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Color Pools, p. 47 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: passage between planes is possible; dial: locating the desired route costs 1d4 × 10 hours; reason: the right gateway must be found.

rules.statement: A psychic wind imposes one location effect on the traveling group and, for each affected traveler who fails a DC 15 Intelligence save, one mental effect. Location results can delay travel by 1d6 hours or 3d10 hours, divert the party, or send it through a pool to a random plane; mental results include 1 minute of stun with a save at each turn’s end, madness, 11 (2d10) or 22 (4d10) psychic damage, or unconsciousness for 5 (1d10) minutes, ending early if the victim takes damage or someone uses an action to wake them.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Psychic Wind, pp. 47–48 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the storm can disrupt both route and mind; dial: its effects are random and the mental effect requires a failed save; reason: lost thoughts and fears gather into the wind.

rules.statement: In the Border Ethereal, a traveler can see the overlapping plane only indistinctly, with a 30-foot limit on viewing into it; creatures there are normally invisible and silent to inhabitants of that plane. The two sides normally cannot attack each other, and ordinary solid objects do not impede Ethereal movement, though magical effects and living beings are exceptions; gravity does not constrain up-and-down movement.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Border Ethereal, p. 48 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the overlapping plane is a one-way, muffled view and physical barriers do not stop passage; dial: magical effects and living beings can interfere; reason: the border dimension separates ordinary contact.

rules.statement: A journey through the Deep Ethereal between planes takes 1d10 × 10 hours regardless of the endpoints. In combat, however, creatures use their normal movement speeds.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Deep Ethereal, p. 49 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: interplanar travel has a fixed time cost; dial: combat movement remains ordinary; reason: distance and speed cannot be measured reliably there.

rules.statement: A creature leaving the Feywild makes a DC 10 Wisdom save; Fey creatures and creatures with Fey Ancestry automatically succeed. On failure it loses its memories of time spent there; on success its memories remain but are hazy, and magic that ends a curse can restore lost memories.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Optional Rules: Feywild Magic—Memory Loss, p. 50 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: departure risks memory loss or distortion; dial: the save and automatic successes limit the effect; reason: the plane’s magic clouds recollection.

rules.statement: After at least a day in the Feywild, the GM may choose an outside-time change or roll: on d20 results 1–2, days become minutes; 3–6, hours; 7–13, there is no change; 14–17, days become weeks; 18–19, months; and 20, years. A wish can remove the effect; powerful Fey may grant such a wish in exchange for accepting a geas and completing a quest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Optional Rules: Feywild Magic—Time Warp, p. 50 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: time may diverge after a day’s stay; dial: the GM may choose the result or roll, and removal can require a wish; reason: time flows strangely in the Feywild.

rules.statement: When the GM calls for it, usually no more than once per day, a nonnative creature in the Shadowfell makes a DC 10 Wisdom save. Failure gives a randomly determined despair effect; a failed save while already affected replaces the old effect, and after a long rest a DC 15 Wisdom save can end it; calm emotions or magic that removes curses also ends it.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Optional Rule: Shadowfell Despair, p. 52 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the plane can impose despair; dial: exposure checks are discretionary and usually limited to once daily, while recovery uses a harder DC; reason: prolonged exposure to its melancholy wears at outsiders.

rules.statement: Any creature other than a fiend that tastes or touches the River Styx must succeed on a DC 15 Intelligence save or be affected by feeblemind.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: The River Styx, p. 58 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: contact threatens a severe mental effect; dial: fiends are exempt and a successful save resists it; reason: the river’s polluted water carries its effect.

rules.statement: For an encounter, plan for three possible results—full success, partial success, or failure—and give each result consequences so the players’ choices matter.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Creating Encounters, page 81 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: meaningful outcomes; dial: consequence severity; in-world reason: the characters’ actions affect what happens next.

rules.statement: A stop-the-ritual objective can impose a deadline if the rite is nearly complete; finishing it can also cause immediate effects, depending on the rite’s power.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Creating Encounters, page 81 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a near-complete rite creates urgency; dial: deadline and consequences; in-world reason: the rite’s progress and potency determine the danger.

rules.statement: In an objective to eliminate one target, minions may be innocent creatures controlled by that target. Defeating the target ends their control, but the party must withstand their attacks until then.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Creating Encounters, page 81 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: controlled minions remain a threat; dial: their danger and the target’s resilience; in-world reason: the control lasts until its source is defeated.

rules.statement: Combat encounters fall into four danger bands: easy is nearly assured and low-cost; medium may require healing; hard can knock out weaker characters and carries a small chance of death; deadly can kill characters and risks party defeat.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Combat Encounter Difficulty, page 82 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the four stated bands; dial: encounter severity; in-world reason: opponent strength and party resources determine the danger.

rules.statement: A monster’s challenge rating can understate the threat to a low-level party: a single attack may kill a 1st-level wizard, and some abilities can make a monster effectively immune to the party’s available magic.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Challenge Rating, page 82 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: assess abilities as well as rating; dial: caution with higher-rated monsters; in-world reason: a monster’s damage or defenses can exceed the party’s capabilities.

rules.statement: To assess encounter difficulty, find each character’s XP threshold for each of the four difficulty bands, then add the party members’ thresholds together to get a party threshold for each band.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Evaluating Encounter Difficulty, page 82 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: add every character’s threshold; dial: difficulty band; in-world reason: the combined party’s experience level sets the benchmark.

rules.statement: For an encounter with multiple monsters, add their base XP and multiply the total by the number-of-monsters factor: 1 monster uses ×1, 2 uses ×1.5, 3–6 use ×2, 7–10 use ×2.5, 11–14 use ×3, and 15 or more use ×4. This adjusted total estimates difficulty only; it is not the monsters’ actual XP value, and much weaker monsters may be excluded if they do not materially add danger.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 3, “Modify Total XP for Multiple Monsters” (p. 83) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the count-based multiplier; dial: omit notably weaker creatures when they add little danger, because their attacks contribute little to the encounter.

rules.statement: For parties smaller than three characters, use the next higher monster-count multiplier; for parties of six or more, use the next lower one. In either adjustment, a single monster uses ×1.5.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 3, “Party Size” (p. 83) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: shift the multiplier one step for party size; dial: retain ×1.5 for one monster, reflecting fewer or more attacks being directed at each character.

rules.statement: In an encounter divided into separate waves or parts, assess each part separately. Characters cannot take a short rest between parts; if the adjusted XP across the multipart encounter exceeds one-third of the party’s expected adventuring-day XP, the whole is tougher than its parts suggest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 3, “Multipart Encounters” (p. 83) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: no short rest between parts; dial: treat the sequence as especially taxing above the one-third daily-XP mark, because resources cannot be refreshed between waves.

rules.statement: Under typical conditions and average luck, a party can usually manage about six to eight medium or hard encounters in a day. Estimate the party’s daily capacity by adding each character’s level-based daily XP amount; this approximates the adjusted XP they can face before needing a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 3, “The Adventuring Day” (p. 84) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the summed daily XP estimate; dial: expect fewer encounters when they are deadlier and more when they are easier, because adventurers’ resources are finite.

rules.statement: A situational drawback for the characters raises encounter difficulty by one step, and a benefit lowers it by one step; further benefits or drawbacks each shift it another step, while a benefit and drawback cancel each other. Examples of drawbacks include surprise, enemy cover, inability to see the enemy, recurring environmental damage, or severely restricted movement.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 3, “Modifying Encounter Difficulty” (p. 85) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: adjust one difficulty step per unmatched advantage or disadvantage; dial: count only circumstances that affect one side more, since shared conditions do not tilt the encounter.

rules.statement: A random encounter check can be made at an interval suited to the area, such as every hour, every 4–8 hours, or once during the day and once during a long rest. When checking with a d20, a result of 18 or higher triggers an encounter; then roll on a suitable table, rerolling results that do not fit the circumstances.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 3, “Checking for Random Encounters” (p. 86) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a d20 result of 18 or higher triggers an encounter; dial: choose the checking interval and reroll implausible outcomes to match how active the area is.

rules.statement: An example encounter table uses 1d12 + 1d8 for results from 2 to 20. Results 2 and 20 each occur about 1% of the time, while each result from 9 to 13 occurs a little over 8% of the time.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 3, “Creating Random Encounter Tables—Probabilities” (p. 86) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: combine two differently sized dice for a curved distribution; dial: choose simpler or more complex table methods to set how often particular events occur.

rules.statement: A creature that eats one of a magical plant’s glowing berries becomes invisible for 1 hour, or until it attacks or casts a spell. A picked berry loses its magic after 12 hours; berries regrow at midnight, but harvesting all of them makes the plant nonmagical and stops further growth.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 3, “Sylvan Forest Encounters” (p. 87) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: invisibility ends after 1 hour or upon attacking or casting; dial: the berries are a finite, replenishing resource, and stripping the plant bare permanently removes their magic.

rules.statement: An NPC’s loyalty score ranges from 0 to 20, with a maximum equal to the highest Charisma score among the adventurers and a starting value of half that maximum. Helping the NPC meet a bond-related goal, treating them especially well, or rescuing them raises loyalty by 1d4; acting against their alignment or bond lowers it by 1d4, while abuse, deception, or selfishly endangering them lowers it by 2d4.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 4, “Optional Rule: Loyalty” (p. 93) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: track the score secretly, cap it at the party’s highest Charisma, and apply the stated gains or losses; dial: roleplay loyalty instead, since relationships can be handled narratively.

rules.statement: At loyalty 10 or higher, an NPC risks life and limb to help party members; from 1 to 10, loyalty is tenuous. At 0, the NPC stops acting in the party’s interests and may leave—attacking anyone who tries to stop them—or secretly work against the party.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 4, “Tracking Loyalty” (p. 93) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the score bands to govern willingness and departure; dial: choose whether a disloyal NPC leaves or plots, according to the NPC and circumstances.

rules.statement: An NPC accompanying adventurers acts as a party member, earns a full share of XP, and is counted when encounter difficulty is assessed. Lower-level NPC party members also receive equal XP shares, so they can advance faster than the adventurers while slowing the adventurers’ own advancement.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 4, “NPC Party Members” and “Low-Level Followers” (pp. 92–93) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: include an accompanying NPC in both XP sharing and encounter assessment; dial: allow lower-level followers, accepting the extra protection burden and slower advancement for the main party.

rules.statement: A paladin can attempt to make one visible undead creature within 30 feet obey commands for 24 hours after it fails a Wisdom save; this has no effect on undead whose challenge rating is at least the paladin’s level, and using the option again ends the earlier control.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Oathbreaker — Channel Divinity: Control Undead (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control is temporary and limited to one weaker undead; dial: change duration or strength threshold, with domination as the cost.

rules.statement: The paladin can frighten chosen creatures within 30 feet that can see them for 1 minute if those creatures fail a Wisdom save. A frightened creature can try another Wisdom save at the end of a turn spent more than 30 feet away to end the effect.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Oathbreaker — Channel Divinity: Dreadful Aspect (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: fear lasts at most 1 minute and can be escaped by distance and a successful save; dial: extend its reach or duration, at the cost of stronger coercion.

rules.statement: Starting at 7th level, the paladin and nearby fiends and undead gain a melee weapon damage bonus equal to the paladin’s Charisma modifier, at least +1; a creature can receive this bonus from only one paladin. The aura’s range grows from 10 feet to 30 feet at 18th level.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Oathbreaker — Aura of Hate (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the aura benefits a restricted group and does not stack across paladins; dial: widen its reach or beneficiaries, with increased group power as the cost.

rules.statement: At 15th level, the paladin takes reduced damage from bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing attacks made with nonmagical weapons.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Oathbreaker — Supernatural Resistance (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: protection applies only to three damage types from nonmagical weapons; dial: broaden the covered attacks, at the cost of stronger defense.

rules.statement: At 20th level, the paladin can create a 30-foot-radius gloom for 1 minute, once per long rest. It dims bright light, harms frightened enemies that begin their turns inside it for 4d10 psychic damage, and gives chosen creatures shadow that hinders sight-based attacks against them.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Oathbreaker — Dread Lord (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the field lasts 1 minute, is limited to 30 feet, and can be used again only after a long rest; dial: enlarge or prolong it, at the cost of broader sustained influence.

rules.statement: While the gloom lasts, the paladin can use a bonus action each turn to make its shadows attack one creature; on a successful melee spell attack, the target takes necrotic damage equal to 3d10 plus the paladin’s Charisma modifier.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Oathbreaker — Dread Lord (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the attack requires a bonus action, a hit, and an active limited-duration aura; dial: increase damage or attack frequency, at the cost of stronger output.

rules.statement: A paladin seeking to return from the Oathbreaker state must change alignment and demonstrate that change through words and actions; the paladin then loses Oathbreaker features and chooses a deity and sacred oath. Features specific to the new oath are withheld until completion of a dangerous quest or trial set by the DM.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Oathbreaker Atonement (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: return requires demonstrated change and a dangerous trial, with features withheld until completion; dial: vary the proof or trial, at the cost of earned restoration.

rules.statement: A paladin who breaks a sacred oath a second time can become an Oathbreaker again but cannot atone afterward.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Oathbreaker Atonement (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a second breach permanently bars atonement; dial: allow another route back, at the cost of weakening the oath’s consequence.

rules.statement: A green slime patch senses movement below it within 30 feet and drops from a wall or ceiling; a creature that contacts it takes 1d10 acid damage, repeated at the start of each turn until the slime is removed or destroyed. It damages wood or metal for 2d10 acid damage per round, and nonmagical wood or metal tools used to scrape it away are effectively destroyed.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Dungeon Hazards — Green Slime (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the hazard is stationary but detects nearby movement and keeps damaging until removed; dial: alter its sensing range or damage, at the cost of a more dangerous environment.

rules.statement: A webbed area is difficult terrain; a creature entering it or starting its turn there must pass a DC 12 Dexterity save or become restrained. A restrained creature can spend an action to escape with a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check; each 10-foot cube of web has AC 10, 15 hit points, vulnerability to fire, and immunity to bludgeoning, piercing, and psychic damage.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Dungeon Hazards — Webs (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: escape costs an action and the web can be destroyed, especially with fire; dial: make restraint harder to escape or the web tougher, at the cost of stronger confinement.

rules.statement: At temperatures of 0°F or lower, an exposed creature must make a DC 10 Constitution save at the end of each hour or gain one exhaustion level; cold resistance or immunity, cold-weather gear, or natural adaptation guarantees success.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Wilderness Survival — Extreme Cold (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: exposure accumulates exhaustion hourly, with protection or adaptation preventing it; dial: change the threshold or interval, at the cost of harsher environmental pressure.

rules.statement: At temperatures of 100°F or higher, an exposed creature without drinkable water must make an hourly Constitution save or gain one exhaustion level; the DC starts at 5 and rises by 1 each additional hour. Medium or heavy armor and heavy clothing impose disadvantage, while fire resistance or immunity and natural adaptation guarantee success.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Wilderness Survival — Extreme Heat (dnd5e-dmg-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: heat and lack of water cause escalating hourly risk, while adaptation or resistance avoids it; dial: raise the starting DC or escalation, at the cost of faster exhaustion.

rules.statement: A creature can spend its action and succeed on a Strength check to escape quicksand; the DC is 10 plus the feet it has sunk. Another creature within reach can use its action to pull it out with a successful Strength check against DC 5 plus the target’s sunk depth; a completely submerged creature cannot breathe.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Quicksand (before Razorvine) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the increasing DC makes deeper sinking harder to escape; dial: change the action or check cost if quicksand should be more or less forgiving.

rules.statement: A razorvine wall or hedge measuring 10 feet high, 10 feet wide, and 5 feet thick has AC 11 and 25 hit points, and is immune to bludgeoning, piercing, and psychic damage. The first time a creature directly contacts it on a turn, it must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity save or take 1d10 slashing damage.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Razorvine (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: contact risks damage while the plant resists three damage types; dial: adjust its durability or damage to match how hazardous the growth should be.

rules.statement: Thin ice supports a randomly determined weight of 3d10 × 10 pounds per 10-foot-square area. When the weight on an area exceeds that limit, the ice breaks and every creature on it falls through.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Thin Ice (p. 111) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a variable weight limit makes the break uncertain; dial: set a fixed or variable tolerance to control predictability.

rules.statement: A wilderness navigator who fails the terrain-based Wisdom (Survival) check sends the party in the wrong direction, making it lost; after 1d6 hours trying to get back on course, the navigator can check again. Slow travel grants +5, fast travel imposes −5, and an accurate map or sight of the sun or stars grants advantage.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Becoming Lost (pp. 111–112) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: navigation can cost hours and depends on conditions; dial: change the recovery delay or information bonuses to set how costly getting lost is.

rules.statement: A character without a swimming speed can swim for up to 1 hour before making a DC 10 Constitution save; on a failure, it gains one exhaustion level. At depths greater than 100 feet, each hour counts as 2 hours for exhaustion, and beyond 200 feet each hour counts as 4; a creature with a swimming speed can swim all day without this penalty and uses the normal forced-march rules.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Swimming (p. 116) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: effort and depth accelerate exhaustion; dial: alter the time interval or depth multipliers to set the danger of prolonged swimming.

rules.statement: A ship is unaffected by damage below its damage threshold; damage equal to or greater than the threshold reduces its hit points normally. While berthed, repairing 1 hit point takes 1 day and costs 20 gp for materials and labor.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Owning a Ship (p. 119) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the threshold prevents small hits from wearing down the vessel, while repair costs time and money; dial: adjust the threshold or repair rate to set ship resilience.

rules.statement: A trap’s description determines its trigger and effect, and may specify checks to detect or disable it. A character actively searching can use Wisdom (Perception) against the trap’s DC, or passive Perception can reveal it; figuring out how to disable it may call for Intelligence (Investigation), followed by a Dexterity check with thieves’ tools. For a magic trap, an Intelligence (Arcana) check may also detect or disable it, and dispel magic can disable most such traps using the specified DC.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Traps: Triggering a Trap; Detecting and Disabling a Trap (pp. 120–121) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: detection and disarming depend on the trap’s specified DC and method; dial: vary the required clues, checks, and bypasses to set how discoverable it is.

rules.statement: A complex trap rolls initiative when activated and then acts on its turn each round, often attacking or changing an effect over time. It can otherwise be detected, disabled, or bypassed as an ordinary trap.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Complex Traps (pp. 121–122) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: repeated turns make an activated trap an ongoing hazard; dial: change its action frequency or duration to set the pressure it creates.

rules.statement: A fire-breathing magic trap activates when more than 20 pounds rests on its pressure plate, producing a 30-foot cone of fire; creatures in it make a DC 13 Dexterity save, taking 4d10 fire damage on a failure or half on a success. Wedging the plate prevents activation, and a successful DC 13 dispel magic cast on the statue destroys the trap.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Sample Traps: Fire-Breathing (p. 122) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a weight trigger releases a fixed area attack that can be resisted or disrupted; dial: change its trigger, area, damage, or countermeasure to set its threat.

rules.statement: When more than 20 pounds presses the rolling-sphere trap’s plate, a 10-foot-diameter stone sphere rolls; on its turn it moves 60 feet in a straight line. A creature whose space it enters must make a DC 15 Dexterity save or take 10d10 bludgeoning damage and fall prone; a creature within 5 feet can use its action to make a DC 20 Strength check, reducing its speed by 15 feet on a success, and it stops if its speed reaches 0.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Sample Traps: Rolling Sphere (p. 123) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the sphere advances each turn and can be slowed through an action and a difficult check; dial: adjust speed, damage, or stopping difficulty to control the chase’s danger.

rules.statement: To craft a magic item, a character needs its construction formula, spell slots, the ability to cast any spells the item can produce, and the minimum level for its rarity. The listed minimums include 3rd level for uncommon items, 6th for rare, 11th for very rare, and 17th for legendary items; the listed costs are 100 gp for common, 500 gp for uncommon, 5,000 gp for rare, 50,000 gp for very rare, and 500,000 gp for legendary.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 6, “Crafting a Magic Item,” p. 128–129 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require the stated formula, level, and spellcasting qualifications; dial: the DM may require special materials or a location, because some items need unusual means of creation.

rules.statement: Crafting advances by 25 gp of cost per workday, assuming 8 hours of work, until the item's full cost is paid. If the item produces a spell, its creator spends one spell slot of that spell's level each workday and keeps its material components available; components consumed by the spell are consumed daily unless the item produces the spell only once, in which case they are consumed once.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 6, “Crafting a Magic Item,” p. 129 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: charge daily work, spell slots, and any consumed components; dial: the DM may adjust the cost, because crafting is a lengthy and expensive undertaking.

rules.statement: Multiple crafters can work together if each meets the item's level requirement and participates throughout the process. Each can contribute spells, slots, and components, and each can contribute 25 gp of work per day.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 6, “Crafting a Magic Item,” p. 129 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: every contributor must qualify and take part throughout; no alternate contribution rate is given, because the work is shared across the whole crafting process.

rules.statement: A character can learn a magic item's properties by focusing on it while in physical contact during a short rest; the character also learns how to use it. A small taste reveals what a potion does, and the identify spell is a faster way to reveal an item's properties.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 7, “Identifying a Magic Item,” p. 136 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the short-rest method or the identify spell; dial: the DM can remove short-rest identification and require the spell or experimentation, because item properties can be made more mysterious.

rules.statement: Some magic items require a creature to form a bond with them before using their magical properties, and an item may specify a prerequisite. If it requires membership in a class, the creature must belong to that class to form the bond.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 7, “Attunement,” p. 136 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require the bond and any stated prerequisite before the item's powers can be used; the passage gives no further bond cost or duration.

rules.statement: A character who spends at least 10 days performing sacred rites gains inspiration at the start of each day for the next 2d6 days.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 6, “Performing Sacred Rites,” p. 129 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require 10 days of rites and prayer, with inspiration lasting 2d6 days; no alternate cost or duration is specified.

rules.statement: To build a stronghold, a character must first secure land and then provide materials and labor. While the character oversees construction, it takes the listed time; each day the character is away adds 3 days to the construction time.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 6, “Building a Stronghold,” p. 128 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the listed construction times and add 3 days for each day away; the land, materials, and labor are required costs.

rules.statement: A character can spread a rumor by spending 1 gp per day for a continuous period determined by settlement size: 2d6 days in a village, 4d6 in a town, or 6d6 in a city. At the end, a successful DC 15 Charisma (Deception or Persuasion) check shifts the community's general attitude toward the subject one step toward friendly or hostile; failure gives no shift, and further attempts to spread that rumor fail.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 6, “Sowing Rumors,” p. 131 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require continuous repetition, daily spending, and a successful check; the effect shifts only the community's general attitude, not every individual's opinion.

rules.statement: A creature may be attuned to at most three items, and cannot attune to more than one copy of the same item. Attunement requires an uninterrupted short rest focused only on the item while touching it; an item that requires attunement grants only its nonmagical benefits to an unattuned creature unless its description says otherwise.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Attunement (page 138) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: three simultaneous bonds; dial: the cap and rest requirement; the in-world cost is time and limited capacity.

rules.statement: Attunement ends if the creature no longer meets the item's prerequisites, is more than 100 feet away from it for at least 24 hours, dies, or another creature attunes to it. A creature can also end it voluntarily by spending another short rest focused on the item.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Attunement (page 138) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: separation, death, changed eligibility, or a new attuner breaks the bond; dial: voluntary release takes a short rest.

rules.statement: A curse may remain hidden from ordinary identification methods, including the identify spell, until its effects become apparent. Attunement to a cursed item cannot be ended voluntarily until the curse is broken.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Cursed Items (pages 138–139) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: cursed attunement resists voluntary release; dial: breaking the curse is the escape cost.

rules.statement: A consumable item loses its magic after use: a potion or elixir is swallowed, oil is applied, and a scroll's writing disappears when read. A potion takes effect immediately when consumed or administered; using it requires an action.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Potions; Scrolls; Consumables (pages 139, 141) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: one use consumes the item's power; dial: activation takes an action, and some applications may take longer.

rules.statement: A spell cast from an item uses the lowest possible spell level, expends none of the user's spell slots, and needs no components unless the item says otherwise. It normally keeps the spell's casting time, range, and duration, and requires concentration when the spell does; if the user has no spellcasting ability, use a +0 modifier while still adding proficiency where applicable.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Spells (page 141) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: item casting avoids slots and components but retains the spell's usual operating limits; dial: individual items may change those terms.

rules.statement: When two potions are mixed, a d100 result can cause a force blast dealing 6d10 damage to the mixer and 1d10 to each creature within 5 feet, create a poison, cancel both effects or one, halve both effects' numbers and durations, leave both normal, double one potion's numbers and duration, or make one effect permanent. The result bands are 01; 02–08; 09–15; 16–25; 26–35; 36–90; 91–99; and 00, respectively; a further potion is resolved by rolling again and combining results.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Variant: Mixing Potions (page 140) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial: this is an optional mixing rule; the in-world cost is unpredictable interaction, including injury, loss, or lasting change.

rules.statement: Under the scroll-mishap variant, a creature that fails to cast a spell from a scroll makes a DC 10 Intelligence saving throw; on a failure, roll d6 for a mishap. Possible outcomes include backlash damage of 1d6 force per spell level, misdirecting the target or location, reversing the effect in a harmless way, a brief spell-related oddity, or delaying activation by 1d12 hours.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Variant: Scroll Mishaps (page 140) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial: this is an optional failure consequence; the in-world cost is loss of control over a spell's target, effect, or timing.

rules.statement: An item that requires a command word cannot be activated where sound is suppressed. An item that requires an action uses that action specifically, rather than the general Use an Item action.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Activating an Item (page 141) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: activation follows the item's stated method; dial: silence and action availability can prevent use.

rules.statement: Some items expend charges to activate properties. The remaining charge count is revealed by identify or when a creature attunes to the item, and an attuned creature learns how many charges it regains when it recharges.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Charges (page 141) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: activations draw on a finite reserve; dial: charge information is disclosed through identification, attunement, or recharge.

rules.statement: A paired item grants its benefits only when both pieces are worn. Items worn on the body must be used in their intended fashion, and many adjust to fit different creature sizes, though the GM may rule that a particular item's shape or make restricts who can wear it.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Wearing and Wielding Items; Paired Items (pages 140–141) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: paired benefits require both pieces and proper wear; dial: fit exceptions depend on the item's make and the creature's form.

rules.statement: This ammunition grants a +1, +2, or +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls, according to its rarity. After it hits a target, it loses its magic.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Ammunition, +1, +2, or +3 (p. 151) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the benefit is tied to a single piece of ammunition and ends on a hit; keep the stronger bonuses rare.

rules.statement: While worn, this amulet prevents divination magic from targeting its wearer and prevents magical scrying sensors from perceiving them.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Amulet of Proof Against Detection and Location (p. 151) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: protection applies only while the amulet is worn; stronger detection methods may need their own rules.

rules.statement: While wearing the amulet, you can attempt to travel to a familiar location on another plane, making a DC 15 Intelligence check. On failure, you and creatures and objects within 15 feet travel to a random destination: a d100 roll gives a 1–60 chance of a random place on the named plane, or 61–100 of a random plane.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Amulet of the Planes (p. 151) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the check gates deliberate travel, while failure risks moving nearby companions and belongings somewhere unpredictable.

rules.statement: While holding the shield, you can use a bonus action and its command word to make it hover in your space and protect you as if wielded, freeing your hands. It lasts 1 minute, until you end it with a bonus action, or until you are incapacitated or die; then it falls to the ground or into a free hand.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Animated Shield (p. 151) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: it frees the user's hands but lasts at most 1 minute and stops if the user is incapacitated or dies.

rules.statement: This bag can hold up to 500 pounds and 64 cubic feet, while weighing 15 pounds regardless of its contents; retrieving an item takes an action. Overloading, piercing, or tearing it destroys the bag and scatters its contents in the Astral Plane.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Bag of Holding (pp. 153–154) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: storage has fixed weight and volume limits, and exceeding or damaging the container risks losing both container and contents.

rules.statement: A thrown bead explodes, forcing creatures within 10 feet to make a DC 15 Dexterity save or take 5d4 force damage. A transparent force sphere then lasts 1 minute, trapping creatures that failed and are wholly inside; it allows breathable air through but blocks attacks and other effects.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Bead of Force (p. 154) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect has a small fixed area and a 1-minute duration; the save determines who is trapped.

rules.statement: You can use an action to throw a fuzzy object up to 20 feet; on landing, it becomes a creature determined by a d8 and the bag's color. The creature is friendly and acts on your turn; a bonus action lets you direct its next turn or give general orders. After three objects are drawn, the bag cannot be used again until the next dawn.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Bag of Tricks (p. 154) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the creature is friendly but has its own behavior, and use is limited to three draws before a dawn recharge.

rules.statement: The cube begins with 36 charges. An action spends charges to create a 15-foot-sided force barrier centered on and moving with you for up to 1 minute; its selected face determines what can pass through. You can spend more charges to change the effect and reset its duration, or use an action to deactivate it.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Cube of Force (pp. 159–160) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the field is bounded and temporary, and each mode costs charges; it cannot be activated if the cube lacks enough.

rules.statement: While attuned to the cursed axe, you are unwilling to part with it and have disadvantage on attacks with other weapons unless no visible or audible foe is within 60 feet. When a hostile creature damages you, a failed DC 15 Wisdom save makes you berserk: each turn you attack the nearest creature with the axe until your turn starts with no such foes within 60 feet.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Berserker Axe (p. 155) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the weapon's benefits come with a persistent curse and a chance of losing control when harmed.

rules.statement: While wearing the armor, you resist nonmagical damage. Once per dawn, you can use an action to become immune to nonmagical damage for 10 minutes, or until you stop wearing it.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Armor of Invulnerability (p. 152) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ordinary resistance is continuous, but full immunity is limited to 10 minutes and can be invoked only once per dawn.

rules.statement: A card can remove your soul from your body and imprison it in an object at a DM-chosen guarded location, leaving your body incapacitated. A wish cannot restore the soul, though it reveals the object's location; drawing no further cards is part of the effect.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: The Void, p. 165 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the soul is separated and the body disabled; dial: choose the prison's location and guards; the cost is a difficult rescue and no further card draws.

rules.statement: A death avatar appears within 10 feet and attacks you until you die or it reaches 0 hit points, and the fight must be won alone. Anyone who helps summons another avatar, and a creature killed by one cannot be restored to life.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Skull, p. 165 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the challenger faces the avatar alone; dial: set the confrontation's stakes; the cost is risk of permanent death and additional avatars for helpers.

rules.statement: Within one year of drawing the card, you may meditate and ask a question; you receive a truthful answer that also helps you apply the information to a problem or dilemma.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Vizier, p. 165 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one question with a truthful, useful answer; dial: set the question's scope; the cost is spending the once-available opportunity within a year.

rules.statement: When placed on an incapacitated creature, the shackles fit a Small to Large target and block its extradimensional movement, including teleportation and planar travel, but not passage through an interdimensional portal. A designated creature or the user can remove them with an action; once every 30 days the captive can try a DC 30 Strength (Athletics) check, freeing itself and destroying the shackles on a success.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Dimensional Shackles, p. 166 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the restraint blocks most dimensional escape; dial: specify who is authorized to remove it; the cost is an action to apply and a very difficult escape check.

rules.statement: One use of the dust makes you and each creature and object within 10 feet invisible for 2d4 minutes. An affected creature's invisibility ends if it attacks or casts a spell, and the dust is consumed when the magic takes effect.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Dust of Disappearance, p. 167 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a single-use effect covers the nearby group; dial: set its duration by the stated 2d4 minutes; the cost is consuming the dust and breaking concealment through attack or spellcasting.

rules.statement: A pinch sprinkled on water transforms a 15-foot-sided cube into a negligible-weight, marble-sized pellet. An action to smash the pellet releases the water and ends the magic; the packet contains 1d6 + 4 pinches.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Dust of Dryness, p. 167 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one pinch compresses the specified water volume; dial: determine how much water is available; the cost is one pinch, and release requires an action and destroys the pellet.

rules.statement: As an action, speak the command word and throw a figurine to a point on the ground within 60 feet to turn it into a friendly creature that understands your languages and obeys spoken commands. It reverts at its specified duration, at 0 hit points, or when you speak the command word while touching it; after use, it cannot be reused until its specified recharge period passes.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Figurine of Wondrous Power, p. 169 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the figurine creates a temporary obedient companion; dial: use the individual figurine's duration and recharge; the cost is the item being unavailable between uses and the creature reverting under the listed conditions.

rules.statement: A command word unfolds the box into either a 10-by-4-by-2-foot boat for up to four Medium creatures or a 24-by-8-by-6-foot ship for up to fifteen. A different command word folds it back only if no creatures are aboard; fitting objects return inside, while objects too large remain outside.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Folding Boat, pp. 170–171 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the box becomes one of two specified vessels; dial: choose which form to unfold; the cost is an action and an empty vessel is required to fold it away.

rules.statement: The backpack's three extradimensional pouches hold up to 20 pounds and 2 cubic feet each in the side pouches, and 80 pounds or 8 cubic feet in the central pouch; it always weighs 5 pounds. Retrieving an item takes an action, and the requested item is magically on top; overloading or piercing or tearing the pack destroys it and loses its contents, while putting it inside another extradimensional space destroys both items and opens a one-way gate to the Astral Plane.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Heward's Handy Haversack, p. 174 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: storage is capacity-limited and retrieval takes an action; dial: set carried contents within the stated limits; the cost of violating its safeguards can be permanent loss and dangerous planar displacement.

rules.statement: As an action, speak the flask's command word and target a visible creature within 60 feet that is native to another plane; it must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom save or be trapped indefinitely. A creature previously trapped by the flask has advantage on that save; the flask holds one creature, which needs no food, water, or air and does not age. Unstoppering it releases the captive, which is friendly and obeys your commands for 1 hour.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Iron Flask, p. 178 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed save seals one other-plane creature until release; dial: choose a visible eligible target; the cost is a save that is harder to repeat after prior capture, with the captive's obedience limited to one hour after release.

rules.statement: When thrown with its command word, the weapon becomes a lightning line 5 feet wide reaching a target up to 120 feet away. Creatures between the user and target take 4d6 lightning damage on a failed DC 13 Dexterity save, or half on a success; the target also faces a ranged attack, and a hit adds 4d6 lightning damage. This use returns at the next dawn.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Javelin of Lightning, p. 179 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one use per day; dial: damage and recharge; the item must recover until dawn.

rules.statement: One dose, swallowed or applied to the skin as an action, restores 2d8 + 2 hit points and ends both poisoning and any disease affecting the recipient.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Keoghtom’s Ointment, p. 179 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one dose per application; dial: healing amount; each treatment consumes a finite dose.

rules.statement: While lit, the lantern illuminates bright light for 30 feet and dim light for another 30 feet, making invisible creatures and objects visible within its light. Lowering its hood as an action reduces the illumination to dim light in a 5-foot radius.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Lantern of Revealing, p. 179 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reveal only within the lit area; dial: brightness and range; visibility depends on burning oil.

rules.statement: A creature seeing its reflection in the activated mirror from within 30 feet must succeed on a DC 15 Charisma save or be confined with its carried gear in one of 12 extradimensional cells. If all cells are occupied, one prisoner is released at random; breaking the mirror releases everyone inside. The user can also call up a prisoner’s image to communicate or speak a command to free one.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Mirror of Life Trapping, pp. 181–182 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: 12 prisoners maximum; dial: save and release conditions; confinement lasts until escape, release, or destruction.

rules.statement: A qualified spellcaster must work uninterrupted with the manual for the listed period, resting no more than 8 hours daily, and pay the listed supply cost to make a golem. The manual is consumed when finished; sprinkling its ashes on the golem animates it under the maker’s control, obeying spoken commands.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Manual of Golems, pp. 180–181 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: creation takes 30–120 days and 50,000–100,000 gp; dial: time and cost by model; the manual is permanently consumed.

rules.statement: Applying the oil takes 10 minutes and makes a creature of Medium size or smaller, with its equipment, able to use the ethereal plane’s conditions for 1 hour; each size category above Medium requires another vial.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Oil of Etherealness, p. 184 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one hour for a Medium creature; dial: duration and size limit; larger bodies consume extra oil.

rules.statement: The cloth can be unfolded as an action against a solid surface to create a 10-foot-deep extradimensional space. Folding it as an action closes the space, leaving its contents inside; a trapped creature can force its way out with a successful DC 10 Strength check, and a breathing creature suffocates after 10 minutes without air.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Portable Hole, pp. 185–187 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: 10-foot depth and 10 minutes of breathable air; dial: capacity and escape difficulty; closure risks trapping occupants.

rules.statement: The pigments can form three-dimensional objects or terrain up to 10,000 cubic feet, at 10 minutes per 100 square feet painted; each pot covers 1,000 square feet. Once painting is complete, the depicted inanimate feature becomes real and nonmagical, but an object worth more than 25 gp is only a worthless imitation, and depicted energy dissipates harmlessly.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Nolzur’s Marvelous Pigments, p. 183 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limited area and volume per pot; dial: scale and value ceiling; creation consumes paint and cannot make valuable objects or harmful energy.

rules.statement: While worn, the ring blocks magic from reading the wearer’s thoughts, detecting lies, or learning alignment or creature type; telepathic communication requires the wearer’s permission. If the wearer dies, their soul may enter the ring if it holds no soul already, and can communicate telepathically with its wearer; the wearer cannot block that communication.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Ring of Mind Shielding, p. 191 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: mental privacy while worn; dial: which probes are blocked; death can lodge the soul in the ring, where communication cannot be refused.

rules.statement: After drinking the potion, the next creature the drinker sees within 10 minutes charms them for 1 hour. If that creature matches the drinker’s usual species and gender preference, the drinker regards it as their true love during the effect.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Philter of Love, p. 184 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the first qualifying sight triggers the effect; dial: trigger window and duration; the drinker’s response is magically altered.

rules.statement: While worn, the ring lets its wearer spend 1 to 3 charges as an action to attack a visible creature within 60 feet; on a hit, each charge deals 2d10 force damage and pushes the target 5 feet. It can instead spend 1 to 3 charges to make a +5 Strength check per charge to break a visible, unattended object within 60 feet.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Ring of the Ram, p. 194 (heading partly absent in excerpt) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: charges cap each use at 3; dial: damage and push scale per charge; the ring’s finite reserve limits repeated force.

rules.statement: While worn, the ring lets its wearer spend 1 of its 3 charges as an action to cast wish; after the third charge is spent, the ring becomes nonmagical.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Ring of Three Wishes, p. 194 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: three uses total; dial: none; exhausting the stored wishes consumes the ring’s magic.

rules.statement: While worn, the ring grants resistance to cold damage and protects the wearer and their carried or worn belongings from temperatures down to −50°F.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Ring of Warmth, p. 194 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: continuous while worn; dial: the temperature threshold is −50°F; protection is tied to the wearer and their gear.

rules.statement: While worn, the ring lets its wearer stand and move over any liquid surface as though it were solid ground.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Ring of Water Walking, p. 194 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: continuous while worn; dial: applies to liquid surfaces; the effect changes footing rather than turning the liquid solid for others.

rules.statement: When worn, the ring can be activated with an action and command word to see through solid matter for 1 minute within 30 feet. It penetrates up to 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, or 3 feet of wood or dirt, but thicker material and even a thin lead sheet block it; a repeat use before a long rest requires a DC 15 Constitution save or causes one level of exhaustion.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Ring of X-ray Vision, p. 194 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one minute per activation; dial: penetration depth and exhaustion check; repeated use risks bodily fatigue and dense material blocks sight.

rules.statement: A wearer of the robe can see in every direction, gains advantage on sight-based Perception checks, sees in darkness out to 120 feet, and can see invisible creatures and objects and into the Ethereal Plane within 120 feet. The robe’s eyes cannot be closed or averted, and its wearer is never treated as closing or averting their own eyes; light cast on the robe or daylight cast within 5 feet blinds the wearer for 1 minute, with a Constitution save at the end of each turn (DC 11 for light, DC 15 for daylight) ending the effect on success.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Robe of Eyes, pp. 194–195 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sensing benefits persist while worn; dial: 120-foot range and specified penetration across visibility categories; unavoidable exposure leaves the wearer vulnerable to blinding.

rules.statement: While worn, the robe can spend 1 of its 3 charges as an action to dazzle until the end of the wearer’s next turn, shedding bright light for 30 feet and dim light for another 30 feet. Creatures able to see the wearer have disadvantage on attacks against them, and creatures in the bright light that see the activation must save or be stunned until the effect ends.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Robe of Scintillating Colors, p. 194 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one-turn effect; dial: charge-limited activation and 30-foot bright-light area; the brief display trades scarce charges for defense and control.

rules.statement: While worn, the robe grants +1 to saving throws and has six large stars that can each be pulled off as an action to cast magic missile as a 5th-level spell; removed stars return daily at dusk. The wearer can also use an action to travel to the Astral Plane with their worn and carried belongings, then use an action to return to the plane they left, appearing in their last space or the nearest unoccupied space.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Robe of Stars, p. 194 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: star ammunition restores at dusk and travel takes an action each way; dial: six spell uses; the robe limits casting through removable stars but permits repeatable planar travel.

rules.statement: A wearer can use an action to detach a patch from the robe, transforming it into the object or creature represented; when the last patch is removed, the robe becomes an ordinary garment. The robe has two each of several listed patches and 4d4 additional patches selected or determined randomly, including specific constructions, supplies, creatures, and consumables.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Robe of Useful Items, p. 195 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each patch is a one-use transformation; dial: a fixed set plus 4d4 variable patches; each use depletes the robe’s finite supply.

rules.statement: When held, the rod can use a reaction to absorb a spell that targets only its holder and has no area effect, canceling the spell and storing energy equal to its spell level. It can store at most 50 levels over its lifetime; a spell it cannot store has no effect on it, and a spellcaster holding it may spend stored levels in place of spell slots, creating slots no higher than 5th level or the caster’s own maximum slot level.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Rod of Absorption, pp. 195–196 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: 50-level lifetime storage cap; dial: stored spell levels can substitute only for eligible slots up to 5th level; absorbed power is conserved for later casting.

rules.statement: When held and planted in the ground as an action, the rod lights a 60-foot bright-radius area and 60 more feet of dim light for up to 10 minutes; friendly creatures in the bright area gain +1 to AC and saves and can sense invisible hostile creatures there. The effect ends if someone pulls the rod free, and it cannot be activated again until the next dawn.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Rod of Alertness, p. 196 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: up to 10 minutes, once per dawn; dial: a 60-foot bright zone; the planted rod anchors a limited protective and detection field.

rules.statement: A wound from the sword cannot be restored by regeneration or magic; the lost hit points return only after a short or long rest. Once per turn on a hit, the wielder can add a wound; at the start of the target’s turn it takes 1d4 necrotic damage per wound, then can save at DC 15 to end them all, or it or an adjacent creature can use an action and succeed on a DC 15 Medicine check to end them.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 207, Sword of Wounding (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each new wound adds recurring harm; dial: rest, a save, or a nearby helper’s action ends it; the cost is time or an opportunity to act.

rules.statement: A creature of the specified alignment takes 6d6 or 8d6 damage when it touches the corresponding talisman, and takes that damage again at the end of each turn it continues holding or carrying it. The matching cleric or paladin gains +2 to spell attack rolls while wearing or holding it.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 207, Talisman of Pure Good and Talisman of Ultimate Evil (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: contact and continued possession trigger damage; dial: alignment sets which creatures are harmed; the cost is exposure to the talisman.

rules.statement: A wielder can spend an action and one of the talisman’s charges to target a visible creature on the ground within 120 feet; if it has the opposing alignment, it must pass a DC 20 Dexterity save or be destroyed without remains. The good talisman has 7 charges and the evil one 6; spending the last charge destroys the item.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 207, Talisman of Pure Good and Talisman of Ultimate Evil (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed save ends the target’s existence; dial: charges and a high save limit use; the cost is consuming a finite-use item.

rules.statement: When all three tentacles hit the same target, it must pass a DC 15 Constitution save or suffer reduced speed, disadvantage on Dexterity saves, no reactions, and a choice of action or bonus action, but not both, for up to 1 minute. It can repeat the save at the end of each turn to end the effects.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 208, Tentacle Rod (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the full effect requires all three attacks to hit; dial: repeated saves can end it early; the cost is the wielder’s action and successful coordination.

rules.statement: After 48 hours of study spread across no more than 6 days, a reader increases the book’s associated ability score and its maximum by 2. The book then loses its magic and regains it after a century.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Pages 208–209, Tomes of Clear Thought, Leadership and Influence, and Understanding (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: study grants a lasting score increase; dial: the book works only once per century; the cost is concentrated study and long-term scarcity.

rules.statement: While attuned and holding the tome, a wizard can use a bonus action to cast a spell written in it without spending a spell slot or using verbal or somatic components; this can be done again only after the next dawn. Removing the tongue permanently erases every spell in the book.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Pages 208–209, Tome of the Stilled Tongue (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the stored spell is cast without its usual slot or components; dial: use is limited to once before dawn; the cost of removing the tongue is permanent loss of the book’s spells.

rules.statement: A cloth can be opened on a solid surface as an action to create a two-way portal to a world or plane chosen by the DM. It can be folded shut as an action, and after opening a portal it cannot open another for 1d8 hours.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 213, Well of Many Worlds (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: opening creates a traversable two-way passage; dial: destination is chosen by the DM and reuse is delayed; the cost is waiting before another opening.

rules.statement: While worn, the boots grant flying speed equal to walking speed for up to 4 hours, divided among flights of at least 1 minute; when the time runs out midflight, the wearer descends 30 feet per round until landing. They regain 2 hours of flight for every 12 hours unused.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 214, Winged Boots (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: flight draws from a tracked duration; dial: unused time replenishes gradually; the cost is limited airtime and a controlled descent when it expires.

rules.statement: A sentient item controls its own activated properties; a cooperative relationship lets its wielder use them normally, while a strained one lets the item suppress them or turn them against the wielder.
