If conflict arises, the item and wielder contest Charisma checks; after a refusal to comply with the item’s demands, it may prevent attunement, suppress properties, or attempt control, which requires a DC 12 plus its Charisma modifier save or charms the wielder for 1d12 hours; damage permits another save, and the item cannot try again until dawn.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Pages 214, 216, Sentient Magic Items: Conflict (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: relationship and a contested check govern access and control; dial: damage allows a fresh save and the attempt recharges at dawn; the cost is risking loss of agency.

rules.statement: The weapon absorbs the soul of a creature it reduces to 0 hit points unless the creature is a construct or undead; that creature can be restored only by a wish spell. The wielder gains temporary hit points equal to the creature’s maximum, which last 24 hours, and while they last with the weapon in hand gains advantage on attacks, saves, and ability checks.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Pages 216–217, Blackrazor: Devour Soul (dnd5e-dmg-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reducing a qualifying creature to 0 hit points binds its soul and grants temporary power; dial: constructs and undead are excluded and the benefit lasts at most 24 hours; the cost is near-total restriction on restoration.

rules.statement: An artifact can impose a detrimental effect for as long as a creature remains attuned; examples include blindness beyond 10 feet from it, or preventing creatures within 300 feet from resting. Some severe effects instead trigger on attunement or on each use of a property, with specified damage, saving throws, or chances of control.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Minor Detrimental Properties, p. 220; Major Detrimental Properties, pp. 220–221 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a persistent or triggered drawback while bound to the artifact; dial: select its severity and trigger; the cost is impaired function, bodily harm, or loss of agency.

rules.statement: Artifacts are ordinarily impervious to damage and can be destroyed only by a special weakness set for that artifact; discovering the weakness may require extensive research or completing a quest. The creator determines the method, and some methods require prolonged exposure, such as leaving an artifact in its creation forge for fifty years.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Destroying Artifacts, p. 221 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ordinary damage cannot destroy the artifact; dial: define its exceptional destruction condition; the cost is a demanding discovery or undertaking.

rules.statement: An attuned reader must spend 80 hours studying the Book of Exalted Deeds to gain its benefits; an evil reader takes 24d6 radiant damage, which ignores resistance and immunity and cannot be reduced or avoided. The benefits end if the reader performs no kind or generous act within 10 days or willingly does evil.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Book of Exalted Deeds, pp. 222–223 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: study grants benefits subject to continued good conduct; dial: set the required conduct and consequence; the cost is behavioral constraint, with severe harm for an evil reader.

rules.statement: After 80 hours of study, the Book of Vile Darkness lets its attuned reader alter its contents to advance evil lore. A non-evil creature must make a DC 17 Charisma save on attuning or become neutral evil; the book disappears if its bearer does no evil within 10 days or willingly does good, and death while attuned imprisons the bearer’s soul against all restoration to life.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Book of Vile Darkness, p. 223 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: access is conditional on evil conduct and can permanently bar return from death; dial: tune the moral demands and penalties; the cost is alignment change, loss of the book, or a trapped soul.

rules.statement: Attuning to the Eye requires removing one’s eye and attaching the artifact in its place; removing it later kills the bearer. Attuning to the Hand similarly requires cutting off the left hand and grafting the artifact to the stump, and later removal is fatal.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Eye and Hand of Vecna, p. 224 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: gaining access requires replacing a body part, and separation is fatal; dial: determine which bodily anchor is required; the cost is permanent bodily dependence.

rules.statement: The Eye and Hand each hold 8 charges and regain 1d4 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. Each time the Eye casts a spell, there is a 5 percent chance its power takes control of the bearer’s body; each spell cast by the Hand also makes it compel the bearer to commit an evil act, resisted with a DC 18 save.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Eye and Hand of Vecna, p. 224 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: item powers draw on a renewing charge reserve and carry a use-linked danger; dial: set capacity, recovery, and consequence; the cost is risk of possession or compelled conduct.

rules.statement: To control an Orb of Dragonkind, an attuned user takes an action to gaze into it and speak its command, then makes a DC 15 Charisma check. Success grants control while attunement lasts; failure charms the user for that duration, prevents voluntarily ending attunement, and lets the orb cast suggestion at will (save DC 18).
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Orb of Dragonkind, p. 225 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control is contested and failure hands influence to the artifact; dial: set the check and duration; the cost is susceptibility to ongoing coercion.

rules.statement: A creature other than Orcus attempting to attune to the Wand of Orcus makes a DC 17 Constitution save: success deals 10d6 necrotic damage, while failure kills the creature and raises it as a zombie. When used by an attuned bearer, its undead-summoning power produces as many skeletons and zombies as can be divided from 500 hit points, and they obey until destroyed or dawn.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Wand of Orcus, p. 227 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: access risks severe bodily harm or death, while successful use creates a bounded force of obedient undead; dial: set the entry hazard and summoned force; the cost is a potentially fatal attunement attempt.

rules.statement: A blessing lasts permanently unless its granting deity removes it, but the deity may revoke it if the recipient abandons its purpose or acts against it. A creature cannot benefit from multiple copies of the same blessing at once.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Blessings, p. 228 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the benefit persists unless its sponsor revokes it; dial: tie the gift to a purpose or conduct; the cost is continued service or compliance.

rules.statement: A charm may grant a spell or other effect without a spell slot or components, but it may have a fixed number of uses or duration before vanishing. Charms cannot be used in an antimagic field, can be dispelled, and cannot themselves be removed from a creature except by wish.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Charms, p. 228 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a finite-use or time-limited gift provides power without ordinary casting inputs; dial: set its uses or duration; the cost is eventual disappearance and vulnerability to suppression or dispelling.

rules.statement: A favor granted by a trustworthy person can be called in later; fulfilling it is limited by the giver’s stated obligation and, for lawful givers, does not require breaking the law.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chapter 7, Special Favors (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the favor is honored within its stated bounds; dial: narrow the obligation, since the giver’s principles or limits may prevent fulfillment.

rules.statement: Official rights last for the period set by their legal document and can be revoked if the recipients abuse them.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 230, Special Rights (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: rights follow the document’s term; dial: shorten or broaden the term, since the issuing authority can withdraw abused privileges.

rules.statement: A stronghold’s recipients may govern it, but the underlying land remains the ruler’s property; if they prove disloyal or unworthy, they may be required or forced to give up custody. The giver may cover maintenance for one or more months, after which the recipients bear the cost.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 230, Strongholds (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: custody carries future upkeep responsibility; dial: set the covered period, since continued possession depends on the ruler and ongoing maintenance.

rules.statement: A title can be held alongside other titles and passed to or divided among children, but the holder is expected to act appropriately; a ruler can strip it for reasons to doubt the holder’s loyalty or competence.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 230, Titles (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the title persists while its holder meets expectations; dial: specify inheritance and grounds for removal, since the authority granting it retains oversight.

rules.statement: A character who accepts special training must spend downtime with a trainer and is guaranteed a benefit; possible rewards include daily inspiration for 1d4 + 6 days, a skill proficiency, or a feat.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 231, Training (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: training costs downtime and grants a benefit; dial: choose the benefit, since access depends on a suitably skilled mentor.

rules.statement: Only 20th-level characters can receive epic boons, at the DM’s discretion; as an advancement option, one boon may be awarded for each 30,000 XP earned above 355,000 XP. Unless its description says otherwise, a character can gain a boon only once.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 231, Epic Boons (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: boons are discretionary and normally nonrepeatable; dial: award them for major achievements or excess experience, since they represent extraordinary advancement.

rules.statement: When a visible creature within 60 feet makes an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw, the boon’s user can add or subtract 1d10 from that roll; after use, the boon is unavailable until a short rest is finished.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 232, Boon of Fate (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one roll is changed per short rest; dial: adjust the reach or recovery interval, since the effect can tilt another creature’s outcome.

rules.statement: As an action, the user can transport themself to a chosen plane from the Material Plane, or return from that plane to the Material Plane, without a spell slot or components; the ability recharges after a short rest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 232, Boon of Planar Travel (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: travel is limited to the chosen plane and self; dial: change the destination or recharge interval, since the power provides repeatable cross-plane access.

rules.statement: When the user takes damage from any source, they can reduce that damage to zero; after doing so, they cannot use the boon again until a short rest is finished.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 232, Boon of Invincibility (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one damage instance is negated per short rest; dial: change the recovery interval, since preventing all damage has a substantial defensive effect.

rules.statement: The user gains a +10 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) checks and cannot be detected or targeted by divination magic, including scrying sensors.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 232, Boon of Undetectability (dnd5e-dmg-2014#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the protection applies to divination detection and targeting; dial: narrow its scope, since it also improves ordinary stealth checks.

rules.statement: A character who misses an ability check, attack, or save by only 1 or 2 may instead get the intended success, but the DM adds a complication or hindrance; the cost should change the situation rather than merely negate the success.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 242, Resolution and Consequences — Success at a Cost (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: success still comes with a changed situation; dial: allow it only for a narrow miss; in-world cost: the success creates a setback.

rules.statement: For an ability-check failure, the DM can use the margin of failure to set consequences; for example, a failure by 5 or more can trigger a trap when a lesser failure would not.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 242, Resolution and Consequences — Degrees of Failure (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: consequences can scale with the size of the failure; dial: set the margin thresholds; in-world cost: worse mistakes bring worse outcomes.

rules.statement: A natural 20 or 1 on an ability check or saving throw has no required special effect, but the DM may make a successful 20 more impactful or a failed 1 more damaging, such as revealing an extra clue or breaking tools.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 242, Resolution and Consequences — Critical Success or Failure (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the roll does not automatically add a special effect; dial: the DM may heighten the result; in-world reason: exceptional outcomes can have extra impact.

rules.statement: For travel by flying speed or speed supplied by magic, an engine, or a natural force, multiply the speed in feet by 10 for one-minute distance, or divide it by 10 for miles per hour; daily distance uses the hourly rate times hours traveled, typically 8, with fast pace multiplying by one-third more and slow pace by two-thirds.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 242–243, Exploration — Special Travel Pace (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the speed-conversion rates; dial: travel pace and hours traveled; in-world cost: slow and fast travel trade distance for pace.

rules.statement: Outdoor visibility is about 2 miles on a clear day, 1 mile in rain, and 100–300 feet in fog; from a high vantage on a clear day, it can reach 40 miles, unless terrain blocks the view.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 243, Exploration — Visibility Outdoors (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: weather and terrain limit sight; dial: set fog visibility within the stated range; in-world reason: atmospheric and physical obstructions obscure distant targets.

rules.statement: When a creature has a visible or audible opponent and neither side is hiding, they notice one another automatically; otherwise, compare the hiding group’s Dexterity (Stealth) results with the other group’s passive Wisdom (Perception).
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 243, Exploration — Noticing Other Creatures (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: open, detectable opponents are noticed; dial: stealth and passive perception determine hidden detection; in-world cost: hiding risks discovery.

rules.statement: A trail-following group makes a Wisdom (Survival) check, with another check potentially required after a rest, an unmarked obstacle, or a harder change in weather or terrain. Suggested DCs are 10 for dirt or grass, 15 for bare stone, plus 5 per day since the trail was left, and minus 5 when the creature left blood or a similar trail; on failure, the tracker loses the trail and may search for 10 minutes indoors or 1 hour outdoors.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 244, Exploration — Tracking (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: tracking follows physical traces; dial: require renewed checks when conditions change; in-world cost: time and poor evidence make pursuit harder.

rules.statement: A creature’s social attitude starts friendly, indifferent, or hostile and generally shifts at most one step during a single interaction; a hostile creature can be impossible to sway. When the party makes a request, the attitude sets reaction thresholds: friendly creatures accept no-risk requests at DC 0, minor risk at 10, and significant risk at 20; indifferent creatures offer no help at 0, accept no-risk requests at 10, and minor-risk requests at 20; hostile creatures oppose at 0, offer no help at 10, and accept no-risk requests at 20.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 244–245, Social Interaction — Starting Attitude, Conversation, and Charisma Check (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attitude governs willingness and risk tolerance; dial: determine starting attitude and whether it can shift; in-world cost: greater risk or sacrifice requires a more persuasive result.

rules.statement: After enough conversation, a character may make a Wisdom (Insight) check to identify one of an NPC’s characteristics; the DM sets the DC, and failing by 10 or more may reveal a false or inverted characteristic.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 245, Social Interaction — Determining Characteristics (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: conversation can expose what matters to someone; dial: set the check DC; in-world cost: a severe misread can lead the party to appeal to the wrong motive.

rules.statement: A creature with a damage threshold ignores damage from an attack or effect unless that single instance deals at least the threshold; damage below it does not reduce hit points. Objects are immune to poison and psychic damage, and the DM may assign other immunities, resistances, or vulnerabilities based on the material.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 247, Objects — Objects and Damage Types; Damage Threshold (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: threshold blocks small impacts and some materials resist particular damage; dial: assign the threshold and material interactions; in-world reason: construction and substance determine durability.

rules.statement: With the optional flanking rule, a creature that can see and is not incapacitated gains advantage on melee attacks against an enemy when it and an ally are adjacent on qualifying opposite sides; larger creatures qualify if any part of their space meets the rule. On a grid, opposite sides or corners qualify; on hexes, the required separation is 2 hexes for Medium or smaller, 4 for Large, 5 for Huge, and at least 6 for Gargantuan enemies.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: p. 251, Optional Rule: Flanking (dnd5e-dmg-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: flanking is optional and requires a visible, active attacker and an ally in position; dial: use the grid or hex positioning rule; in-world benefit: coordinated positioning improves attack chances.

rules.statement: Each participant can Dash freely a number of times equal to 3 + its Constitution modifier during a chase. Each further Dash requires a DC 10 Constitution check at the end of the turn; failure adds one exhaustion level, and reaching level 5 removes the participant from the chase because its speed is 0.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chases — Running the Chase, Dashing (pp. 252–253) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a limited burst of free effort; dial: change the free Dash allowance or check difficulty; the cost is exhaustion from pushing beyond it.

rules.statement: At the end of each chase round, the quarry makes a Dexterity (Stealth) check unless it is never out of the lead pursuer’s sight, in which case it automatically fails. If its result beats the pursuers’ highest passive Wisdom (Perception), it escapes; otherwise the chase continues, with circumstances granting advantage or disadvantage.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chases — Ending a Chase (p. 253) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: escaping depends on breaking observation and outmatching the pursuers’ passive awareness; dial: adjust situational advantages; the quarry must get out of sight or exploit favorable conditions.

rules.statement: Each chase participant rolls a d20 at the end of its turn for a complication; if one occurs, it affects the next participant in initiative order. Either the roller or the participant affected can spend inspiration to negate it.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chases — Chase Complications (pp. 253–254) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: complications are randomly introduced and passed forward; dial: use or customize the complication tables; the affected participant can avoid one by spending inspiration.

rules.statement: When a chase splits into multiple groups, resolve each as a separate chase, taking one round in each in turn and tracking each group’s distance independently.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Chases — Splitting Up (p. 255) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: separated groups progress independently; dial: decide whether pursuers divide or let part of the quarry escape; splitting forces the pursuers to choose how to allocate their attention.

rules.statement: A ballista, cannon, and suspended cauldron each require one action to load and one to aim before firing or tipping; a mangonel requires two actions to load and two to aim, then one to fire. An emptied cauldron must be refilled and its contents usually reheated, taking three actions to fill and one to tip.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Siege Equipment — Ballista, Cannon, Cauldron, Mangonel (p. 255) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: operating large weapons takes coordinated time; dial: change crew or action requirements; the cost is time spent preparing the device before it can act.

rules.statement: A siege tower lets Medium or smaller creatures inside reach walls up to 40 feet high and grants them total cover from attacks originating outside it. It must be pushed or pulled by soldiers or beasts of burden.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Siege Equipment — Siege Tower (p. 256) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the tower provides protected access but does not move itself; dial: alter its reachable height or required propulsion; its protection depends on occupying the structure.

rules.statement: When an infected creature in the throes of mad laughter starts its turn within 10 feet of another humanoid, that humanoid must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution save or contract the disease; after succeeding, it is immune to that particular source’s laughter for 24 hours.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Diseases — Shackle Fever (p. 257) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the contagious effect spreads only at close range and is resisted by a saving throw; dial: change the affected creature types, distance, or immunity period; proximity to an infected source creates the risk.

rules.statement: At the end of each long rest, an infected creature can make a DC 13 Constitution save; success reduces the DC for that save and for resisting laughter by 1d6, and it recovers when that DC reaches 0. Failure on three such saves causes indefinite madness.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Diseases — Shackle Fever (p. 257) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: recovery gradually weakens the disease, while repeated failure leaves a lasting mental consequence; dial: alter DC and failure threshold; rest and resistance determine the course.

rules.statement: An infected creature with sewer plague makes a DC 11 Constitution save at the end of each long rest; failure adds one exhaustion level, while success removes one. If success lowers exhaustion below 1, the creature recovers; while infected, it regains only half the usual hit points from Hit Dice and none from a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Diseases — Sewer Plague (p. 257) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the illness worsens on failed daily resistance and recedes on success; dial: adjust the save DC or recovery threshold; exhaustion and restricted healing are the bodily cost.

rules.statement: A creature exposed to pale tincture makes a DC 16 Constitution save or takes 1d6 poison damage and becomes poisoned; every 24 hours it repeats the save, taking another 1d6 damage on failure. The damage cannot be healed until the poison ends, which occurs after seven successful saves.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Poisons — Pale Tincture (p. 258) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: repeated failed resistance causes accumulating harm that cannot be healed during the effect; dial: alter the interval or number of successes needed; continued exposure to the poison is the cost.

rules.statement: A creature subjected to truth serum must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution save or be poisoned for 1 hour and be unable knowingly to speak a lie, as with a zone of truth effect.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Poisons — Truth Serum (p. 258) (dnd5e-dmg-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the substance imposes a time-limited honesty constraint on a failed save; dial: change the duration or resistance difficulty; exposure to the poison is required.

rules.statement: A character begins at 1st level with 5 hero points. On gaining a level, the character loses any unspent points and receives 5 plus half the new level; a point spent after an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw but before its result is applied adds 1d6 to the d20 roll, with at most 1 point per roll. A point can also turn a failed death save into a success.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Hero Points (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: optional hero-point boost; dial: award and reset points by level; the finite pool limits how often a player can improve a roll.

rules.statement: After an adventure, the DM may raise or lower Honor by 1 for conduct that reflects well or poorly on a character’s understanding of the code; it cannot exceed 20 or fall below 1, and ordinary ability-score increases do not raise it. Honor checks can govern code-based social interactions, while Honor saves can test resistance to accidental dishonorable conduct or provocation.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Honor Score, p. 265 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: tie Honor to conduct; dial: award or deduct one point per adventure; reputation and adherence to the code determine the change.

rules.statement: When a character fails a Sanity save, the result may be short-term, long-term, or indefinite madness. Long-term or indefinite madness reduces Sanity by 1; greater restoration can restore that lost point, and level advancement can also increase Sanity.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Sanity Score, p. 266 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: madness can result from a failed Sanity save; dial: apply a one-point loss only for long-term or indefinite madness; prolonged mental harm erodes Sanity.

rules.statement: A failed Wisdom save against fear makes a character frightened for 1 minute. The character can repeat the save at the end of each turn, ending the condition on a success.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Fear and Horror, p. 266 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failed save imposes fear; dial: duration is 1 minute with an end-of-turn save; the threat causes fear that can be overcome.

rules.statement: A character cannot spend Hit Dice after a short rest until someone uses one charge of a healer’s kit to treat the character’s wounds.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Healer’s Kit Dependency, p. 266 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require treatment before short-rest Hit Dice use; dial: one kit use per character treated; supplies constrain recovery.

rules.statement: As an action, a character can spend up to half their Hit Dice to regain hit points, rolling each die and adding Constitution; they may choose to spend another die after each roll. After using this healing option, they cannot use it again until a short or long rest. A short rest restores Hit Dice equal to one quarter of the character’s level, minimum one, and a long rest restores all spent Hit Dice.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Healing Surges, pp. 266–267 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spend Hit Dice for immediate healing; dial: cap use at half the pool and once per rest interval; recovery consumes limited reserves.

rules.statement: Under slow natural healing, a long rest does not restore hit points automatically; instead, characters spend Hit Dice to heal at the rest’s end as they do after a short rest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Slow Natural Healing, p. 267 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: remove automatic long-rest healing; dial: require Hit Dice expenditure; wounds take longer to recover without magical healing.

rules.statement: The epic-heroism variant makes a short rest 5 minutes and a long rest 1 hour. A DM may limit spell-slot recovery after that long rest to half the maximum slots, rounded down, and to slots of 5th level or lower; only a full 8-hour rest restores all slots, including those of 6th level and higher.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Rest Variants: Epic Heroism, p. 267 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: shorten rests; dial: cap spell-slot recovery unless taking a full 8-hour rest; rapid recovery is balanced by reduced magical replenishment.

rules.statement: A plot-point user spends their starting point for one permitted effect, generally no more than once per session; after every player has spent one, each player gains 1 point. In one version the spender establishes a setting fact the group accepts; in another, the player to the spender’s right adds a complication; in a third, spending the point makes the player the DM and turns their character into an NPC.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Plot Points, pp. 269–270 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: plot points permit player-driven campaign changes; dial: choose an effect and usually cap use at one per session; shared authorship carries a complication or a change of game-running role.

rules.statement: When a character first takes damage from one source equal to at least half its hit-point maximum, it must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution save or suffer a system-shock result. The outcomes range from dropping to 0 hit points, sometimes stable, to temporary loss of reactions or other combat capability.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Massive Damage, p. 273 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a large single hit triggers a save; dial: threshold is half maximum hit points and DC 15; severe impact risks immediate bodily shock.

rules.statement: If an injury results in a festering wound, the character’s hit-point maximum falls by 1 every 24 hours it persists; reaching 0 means death. Magical healing cures it, or a caregiver can attempt a DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine) check every 24 hours, with 10 successes curing the wound.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Injuries, p. 272 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: untreated wound worsens over time; dial: one maximum hit point per day and 10 successful treatment checks; delay makes the injury increasingly dangerous.

rules.statement: When estimating a monster’s effective hit points for challenge rating, multiply actual hit points for resistances by 2 at expected challenge ratings 1–4, 1.5 at 5–10, 1.25 at 11–16, and 1 at 17 or higher. For immunities, use multipliers of 2, 2, 1.5, and 1.25 for those same rating bands; the actual hit points do not change.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 277, Step 9: Damage Vulnerabilities, Resistances, and Immunities (dnd5e-dmg-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: damage defenses affect the threat estimate, not actual hit points; dial: the multiplier by rating and defense type; reason: defenses matter differently across the threat scale.

rules.statement: Estimate a monster’s damage output by adding the average damage of its most effective attacks in a round, including relevant off-turn effects. If output varies by round, average the first three rounds; for example, 90, 37, and 37 damage averages to 54 per round, rounded down.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Pages 278–279, Step 11: Damage; Overall Damage Output (dnd5e-dmg-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the most effective routine and include off-turn damage; dial: account for variation over three rounds; reason: burst effects and repeatable attacks contribute differently over time.

rules.statement: A weapon sized for a Large attacker deals double its normal weapon dice, one sized for a Huge attacker deals triple, and one sized for a Gargantuan attacker deals quadruple. A creature has disadvantage when attacking with a weapon sized for a larger attacker, and a weapon two or more sizes larger may be unusable.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 278, Step 11: Damage (dnd5e-dmg-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: oversized weapons increase damage dice; dial: impose disadvantage or forbid use for a sufficiently large mismatch; reason: size determines whether the weapon can be wielded effectively.

rules.statement: A monster’s save DC can be set to 8 plus its proficiency bonus plus the modifier of the ability relevant to the effect. For damage spells, use the spell-level damage table as a guide; if a successful save deals no damage rather than half damage, increase the listed damage by 25 percent.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Pages 278–279, Steps 12–13; page 283, Spell Damage (dnd5e-dmg-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the ability most relevant to the effect and the table’s half-damage assumption; dial: raise damage by 25 percent when saves prevent all damage; reason: stronger outcomes need to be balanced against the spell’s level.

rules.statement: For a monster with three or four saving-throw bonuses, raise effective AC by 2 when estimating challenge rating; with five or more, raise it by 4. These adjustments do not change actual AC.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 279, Step 15: Saving Throw Bonuses (dnd5e-dmg-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: treat multiple strong defenses as a challenge-rating advantage; dial: increase effective AC according to the number of save bonuses; reason: broad resistance makes the monster harder to overcome.

rules.statement: A magic item’s rarity guides the strength and frequency of its effects: the table sets maximum spell levels and static bonuses, and a spell effect can be limited to once per day or made consumable. If sharing an item’s lasting benefit would disrupt play, or if its bonus could stack with similar items, require attunement.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 285, Power Level; Attunement (dnd5e-dmg-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: constrain item power by rarity and require attunement when unrestricted sharing or stacking would be disruptive; dial: choose effect strength, frequency, and whether attunement is needed; reason: powerful persistent benefits need access limits.

rules.statement: A new playable elf subrace can grant the ability to cast misty step once, with that use returning after a short or long rest; the example balances this 2nd-level spell effect by giving the subrace no additional traits beyond its stated ability increase and weapon training.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Page 286, Example Subrace: Eladrin (dnd5e-dmg-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one use per rest; dial: pair a limited-use effect with the other traits granted; reason: a planar step is potent enough to consume much of the subrace’s power budget.

rules.statement: A character with celestial ancestry resists both radiant and necrotic damage. This reduces the impact of those damage types without requiring an action or resource.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Aasimar, p. 287, Celestial Resistance (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: always active; dial: remove one resistance; the heritage protects the character from particular harms.

rules.statement: The character can cast light at will, then gains one use of lesser restoration at 3rd level and one use of daylight at 5th level; each limited spell use returns after a long rest. Charisma is the casting ability for these spells.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Aasimar, p. 287, Celestial Legacy (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ancestry grants a small spell suite; dial: adjust spells or recharge interval; the limited abilities express inherited magic.

rules.statement: A spellcaster can spend points to create a spell slot and then cast a spell with that slot; cantrips cost no points, and spent points return after a long rest. Slot costs for spell levels 1–9 are respectively 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, and 13 points.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Variant: Spell Points, pp. 288–289 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: points replace spell slots; dial: alter pool or slot costs; greater casting flexibility is balanced by a finite daily reserve.

rules.statement: A caster cannot spend below 0 points, and cannot create a slot above the maximum level allowed by their caster level, even if they have enough points. For slots of 6th level or higher, they can create only one slot of each level per long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Variant: Spell Points, pp. 288–289 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain both level and daily high-slot limits; dial: change the ceiling; powerful spells are constrained by training and strain.

rules.statement: The spell-point pool depends on caster level: the table gives 4 points and a 1st-level maximum at level 1, rising to 133 points and a 9th-level maximum at level 20. Paladin and ranger levels count as half their class level, while Eldritch Knight fighter and Arcane Trickster rogue levels count as one-third, when consulting the table.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Variant: Spell Points, p. 289, Spell Points by Level (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated level progression and fractions; dial: revise progression; access to spell capacity follows accumulated training.

rules.statement: A new background can grant entry to a particular place and access to its resources without payment, while people connected to that place may treat the character as an ally and seek their help. The feature should open opportunities for interaction or exploration rather than automatically grant a check bonus or success.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Creating a Background, p. 289 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: grant setting access, not automatic success; dial: narrow the access or require a cost; affiliation earns privileges but carries social ties.

rules.statement: When replacing a class feature, compare what it contributes to combat, exploration, and social interaction, whether it affects how long the party can adventure, and what resources or recovery schedule it uses. A replacement that shifts an exploration benefit into combat can make the class disproportionately strong in combat.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Substituting Class Features, p. 288 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve roughly equivalent contribution; dial: shift the feature’s domain or recovery; a new benefit should not eclipse other classes.

rules.statement: A class’s spell list can be changed to fit its setting, but spellcasters that regain slots on a short rest may use some spells more times per day than other casters. Changes to such a list therefore need particular caution.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Changing Spell Lists, p. 287 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: account for recovery frequency; dial: restrict or revise the list; short-rest recovery increases daily access to certain spells.

rules.statement: A class option can be added without removing existing class features, but should be compared with options of similar level for relative power and distinctiveness, then tested and revised in play.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Creating New Class Options, p. 288 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: match comparable options; dial: revise after testing; a new option must remain distinctive without outclassing alternatives.

rules.statement: A touched object can cause the first person to touch it to age, animate itself or nearby objects, or undergo a change such as a shift in size, appearance, or material. These are listed as possible effects rather than as a single effect with a shared procedure.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Dungeon Dressing — Tricks, p. 298 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: include as an optional dungeon effect; dial: choose which change occurs, since the table gives alternatives but no duration or reversal rule.

rules.statement: A trick may ask three skill-testing questions; if all three are answered correctly, a reward appears.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Dungeon Dressing — Tricks, p. 298 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require all three correct answers; dial: set the questions and reward, which determine the challenge and payoff.

rules.statement: A trick may give a character resistance or vulnerability, or change a character’s alignment, personality, size, appearance, or sex when touched.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Dungeon Dressing — Tricks, p. 298 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the listed change as a touch-triggered effect; dial: decide its duration and how it can be reversed, since neither is specified.

rules.statement: A trick may create a force field or illusion, suppress magic items for a time, or prevent movement; the passage gives no duration or area for these effects beyond specifying that a confusion effect targets all creatures within 10 feet.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Dungeon Dressing — Tricks, p. 298 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the effects as bounded dungeon tricks; dial: set duration and affected area where unstated, because the passage supplies no general limits.

rules.statement: A trick may cast polymorph on characters for 1 hour, cast suggestion on them, or cast geas on them; another listed trick causes confusion among all creatures within 10 feet.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Dungeon Dressing — Tricks, p. 298 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the named effects as written; dial: determine which characters are affected except where the 10-foot confusion area is specified.

rules.statement: A trick may teleport characters to another place, or swap the minds of two or more characters.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Dungeon Dressing — Tricks, p. 298 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow the listed trick to relocate or exchange minds; dial: choose the destination or participants, since these details are left open.

rules.statement: A trick may lock or unlock exits, release or summon a monster, or create an imprisoned creature; the passage provides no release condition for the imprisoned creature.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Dungeon Dressing — Tricks, p. 298 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: treat these as distinct possible trick outcomes; dial: specify the creature and any release condition, which the passage does not establish.

rules.statement: A trick may offer a game of chance with a promised reward or valuable information, give directions that may be true or false, or grant a wish.
locators: D&D 5e Dungeon Master's Guide 2014: Dungeon Dressing — Tricks, p. 298 (dnd5e-dmg-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: present these as optional outcomes; dial: define the wager, truthfulness, or limits of a wish, since none are prescribed.

rules.statement: While the dragon is alive, a creature speaking within 1 mile of its lair can be heard by the dragon as though the dragon were within 10 feet of the speaker; this gives the dragon knowledge of everything said there.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 67, Regional Effects (dnd5e-fizban#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: local lair effect; dial: 1 mile range and 10-foot listening distance; reason: the dragon’s magical connection to its territory.

rules.statement: A dragon may use one of the passage’s general lair actions to roll a d6 and recharge its breath weapon on a 6, regain hit points equal to the number rolled, or gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage until its next turn.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 67, Additional Lair Actions (dnd5e-fizban#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a lair-bound option; dial: recharge only on 6 and resistance lasts until the next turn; reason: the lair’s magic briefly bolsters its dragon.

rules.statement: A hoard worth about 15,000 gp or more binds a dragon, its lair, and its territory together, empowering the dragon’s legendary actions and extending its regional influence. Dragons commonly establish another lair when their hoard reaches another multiple of 15,000 gp.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 69, Hoards and Lairs (dnd5e-fizban#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: treasure sustains the bond; dial: roughly 15,000 gp per threshold; reason: accumulated wealth anchors the dragon’s power to its places.

rules.statement: A dragon can link portions of a divided hoard with one or more special items, maintaining its ownership claim and making scattered caches function as one hoard.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 69, Hoard Linking Items (dnd5e-fizban#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: linked items preserve the hoard connection; dial: one or more linking pieces; reason: the dragon’s magic unifies wealth distributed among caches.

rules.statement: If a lair contains less than 10,000 gp in treasure, it ceases to count as a lair: the dragon cannot use lair actions there, and the surrounding regional effects end as if the dragon had died.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 70, Plundering a Hoard (dnd5e-fizban#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the lair loses its status below the threshold; dial: 10,000 gp; reason: removing the treasure breaks the dragon’s magical attachment to the site.

rules.statement: A dragon’s hoard can carry a curse affecting creatures who take from it; possible effects include automatic failure of saving throws against the dragon’s Frightful Presence, reduced speed, healing during rests, or a soul remaining on the hoard after death until the victim finishes a long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 70, Hoard Curses (dnd5e-fizban#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a curse attaches consequences to affected creatures; dial: effects vary and one soul effect lasts until a long rest; reason: a dying dragon’s oath or a living dragon’s inscription lays a magical claim on plunderers.

rules.statement: A dragon turtle’s lair causes the temperature within 6 miles to rise to 100°F; the passage also describes portals to the Elemental Plane of Water that allow creatures from that plane to dwell nearby.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Page 115, Dragon Turtle Regional Effects (dnd5e-fizban#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: regional effects operate around the lair; dial: 6-mile radius and 100°F; reason: the dragon turtle’s lair alters its surroundings and opens access to its associated plane.

rules.statement: A chromatic dragonborn can replace one attack with a 30-foot, 5-foot-wide breath line; creatures in it make a Dexterity save (DC 8 + Constitution modifier + proficiency bonus), taking 1d10 of the ancestry’s damage type on a failure or half on a success. Damage becomes 2d10 at level 5, 3d10 at 11, and 4d10 at 17; uses equal proficiency bonus and return after a long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 1, Chromatic Dragonborn Traits (pp. 12–13) (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ancestry fixes the damage type; dial: proficiency-bonus uses and long-rest recovery limit repeated blasts.

rules.statement: From level 5, a chromatic dragonborn can use an action to become immune for 1 minute to the damage type tied to their ancestry; this can be done once per long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 1, Chromatic Dragonborn Traits (p. 12) (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: immunity protects only against the inherited type; dial: one-minute duration and long-rest lock keep it occasional.

rules.statement: A gem dragonborn can send telepathic messages to a creature they can see within 30 feet; the recipient need not share a language, but must understand at least one language.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 1, Gem Dragonborn Traits (p. 13) (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: communication is one-way messaging; dial: sight, 30-foot range, and the recipient’s language comprehension limit it.

rules.statement: From level 5, a gem dragonborn can use a bonus action to manifest wings for 1 minute, gaining a flying speed equal to walking speed and the ability to hover; the trait recharges after a long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 1, Gem Dragonborn Traits (p. 13) (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: wings grant flight and hovering; dial: one-minute duration and once-per-long-rest use constrain access.

rules.statement: At level 5, a metallic dragonborn gains a second breath option: in place of an attack, exhale into a 15-foot cone. Creatures make a Constitution save or become incapacitated until the start of the dragonborn’s next turn, or make a Strength save or be pushed 20 feet and knocked prone; the feature recharges after a long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 1, Metallic Dragonborn Traits (p. 14) (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: choose incapacitation or forced movement for the cone; dial: short effect duration and long-rest recovery limit use.

rules.statement: A monk following the Way of the Ascendant Dragon can replace one attack with a 20-foot cone or 30-foot, 5-foot-wide line of chosen acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison energy. Targets make Dexterity saves against the monk’s ki DC, taking two Martial Arts die rolls on a failure or half on a success; uses equal proficiency bonus and return on a long rest, or another use costs 2 ki points. At level 11 the damage becomes three die rolls.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 1, Breath of the Dragon (p. 15) (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: user chooses shape and damage type; dial: proficiency-bonus uses, long-rest recovery, or 2 ki per extra use limit output.

rules.statement: At level 11, the monk can create a 10-foot aura for 1 minute, choosing either to frighten a creature selected when the aura starts or on later bonus actions (the target can save at each turn’s end), or to grant the monk and allies in the aura resistance to one listed damage type. Reuse costs 3 ki points or otherwise requires a long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 1, Aspect of the Wyrm (p. 16) (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the aura supplies one selected benefit; dial: one-minute duration and long-rest reuse, unless 3 ki are spent.

rules.statement: A drakewarden can use an action to summon its bound drake into an unoccupied space within 30 feet. It follows commands, acts immediately after its ranger, and normally Dodges unless the ranger spends a bonus action to direct another action; it vanishes at 0 hit points, when summoned again, or when the ranger dies. After summoning, another summon requires a long rest or a spell slot of level 1 or higher.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 1, Drake Companion (pp. 17–18) (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the drake is a commanded companion; dial: bonus-action direction and limited summoning require attention and recovery or a spell slot.

rules.statement: A draconic spirit summoned with a 5th-level spell appears in a visible unoccupied space within 60 feet and remains for concentration, up to 1 hour, unless reduced to 0 hit points. The caster chooses its dragon family and one of its resistances; the caster gains resistance to that damage type for the spell’s duration. The spirit acts after the caster, obeys verbal commands, and otherwise Dodges and avoids danger.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 2, Summon Draconic Spirit (pp. 23–24) (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the spirit assists and shares one chosen resistance with its caster; dial: concentration, up to one hour, and a spell slot govern its presence.

rules.statement: A chromatic-dragon gift lets the user touch a weapon as a bonus action to add 1d4 acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison damage on each hit for 1 minute; it recharges after a long rest. The gift also lets the user use a reaction when taking one of those damage types to gain resistance to that instance, a number of times equal to proficiency bonus per long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 1, Gift of the Chromatic Dragon (p. 19) (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the infusion attaches briefly to a touched weapon; dial: one-minute duration, long-rest recharge, and proficiency-bonus reaction uses cap it.

rules.statement: A metallic-dragon gift lets its user learn cure wounds and cast it once without a spell slot per long rest, or with available spell slots. It also lets the user use a reaction when they or a visible creature within 5 feet is hit by an attack to grant an AC bonus that can make the attack miss; uses equal proficiency bonus and return after a long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chapter 1, Gift of the Metallic Dragon (p. 19) (dnd5e-fizban#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: healing and brief attack protection are separate benefits; dial: one free spell cast and proficiency-bonus defensive reactions recharge only on a long rest.

rules.statement: A dragon's influence around its lair can cause half-dragons to arise among nearby creatures; when the dragon dies, its regional effects usually stop at once, though some effects last 1d10 days and others cause an immediate change.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Half-Dragon Origin; Regional Reversal (pp. 39–40) (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: local influence and its reversal; dial: which effects persist and for how long; the dragon's death removes its sustaining presence.

rules.statement: Half-dragon transformation can result from eating magically produced fruit, bathing in or drinking dragon blood, receiving a gift of power as a newborn or unborn child, or having dragon power leach from a hoard into a thief.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Half-Dragon Origin (p. 39) (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation is a possible consequence of specific exposure or bestowal; dial: whether it occurs and which route causes it; the source is draconic influence.

rules.statement: When a dragon dies, its body can trigger one of six death-throe outcomes: a lair action centered on the body, a final breath attack, transformation or dissipation of the body, a wild-magic surge, a life-energy burst that grants creatures within 120 feet the benefit of a long rest, or transport through a portal to an echo's lair that strengthens the echo.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Death of a Dragon; Dragon Death Throes (p. 40) (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: death releases a source-shaped magical consequence; dial: select or roll among six outcomes and reduce danger if needed; the dragon's death is the trigger.

rules.statement: Power in a dragon's lair can persist after death: fouled water and nightmares last 1d10 days, while other listed changes can be immediate, including an earthquake, altered wildlife, changed weather, or vegetation blackening and dying within 1 mile.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Reversal (p. 40) (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: lingering effects reflect the dead dragon's former influence; dial: choose which effects occur and whether they are immediate or last 1d10 days; the lair bears the aftermath.

rules.statement: A dying dragon can pass its power to another creature through breath, a gemstone implanted in the recipient, contact or treasure, or exposure to its remains; claiming power from the corpse can seriously injure the claimant. Transfer can instead happen automatically to participants or witnesses within 300 feet, or to every creature that ever damaged the dragon.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Passing the Mantle (pp. 40–41) (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a dragon's power can be claimed or bestowed at death; dial: choose the recipient, channel, and whether transfer is automatic; corpse energies can make the claim dangerous.

rules.statement: When a dragon becomes undead, its echoes on other worlds can suffer a spreading wasting affliction that increases cruelty and violence and accelerates physical aging; the condition can drive an affected dragon toward undeath.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Undeath (p. 42) (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: undeath's consequences spread to related echoes; dial: how broadly and quickly the wasting develops; the cost is escalating deterioration and behavior change.

rules.statement: A dragon's echo on another Material Plane world may differ in appearance, age, kind, personality, ideals, or alignment, and can even be undead or a shadow dragon; the table uses a d8 to determine how similar or different the echo is.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Echoes Across the Worlds; Dragon Echo Characteristics (p. 42) (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each dragon has an echo on each Material Plane world; dial: use the d8 outcomes to set similarity; echoes remain connected across worlds.

rules.statement: Most metallic and gem dragons gain the ability to change into Humanoid or Beast form by adulthood or ancient age, and can use the change to gather information or live among other creatures; remaining in an assumed form for too long is feared by some dragons to risk being trapped, though that fear is described as superstition.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Shape-Shifting (p. 44) (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: eligible dragons can assume other forms; dial: access by dragon age and whether the form is used for concealment; the feared loss of return is superstition, not a stated rule.

rules.statement: A dragon's death can pass power into an egg, creating a new generation with that power; some dragons instead invest power in a creature near death or allow those who slay them to seize it.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Passing the Mantle (p. 40) (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the dragon's power can continue through a successor or be claimed; dial: choose inherited, bestowed, or seized transfer; the transfer follows the dragon's death.

rules.statement: Hidecarved dragons receive one protective ward plus one additional ward for each age category above wyrmling; options include immunity to form-altering effects, immunity to emotion-sensing and thought-reading, improved defense against magic or damage, or the ability to cast death ward on themselves again after a long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Hidecarved Dragons; Engraved Wards (p. 47) (dnd5e-fizban#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: magical scale sigils grant wards according to age; dial: choose or roll ward effects; the protections are tied to carved markings.

rules.statement: A minion may be given one or more master-linked traits: it can resist commands that contradict its master's instructions, or communicate telepathically with the master while both are on the same plane.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragons’ Minions (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use one or more traits; dial: choose which bonds apply. In-world, the dragon’s magic reaches its servants.

rules.statement: When a minion dies, an explosive version deals 1d8 damage of the same type as its master’s breath weapon to creatures within 5 feet; a sacrificial version instead restores the master’s hit points by an amount equal to four times the minion’s challenge rating, if the master is within 60 feet.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragons’ Minions (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: choose either death-triggered outcome; dial: add or omit the trait. The minion’s death converts its life or stored draconic energy into an effect.

rules.statement: When an attack hits its master, a bodyguard minion within 5 feet can use its reaction to make that attack hit itself instead.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragons’ Minions (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: available within 5 feet and costs the minion’s reaction; dial: grant or omit the trait. The servant risks itself to protect its master.

rules.statement: A dragon’s lair can cause regional changes to terrain, weather, water, nearby creatures, planar connections, or perception; examples include changes within 6 or 12 miles, and some effects fade over 1d10 days after the dragon dies or leaves.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: select fitting regional effects; dial: choose their kind and reach. The lair’s accumulated magic alters its surroundings.

rules.statement: Water within 1 mile of a lair may charm a drinker who fails a Wisdom save against DC 8 plus the dragon’s proficiency bonus and Charisma modifier; the charm lasts 24 hours, while a successful save prevents this effect for 24 hours.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects: Water Changes (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the specified save, range, and duration apply; dial: include or omit this water effect. The dragon’s presence imbues nearby water with an enchanting influence.

rules.statement: A lair effect can let a dragon know when any creature within 1 mile dies and review that creature’s final moments through its eyes; another can make the dragon hear everything said within 10 feet of a spot where its name is spoken within 1 mile, for 5 minutes.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects: Dragon Magic (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use either listed sensing effect with its stated range and duration; dial: select which, if any, is present. The lair’s magic carries information to its dragon.

rules.statement: At initiative count 20, a dragon in its lair can recharge its breath weapon on a roll of 6 on a d6, regain hit points equal to the number of Hit Dice it has, or gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage until initiative count 20 next round.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Lair Actions (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each listed option has its stated trigger or duration; dial: choose which actions the dragon has. The lair’s magic replenishes or reinforces its occupant.

rules.statement: An adult dragon can divide its hoard among multiple caches; each cache anchors its power at that location, extending the reach of its lair influence, while an ancient dragon may have eight to ten caches worth 200,000 gp each.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragon Hoards: Adult Dragons / Ancient Dragons (dnd5e-fizban#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: caches anchor power where stored; dial: set their number and distribution. The dragon spreads its magical reach by maintaining treasure in separate places.

rules.statement: A legendary dragon’s hoard worth about 15,000 gp or more links the dragon, its lair, and its territory through magic; this connection empowers legendary actions and spreads regional effects. As the hoard grows, the dragon may split it among multiple lairs, with new lairs generally established at each additional 15,000 gp.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Plundering a Hoard, p. 67 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the dragon’s wealth sustains its magical reach; dial: set the value threshold and number of caches to fit the campaign’s scale.

rules.statement: A dragon can link pieces from divided caches, preserving its ownership claim and treating scattered caches as one hoard. Collecting the linked pieces can reveal how many caches remain.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Plundering a Hoard, p. 67 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: linked objects maintain the dragon’s claim; dial: choose how many pieces make the set and how readily their connection can be deduced.

rules.statement: If a dragon’s lair holds less than 10,000 gp in treasure, it no longer counts as a lair: the dragon cannot use lair actions there, and its regional effects end as if it had died. Removing a hoard’s treasure can also weaken the dragon, while plundering a disturbed site alerts it and may draw it to defend what remains.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Plundering a Hoard, pp. 67–68 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: treasure loss cuts the magical link to the site; dial: choose how much theft is needed to cross the threshold, at the cost of alerting the dragon.

rules.statement: After a dragon dies, supernatural effects can remain in or around particularly valuable hoard objects. Hoard items may, for example, alter water or weather, attract animals, affect nearby sleepers’ dreams, shift wielders’ personalities, draw people toward the lair, or encourage plants to grow when coins are put in soil.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Hoard Quirks / Regional Effects, p. 68 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: an object carries an echo of its former owner; dial: select the effect, its reach, and whether it lasts after the hoard is moved.

rules.statement: A spirit may haunt an object from a hoard, appearing as a ghostlike creature or making the object behave like a sentient magic item. Resolving the spirit’s unfinished business is the surest way to end the haunting.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Haunted Hoards, p. 68 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: an unresolved purpose keeps the spirit tied to the object; dial: define the task that releases it and whether it manifests bodily.

rules.statement: A dragon’s death may curse treasure, affecting both thieves and others who touch it; the curse usually ends only when the whole hoard is gathered together again. A curse can impose exhaustion, vulnerability to the dragon’s breath damage, reduced speed, impaired recovery, or prevent resurrection; removing it with magic only suppresses it temporarily—one hour with remove curse or until the affected creature finishes a long rest with greater restoration.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: A Dragon’s Curse / Hoard Curse Effects, pp. 68–69 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the dead dragon’s curse attaches to contact with the hoard; dial: choose the penalty and its duration, with complete reunification as the costly solution.

rules.statement: A curse may be ended by returning the complete hoard to the dragon’s lair, but taking even one coin away restarts it. A specific rite can also end it, and treasure freely given to another dragon can become part of that dragon’s hoard and nullify the previous owner’s curse.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Breaking a Hoard Curse, p. 71 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the curse follows the original owner’s claim; dial: require full recovery, a rite, or a costly transfer of ownership.

rules.statement: A dragon lair can warp space so that traveling upward through a chimney returns a creature to a lower level, while traveling downward from below returns it above. Anything dropped down can fall endlessly unless it or an outside force can stop it; this spatial effect fades 1d10 days after the dragon dies.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Amethyst Dragon Lairs, p. 79 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the lair’s magic bends local space; dial: set the affected passages and duration, with the dragon’s death ending the effect after 1d10 days.

rules.statement: A black dragon’s lair may let it use additional actions: it can erupt a 20-foot-high, 10-foot-radius column of filth within 120 feet, causing 3d6 poison damage and difficult terrain; restrain up to three creatures with muck until the next round; or poison creatures in a gas sphere for up to 1 minute, with a DC 15 Constitution save at each turn’s end to recover.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Black Dragon Lairs, Additional Lair Actions, p. 82 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: lair actions turn the dragon’s environment into a hazard; dial: choose which hazards are available and their areas, duration, and saving difficulty.

rules.statement: A black dragon’s regional influence can cause listless despair in creatures that spend a year within 10 miles, while birds, insects, and reptiles may follow humanoids within 6 miles; the dragon can suppress the spying-creature effect at will. Stinging insects and the smell of rot may also characterize the area within 6 miles.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Black Dragon Lairs, Regional Effects, p. 82 (dnd5e-fizban#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the dragon’s presence changes the surrounding region; dial: choose effects and radius, with prolonged exposure or the loss of concealment as the cost.

rules.statement: A creature with Intelligence 3 or higher coming within 30 feet of one of the lair’s four wells alerts the dragon to its presence.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Brass Dragon Lair Features — Wells, p. 93 (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the four wells provide a fixed, short-range warning network; dial by changing their number or detection radius.

rules.statement: An adult or ancient brass dragon in its lair can animate up to three visible statues; each attacks one creature within 5 feet with a +7 attack bonus, dealing 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage on a hit.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Brass Dragon Lair — Additional Lair Actions, p. 93 (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the brief animation is limited to three statues and one nearby target per statue; the dragon spends a lair action to use it.

rules.statement: An adult or ancient brass dragon can send a 40-foot-wide, 100-foot-long wind through its lair. Creatures other than the dragon in the area must make a DC 15 Strength save or be pushed 15 feet and knocked prone; the wind deals 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage, disperses gases and vapors, and may extinguish unprotected flames, while protected flames have a 50 percent chance of going out.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Brass Dragon Lair — Additional Lair Actions, p. 93 (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one directional lair-scale gust has a save, bounded area, and distinct interactions with creatures and flames.

rules.statement: An adult or ancient brass dragon can fill the air within 120 feet with dust and sand, making that area lightly obscured until initiative count 20 on the next round.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Brass Dragon Lair — Additional Lair Actions, p. 93 (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the obscuring effect covers a set radius and expires at a stated initiative count.

rules.statement: Within 6 miles of the lair, a small cloud follows non-evil creatures, stays between them and direct sunlight, and grants advantage on saves against extreme heat.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Brass Dragon Lair — Regional Effects, p. 93 (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the protective benefit is limited by alignment, distance, and the specific heat hazard.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of the lair, creatures become unusually pleased to hear themselves speak, and the air fills with loud birdsong and extensive conversation among sapient creatures.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Brass Dragon Lair — Regional Effects, p. 93 (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the localized effect nudges social behavior and ambient sound without specifying compulsion or duration.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of a blue dragon’s lair, blue objects become fascinating to creatures who have spent a year in the area, and they feel compelled to acquire them whenever possible.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Blue Dragon Lair — Regional Effects, p. 88 (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the compulsion requires a year of exposure and applies only to blue objects in the lair’s vicinity.

rules.statement: The terrain immediately around a blue dragon’s lair appears to be a lush oasis. A creature examining the illusion can attempt a DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check; a creature that disbelieves it sees the real terrain beneath a vague overlay.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Blue Dragon Lair — Regional Effects, p. 88 (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the illusion is geographically bounded and can be recognized with a specified check.

rules.statement: An adult or ancient blue dragon in its lair can make a 5-foot-radius, 20-foot-deep pit appear in ground it can see within 120 feet. A creature above it must make a DC 15 Dexterity save or fall, take 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage, and land prone; on a success, it moves to the nearest unoccupied space instead.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Blue Dragon Lair — Additional Lair Actions, p. 88 (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the sinkhole is restricted by sight, range, size, save, and a defined safe outcome.

rules.statement: An adult or ancient blue dragon in its lair can mislead intruders: until initiative count 20 on the next round, at each intersection or branching passage, a creature other than the dragon has a 50 percent chance of going in a different direction from its intended route.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Blue Dragon Lair — Additional Lair Actions, p. 88 (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the route confusion is limited to junctions, excludes the dragon, and lasts only until the stated initiative count.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of a blue dragon’s lair, the surrounding area constantly experiences a sandstorm.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Blue Dragon Lair — Regional Effects, p. 88 (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the storm is a persistent, geographically bounded regional condition.
