rules.statement: Within 30 feet of a bronze dragon’s magically warded sentinel statue, intruders can trigger an alert that informs the dragon of their presence.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Bronze Dragon Lair Features — Sentinel Statue, p. 96 (dnd5e-fizban#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a fixed magical lookout protects one hidden cove at a specified short range.

rules.statement: A concealed magical door can reshape its junction to open or close when the dragon commands it, or when stone shaping affects it. A creature with Intelligence 3 or higher that comes within 10 feet alerts the dragon to that creature’s presence and location; the door otherwise looks like solid stone, though it gives off transmutation magic.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Copper Dragon Lairs — Secret Doors (p. 102) (dnd5e-fizban#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the door hidden and the proximity alert active; dial: remove the alert or make the door detectable by ordinary inspection; in-world, the dragon relies on secret passages and awareness of intruders.

rules.statement: In its lair, a legendary copper dragon can choose a visible ground point within 120 feet and fill a 20-foot-radius sphere there with gas. Creatures in the sphere that fail a DC 15 Wisdom save laugh uncontrollably and are incapacitated until the end of their next turn.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Copper Dragon Lairs — Additional Lair Actions (p. 102) (dnd5e-fizban#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the gas as a brief crowd-control field; dial: alter the radius, save, or duration; the effect is confined to the dragon’s lair action and lasts only one turn.

rules.statement: In its lair, a legendary copper dragon can target a creature it can see within 120 feet. If the target fails a DC 15 Constitution save, its speed is halved and it cannot take reactions or bonus actions until the end of its next turn.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Copper Dragon Lairs — Additional Lair Actions (p. 102) (dnd5e-fizban#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply a short-lived impairment to one target; dial: change the save or duration; the lair action limits the effect to a visible creature and one turn.

rules.statement: Near a copper dragon’s lair, wind-carried ethereal music can be heard within 1 mile. Alternatively or additionally, hilltop standing stones within 1 mile shed dim light in a 10-foot radius at night; if the dragon dies, the stones remain but stop glowing.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Copper Dragon Lairs — Regional Effects (p. 102) (dnd5e-fizban#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the music and/or nighttime stone light as a regional sign; dial: omit either effect or change its range; the light is tied to the living dragon and ends at its death.

rules.statement: As a lair action, the dragon creates warm light in a 30-foot-radius sphere centered on itself. Each creature in the sphere must pass a DC 15 Wisdom save or be charmed until initiative count 20 in the next round.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Gold Dragon Lair — Additional Lair Action (dnd5e-fizban#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one short-lived, local charm; dial: the DC and radius; reason: the dragon’s light briefly beguiles nearby creatures.

rules.statement: Within 10 miles of the lair, small dragon-shaped runes appear to creatures in great need and mark a subtle route to the lair.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Gold Dragon Lair — Regional Effects (dnd5e-fizban#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a need-triggered route appears within 10 miles; dial: the definition of great need; reason: the trail guides the desperate toward the dragon.

rules.statement: A creature that has spent a year within 6 miles of the lair puts fairness and justice ahead of personal feelings.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Gold Dragon Lair — Regional Effects (dnd5e-fizban#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect follows a year of residence; dial: its strength and duration; reason: prolonged exposure changes residents’ priorities.

rules.statement: Within 6 miles of the lair, a creature deliberately trying to lie must pass a DC 15 Charisma save or accidentally disclose the truth it meant to hide. A creature that succeeds becomes immune to this effect for 24 hours.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Gold Dragon Lair — Regional Effects (dnd5e-fizban#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failed saves expose the intended truth, while success grants 24-hour immunity; dial: the radius and DC; reason: the lair’s influence frustrates deliberate deception.

rules.statement: The dragon animates up to three humanoid corpses as zombies. They act immediately after the dragon; when a zombie is destroyed or the dragon uses this action again, it becomes an inanimate corpse, and the effect lasts no more than 1 minute.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Green Dragon Lair — Additional Lair Actions (dnd5e-fizban#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: three corpses at most and a 1-minute limit; dial: the number animated; reason: the dragon temporarily puts nearby dead bodies to use.

rules.statement: One large lair root or branch attacks a creature within 10 feet, using a +7 attack bonus and dealing 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage on a hit. A Medium or smaller target must pass a DC 15 Strength save or fall prone.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Green Dragon Lair — Additional Lair Actions (dnd5e-fizban#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one nearby target can be struck and possibly knocked prone; dial: attack bonus, damage, and save DC; reason: the lair’s roots lash out at intruders.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of the lair, the dragon can make any Tiny beast act as its mouthpiece: the creature’s mouth and throat temporarily warp to resemble the dragon’s, allowing the dragon’s voice to emerge.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Green Dragon Lair — Regional Effects (dnd5e-fizban#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: Tiny beasts within 1 mile are eligible; dial: duration and frequency; reason: the dragon uses local wildlife to speak at a distance.

rules.statement: A dragon can fill a 20-foot-radius sphere it can see within 120 feet with thick smoke that spreads around corners and heavily obscures the area. A creature other than the dragon that enters it for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must pass a DC 15 Constitution save or be poisoned until the end of its next turn; the cloud ends at initiative count 20 on the next round.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Red Dragon Lair — Additional Lair Actions (dnd5e-fizban#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a brief cloud with a one-turn poison effect; dial: radius, save DC, and duration; reason: smoke fouls the air around the dragon.

rules.statement: A dragon can spread searing heat in a 15-foot-radius sphere it can see within 120 feet. A creature entering the area or starting its turn there makes a DC 15 Constitution save, taking 10 (3d6) fire damage on a failure or half on a success; the heat ends at initiative count 20 on the next round.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Red Dragon Lair — Additional Lair Actions (dnd5e-fizban#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: short-lived heat that damages creatures in the area; dial: sphere size, DC, and damage; reason: the dragon’s lair becomes dangerously hot.

rules.statement: Within 6 miles of the lair, precipitation is nearly absent and most plant life becomes withered and brown. Open flames within that range turn dark red, hiss and crackle, and shed embers and sparks.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Red Dragon Lair — Regional Effects (dnd5e-fizban#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dry, withered surroundings and visibly altered flames within 6 miles; dial: affected range and intensity; reason: the dragon’s presence leaves the region parched and ominous.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of the lair, the dragon can hear through any open flame.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Red Dragon Lair — Regional Effects (dnd5e-fizban#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: open flames within 1 mile provide sound; dial: range and whether other senses are included; reason: nearby fire carries sounds to the dragon.

rules.statement: A sapphire dragon in its lair can use a lair action to open or close passages through its walls, changing which parts of the lair are connected and accessible.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Sapphire Dragon Lair Features, p. 142 (dnd5e-fizban#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limited to the dragon’s lair and its lair action; dial: decide how many passages can change; the dragon controls its own routes through the stone.

rules.statement: A legendary adult or ancient shadow dragon in its lair can extinguish nonmagical lights in a 60-foot-radius sphere centered on itself and dispel spells that create light in that area.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Additional Lair Action: Banish Light, p. 146 (dnd5e-fizban#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: 60-foot radius and restricted to the lair action; dial: omit or adjust the optional action; the dragon’s presence suppresses illumination.

rules.statement: When a shadow dragon establishes a lair on the Material Plane, creatures within 1 mile with Intelligence 5 or higher feel forlorn and hopeless.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects, p. 146 (dnd5e-fizban#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a 1-mile regional effect with an Intelligence threshold; dial: choose whether it affects the region; the lair’s Shadowfell influence weighs on nearby minds.

rules.statement: Within 6 miles of a shadow dragon’s Material Plane lair, light is diminished so the land is lightly obscured by gloomy shadows.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects, p. 146 (dnd5e-fizban#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a 6-mile range and light obscuration; dial: choose whether this regional effect applies; the lair’s influence dims its surroundings.

rules.statement: Some deeply gloomy places within 1 mile of a shadow dragon’s lair form portals to the Shadowfell, allowing creatures from that plane to dwell nearby.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects, p. 146 (dnd5e-fizban#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: portals form only in some gloomy places within 1 mile; dial: decide which places qualify; Shadowfell influence opens routes for its creatures.

rules.statement: A legendary adult or ancient silver dragon in its lair can impose a supernatural chill on creatures it can see within 120 feet; each must make a DC 15 Constitution save or be restrained until initiative count 20 in the next round. Cold resistance grants advantage, while cold immunity guarantees success.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Additional Lair Action: Icy Grip, p. 150 (dnd5e-fizban#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: 120 feet, DC 15, and restraint ends at the next initiative count 20; dial: the optional action can be included at the table’s discretion; cold resistance or immunity mitigates it.

rules.statement: A legendary white dragon in its lair can use either or both of two additional lair effects: sleet fills a 20-foot-radius, 40-foot-high cylinder within 120 feet and can blind creatures there until the next round on a failed DC 15 Constitution save; or a strong wind fills a 30-foot-radius sphere around the dragon and lasts until it next uses a lair action or dies.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: White Dragon Lairs — Additional Lair Actions, p. 157 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the lair effects are available to adult or ancient white dragons while at home; dial: choose either or both; the weather-like hazards end on a short trigger or the dragon’s death.

rules.statement: Within 6 miles of a white dragon’s lair, extreme cold can impose disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity checks for creatures lacking cold resistance or immunity when the area is already extremely cold. Icy surfaces also hinder hiding, and at each passage junction non-dragons have a 50 percent chance of going in a direction other than the one intended.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Regional Effects, p. 159 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: these effects may occur around the lair; dial: use either or both; the dragon’s territory imposes environmental and navigational costs.

rules.statement: Once per day, a legendary amethyst dragon can use a no-component legend-lore effect, naming any person, place, or object within 1 mile of its lair as the subject. Water within 6 miles of the lair also lets it use a no-component clairvoyance effect as an action to target any body of water in that region.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Amethyst Dragon — Regional Effects, p. 162 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: these senses are available to a legendary amethyst dragon; dial: the first is once daily and the second is limited to regional water; the lair and nearby waters define their reach.

rules.statement: If an amethyst dragon dies, nearby aquatic life returns to normal abundance over 1d10 days, while existing amethyst deposits remain and new crystals form only at the ordinary rate.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Amethyst Dragon — Regional Effects, p. 162 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ecological benefit ends gradually after the dragon’s death; dial: recovery takes 1d10 days, while already-formed crystals persist.

rules.statement: An ancient amethyst dragon can create a duplicate presence in a space it can fit within its lair, occupying both spaces until the next round. When moving or acting it chooses which presence to use; an effect that reaches both affects it only once.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Amethyst Dragon — Lair Actions, p. 162 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: this is a lair action; dial: it lasts only until the next round and does not multiply effects that hit both presences.

rules.statement: An amethyst dragon can magically teleport as a bonus action to an unoccupied space it can see within 60 feet. It can also change into any Medium or Small creature while retaining its statistics except size; the change ends at 0 hit points or when it uses a bonus action to end it.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ancient Amethyst Dragon — Bonus Actions, p. 162; Adult and Young Amethyst Dragon, p. 163 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: these are innate magical options; dial: teleportation requires a visible unoccupied destination within 60 feet, and the other form is limited by size and ends on incapacitating defeat or a chosen bonus action.

rules.statement: An ancient amethyst dragon’s gravitational breath fills a 90-foot cone; creatures there make a DC 23 Strength save, taking 14d8 force damage and having speed reduced to 0 until the start of the dragon’s next turn on a failure, or half damage without the speed reduction on a success. The breath recharges on a 5–6.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ancient Amethyst Dragon — Actions, p. 162 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the breath is an innate area attack; dial: a 90-foot cone, a save, and recharge on 5–6 limit its reach, effect, and frequency.

rules.statement: An animated breath is formed from a chromatic dragon’s breath energy, taking one of five energy types that determines its armor class, resistance, traits, and attack damage. It has 95 hit points, flies while hovering, and can make two slams; its type-specific effects include a fire aura, a poisoning aura for acid or poison forms, or a short-range teleport that damages nearby creatures for lightning form.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Animated Breath, p. 165 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dragons with sufficient practice can turn their own breath energy into a guardian; dial: one chosen matching energy type fixes the creature’s special properties.

rules.statement: The aspect of Bahamut’s healing breath restores 71 hit points to creatures he chooses within a 300-foot cone and revives chosen creatures there that have been dead no longer than 1 hour, restoring them with all hit points. His other breath option deals 12d10 radiant damage in the same-sized cone, with a DC 26 Dexterity save for half damage.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Aspect of Bahamut — Actions, p. 167 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the aspect chooses between restoration and damage; dial: both use a 300-foot cone, while revival is limited to the recently dead and the healing amount is fixed.

rules.statement: When the aspect of Bahamut would fall to 0 hit points, its hit points instead reset to 500, it recharges its breath and legendary resistance, and it gains access to mythic actions for 1 hour. Defeating it after this change awards an additional 155,000 XP.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Aspect of Bahamut — Platinum Brilliance, p. 167 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the first lethal blow triggers a second phase; dial: the reset is once per short or long rest and the empowered phase lasts 1 hour.

rules.statement: The aspect of Tiamat can target a creature it is grappling with a mythic effect: on a failed DC 25 Charisma save, the target takes 8d10 psychic damage and is banished to Avernus, then reappears in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of her at the start of her next turn.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Aspect of Tiamat — Mythic Actions, p. 168 (dnd5e-fizban#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: this is available only after the aspect’s second phase begins; dial: it costs two legendary actions, requires a grappled target, and the banishment lasts only until her next turn.

rules.statement: A greatwyrm can replace a failed saving throw with a success up to 4 times per day; a crystal or deep dragon can do so up to 3 times per day.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chromatic Greatwyrm; Ancient Crystal Dragon; Ancient Deep Dragon (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limited resistance; dial: change uses per day; reason: exceptional resilience is finite.

rules.statement: A greatwyrm’s awakening restores it to 425 hit points, refreshes its breath and all spent legendary resistance uses, and grants access to mythic actions for 1 hour; defeating it after activation awards an additional 105,000 XP.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Chromatic Awakening (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a single major recovery; dial: duration and restored resources; reason: the awakening is a temporary second phase.

rules.statement: A crystal dragon’s radiant breath recharges on a 5–6, damages creatures in a cone, and grants the dragon 5, 10, 15, or 25 temporary hit points by absorbing some of its energy, depending on age.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Crystal Dragon actions, pages 170–174 (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: recovery is tied to using the breath; dial: damage, cone size, and temporary hit points; reason: the dragon converts radiant force into protection.

rules.statement: A deep dragon’s spore breath recharges on a 5–6; creatures failing a Wisdom save take psychic damage and become frightened for 1 minute, with a new save at the end of each of their turns to end the fear.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Nightmare Breath, pages 173–177 (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: fear lasts up to 1 minute but is repeatedly resistible; dial: duration and save frequency; reason: spores impose terror that can be shaken off.

rules.statement: A dracohydra regrows two heads for each head lost since its last turn unless it took radiant damage since then, regaining 10 hit points per head restored; its heads each provide a bite and an extra opportunity-attack reaction.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dracohydra, page 178 (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: regrowth follows a turn-based check and radiant damage blocks it; dial: heads and healing per head; reason: its regenerative biology is vulnerable to radiant injury.

rules.statement: When a draconian dies, its remains trigger a kind-specific magical hazard: for example, a dreadnought explodes in a 10-foot radius for fire damage, while a foot soldier emits petrifying gas that can restrain and then petrify nearby creatures.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Draconian Death Throes, pages 179–180 (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the hazard occurs at 0 hit points; dial: area, damage, and condition; reason: corrupted draconic magic erupts as the body fails.

rules.statement: A draconian dreadnought that kills a Medium or smaller humanoid can transform into that creature, keeping its statistics except size; the disguise ends if the draconian dies or uses an action to end it.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Draconian Dreadnought, page 179 (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the form copies the slain target but not its statistics; dial: eligible targets and ending conditions; reason: the transformation exploits a victim’s likeness.

rules.statement: An infiltrator’s paired dagger hits can poison a target until the end of its next turn, and while poisoned this way the target is also paralyzed; its death-acid can be scraped or washed away, otherwise dealing damage at the start of each turn for 1 minute.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Draconian Infiltrator, page 180 (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: paired hits trigger a short paralysis and acid persists for at most 1 minute; dial: trigger and duration; reason: venom and bodily acid make close combat dangerous.

rules.statement: A draconian mastermind’s breath recharges on a 5–6 and can inflict poison damage plus one exhaustion level on a failed save; a successful save halves the damage, avoids exhaustion, and grants immunity to all draconian masterminds’ breath for 24 hours.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Draconian Mastermind, page 182 (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failed resistance causes lasting fatigue; dial: exhaustion severity and immunity window; reason: surviving the gas grants temporary acclimation.

rules.statement: A draconic shard is forced into a cracked gemstone if its spectral body or inhabited object is destroyed, and is only put to rest if that gemstone is also destroyed.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Draconic Shard, page 182 (dnd5e-fizban#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: destruction displaces rather than ends the spirit; dial: anchor durability and recovery; reason: its will persists through a gemstone vessel.

rules.statement: A shard can move its psychic essence into a visible nonsentient object no larger than Medium within 30 feet. The object takes the shard’s AC, and damage to it reduces the shard’s hit points; the shard can leave as an action, or is expelled if turned, reduced to 0 hit points, or affected by an effect that ends possession.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Inhabit Object, p. 181 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: possession lasts until an explicit exit or interruption; dial: the vessel must be visible, nonsentient, and Medium or smaller; cost: damage to it harms the shard.

rules.statement: While possessing an object, the shard can make it fly at its own flying speed, use its senses, speak, cast spells, and use legendary actions. If a creature wears or carries the object, the shard can grant it an extra 1d8 force damage on each attack hit and resistance to psychic damage.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Inhabit Object, p. 181 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: abilities are available while possession continues; dial: the damage bonus applies per hit and the resistance is limited to psychic damage; cost: the creature must wear or carry the possessed object.

rules.statement: When the shard reaches 0 hit points, it disappears and leaves a Tiny gemstone with AC 20 and 15 hit points, immune to all damage except force. If the gemstone remains intact, after 1d20 days it dissipates and the shard reforms there or in the nearest unoccupied space, restored to full hit points.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Rejuvenation, p. 181 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reformation follows destruction of the shard’s body; dial: it takes 1d20 days; cost: destroying the gemstone prevents the return.

rules.statement: The shard can target creatures of its choice in a 60-foot-radius sphere with a psychic pulse; each makes a DC 20 Intelligence save, taking 10d10 psychic damage and becoming stunned until the end of its next turn on a failure, or taking half damage without being stunned on a success.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Psychic Crush, p. 181 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the pulse affects chosen creatures in the sphere; dial: DC 20 and the 60-foot radius set its reach; cost: the stun lasts only until the target’s next turn ends.

rules.statement: A creature the shard can see within 30 feet must succeed on a DC 20 Wisdom save or be charmed until the end of its next turn. While charmed, it is the shard’s puppet, follows telepathic commands, and can take only the Attack action against a target chosen by the shard or Dash on its turn.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Commanding Thought, p. 181 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failed resistance grants brief control; dial: range is 30 feet and the effect lasts one turn; cost: the target’s available actions are sharply restricted.

rules.statement: The dragonbone golem’s pinions can each restrain one Medium or smaller creature hit by the pinion attack. A restrained creature can try to free itself at the start of its turn with a successful DC 17 Strength (Athletics) check, and the golem cannot attack with a pinion that is holding someone.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Dragonbone Golem, p. 183 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each of two pinions holds at most one target; dial: the target must be Medium or smaller and escape uses DC 17; cost: each occupied pinion is unavailable for attacks.

rules.statement: The dragonbone golem exhales petrifying gas in a 60-foot cone; each creature in it that fails a DC 15 Constitution save takes 10d6 poison damage and is restrained while beginning to turn to stone. The target repeats the save at the end of its next turn, ending the effect on a success and becoming petrified on a failure.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Petrifying Breath, p. 183 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect progresses from restraint to petrification after a failed follow-up save; dial: the cone is 60 feet and the save DC is 15; cost: a successful follow-up save ends the effect.

rules.statement: When the ancient dragon turtle would be reduced to 0 hit points, its hit points instead reset to 350, and for 1 hour it can use mythic actions. Defeating it after this change awards an additional 62,000 XP.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ancient Dragon Turtle, p. 191 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the first lethal reduction triggers a second phase; dial: it returns at 350 hit points and the phase lasts 1 hour; cost: the additional reward requires defeating it again.

rules.statement: When the egg hunter takes damage, it gives itself resistance to that damage.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Rapid Adaptation, p. 193 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resistance responds to damage received; dial: it applies to that damage type; cost: the passage specifies no duration or additional expenditure.

rules.statement: An emerald dragon can magically become a Small or Medium creature, retaining its game statistics except for its size. The change ends if it reaches 0 hit points or uses a bonus action to end it; it can also teleport to a visible unoccupied space within 60 feet as a bonus action.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Change Shape and Psychic Step, p. 195 (dnd5e-fizban#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the guise ends on incapacitating damage or the dragon’s choice; dial: only Small or Medium forms and visible destinations within 60 feet are allowed; cost: both abilities use a bonus action.

rules.statement: An adult emerald dragon can use a bonus action to take the form of a Medium or Small creature while keeping its statistics except for size; the change ends if it reaches 0 hit points or uses a bonus action to end it. A gem greatwyrm has the same transformation, but ends it with an action instead.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Adult Emerald Dragon; Gem Greatwyrm, Change Shape (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one-form-at-a-time disguise; dial: change the action cost or eligible sizes, with the cost of reduced access to a dragon's visible identity.

rules.statement: A gem dragon can teleport to an unoccupied space it can see within 60 feet; using this option as a legendary action costs 2 actions. The greatwyrm has the same 60-foot movement.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Adult Emerald Dragon; Gem Greatwyrm, Psychic Step (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: visible destination within 60 feet; dial: distance or destination restrictions, because unseen or occupied destinations are excluded.

rules.statement: A gem dragon's breath affects a cone whose size depends on its age: 15 feet for a wyrmling, 30 feet for a young dragon, and 60 feet for an adult. A creature that fails its Intelligence save takes psychic damage and, until the end of its next turn, subtracts a die roll from each attack roll and ability check; success halves damage and avoids the penalty.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Emerald Dragon, Disorienting Breath (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: cone, recharge on 5–6, and one-turn penalty; dial: area, penalty die, or duration, at the cost of less reliable disruption.

rules.statement: A dragon can burrow through solid rock at half its burrowing speed and leave a tunnel behind; the tunnel is 5 feet wide for a wyrmling, 10 feet for a young dragon, and 15 feet for an adult.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Emerald Dragon, Tunneler (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: half-speed travel through solid rock; dial: tunnel size or speed, because excavation leaves a permanent passage.

rules.statement: A greatwyrm that would reach 0 hit points instead resets to 400 hit points, restores its breath weapon and expended legendary resistances, and gains access to mass telekinesis for 1 hour. This awakening can happen again after a short or long rest.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Gem Greatwyrm, Gem Awakening (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one reset per short or long rest and a temporary new ability; dial: restored health or duration, because a defeated greatwyrm returns stronger.

rules.statement: During its awakening, a gem greatwyrm can target any number of visible creatures and objects within 120 feet, excluding worn or carried objects and objects over 4,000 pounds. A failed Strength save restrains a creature; at the end of its turn it may save again, and on the greatwyrm's turn each held target can be moved up to 60 feet while remaining within 120 feet, with restrained creatures also eligible for force damage.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Gem Greatwyrm, Mass Telekinesis (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: awakening-only, line of sight, weight limit, and repeated escape saves; dial: targets or movement, at the cost of controlling a crowd.

rules.statement: When a gem dragon kills an aberrant creature from the Far Realm, it can reshape the corpse into a gem stalker, imbuing it with life, sapience, and a purpose through the dragon's breath energy. The created guardian serves its creator.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Gem Stalker (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: requires a dead aberrant creature and ties the result to its creator; dial: eligible corpses or duration, because the servant's origin and mission constrain it.

rules.statement: A gem stalker can reduce damage to another visible creature within 30 feet by 10, then takes that same amount of damage itself.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Gem Stalker, Protective Link (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: fixed 10-point prevention with equal damage transferred to the guardian; dial: range or amount, because protection conserves the harm rather than erasing it.

rules.statement: A ghost dragon is bound to a single priceless object connected to its hoard. A hollow dragon that reaches 0 hit points separates into nine pieces; if all remain within 6 miles of the head, they reunite there after 1d6 days and restore the dragon to full hit points.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Ghost Dragon; Hollow Dragon, Reconstruction (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ghost depends on one focal object, while the hollow dragon requires all nine pieces nearby; dial: anchor or reunion conditions, because persistence depends on what remains intact.

rules.statement: A hoard scarab's magical dust can outline nearby creatures for 10 minutes; an outlined creature sheds dim light, cannot benefit from invisibility, and every dragon within 1 mile knows its location and can track it without error. Dispel magic ends the effect.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Hoard Scarabs, Scale Dust (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one-day use, 10-minute mark, and dragon-only tracking within 1 mile; dial: duration or sensing range, because the mark exposes the target to nearby dragons.

rules.statement: A metallic peacekeeper can release calming gas in a 30-foot-radius sphere; each creature that fails a Charisma save is charmed for 1 minute, incapacitated, and reduced to speed 0.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Metallic Peacekeeper, Calming Mist (dnd5e-fizban#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: short-lived area control with a saving throw; dial: radius or duration, because affected creatures lose both actions and movement.

rules.statement: The warbler resists any magic or other effect that would change its shape. Its master and the warbler can communicate mentally, and while they are on the same plane the warbler can also send its sensory information to the master.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Warbler stat block, Immutable Form and Telepathic Bond (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: block shape changes and allow a single companion link; the same-plane condition limits the link’s reach.

rules.statement: The warbler can release calming gas in a 5-foot-radius sphere around itself; affected creatures that fail a DC 11 Charisma save are charmed for 1 minute, incapacitated, and unable to move. It can use this again only when its recharge condition is met on a 5 or 6.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Warbler stat block, Calming Mist (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: brief, close-range crowd control; the small radius and recharge gate limit repeated use.

rules.statement: A moonstone dragon’s dream mist fills a 90-foot cone. A creature failing the listed Constitution save falls unconscious for 10 minutes, but damage or an action spent waking it ends the effect; the save DC varies by age, from 12 for a wyrmling to 21 for an ancient dragon.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Moonstone dragon stat blocks, Dream Breath (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: strong but interruptible sleep effect; damage, deliberate waking, and a recharge restriction provide counterplay.

rules.statement: A moonstone dragon can target a visible creature within 120 feet from its lair and send it to a harmless dream demiplane if it fails a DC 15 Charisma save. The target is stunned there until initiative count 20 of the next round, then returns to its former space or the nearest open space.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Moonstone dragon lair actions, Banish into Dream (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: temporary removal rather than lasting imprisonment; the short duration and safe destination constrain the effect.

rules.statement: Near an ancient moonstone dragon’s lair, dream communication can connect the dragon with a sleeping or trancing creature that understands a language; the creature remembers the conversation afterward. Portals within 6 miles link the Material Plane, Feywild, and Border Ethereal, and crossing takes 5 feet of movement; the portals close if the dragon dies.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Moonstone dragon regional effects (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: local, accessible cross-plane routes and dream contact; the portals depend on the dragon’s continued life.

rules.statement: A sapphire dragon can magically take the form of any Small or Medium creature while keeping its statistics except for size. It can end the change with a bonus action, and the change also ends if it reaches 0 hit points.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Sapphire dragon stat blocks, Change Shape (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reversible disguise with combat statistics retained; incapacitation by death or spending an action ends it.

rules.statement: A sapphire dragon can teleport to a visible unoccupied space within 60 feet. Its legendary-action option lets it use this step or cast one of its spells for 2 of its 3 legendary actions.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Sapphire dragon stat blocks, Psychic Step and Legendary Actions (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: short-range repositioning; using it as a legendary action consumes most of the dragon’s available off-turn actions.

rules.statement: A sapphire dragon’s lair can make natural stone within 6 miles a channel for its psionic presence, letting it use clairvoyance on a natural stone formation in that region as an action without components. Within 1 mile of the lair, creatures with telepathy have double their telepathy range.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Sapphire dragon regional effects (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: powerful sensing and communication enhancement tied to nearby natural stone and a defined lair radius.

rules.statement: A topaz dragon’s desiccating breath fills a cone whose size depends on age, from 30 feet for a young dragon to 90 feet for an ancient one. A creature failing the listed Constitution save takes necrotic damage and is weakened until the end of its next turn, giving it disadvantage on Strength checks and saves and halving damage from Strength-based weapon attacks; a successful save halves the damage and avoids weakening.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Topaz dragon stat blocks, Desiccating Breath (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a short-lived debilitation paired with damage; a successful save prevents the secondary effect and use is recharge-limited.

rules.statement: Near an ancient topaz dragon’s lair, creatures other than the dragon in the lair cannot regain hit points while a one-round negative-energy infusion is active. A creature finishing a long rest within 6 miles must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution save or be unable to reduce exhaustion or regain spent Hit Dice; resistance or immunity to necrotic damage prevents this regional effect.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Topaz dragon lair actions and regional effects (dnd5e-fizban#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: healing and recovery are suppressed only in a bounded region or briefly; necrotic resistance or immunity protects against the long-rest penalty.

rules.statement: The dragon can breathe in both air and water, with no stated duration limit.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Amphibious, p. 223 (dnd5e-fizban#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: both environments; dial: none stated; no extra cost or limit is given.

rules.statement: It senses without sight within 10 feet and sees in darkness out to 120 feet; its passive Perception is 15.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Senses, p. 223 (dnd5e-fizban#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the listed ranges and passive score; dial: none stated; these define its sensory reach.

rules.statement: It can communicate telepathically at up to 120 feet.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Languages, p. 223 (dnd5e-fizban#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: 120-foot range; dial: none stated; the communication is limited by distance.

rules.statement: Cold and necrotic damage are resisted, reducing damage of either type by half.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Damage Resistances, p. 223 (dnd5e-fizban#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resistance to the two listed damage types; dial: none stated; other damage types receive no listed protection.

rules.statement: A bite that hits one target within 5 feet deals 7 piercing damage plus 2 additional damage; the attack bonus is +4.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Bite, p. 223 (dnd5e-fizban#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one target at 5 feet; dial: none stated; the attack requires a hit.

rules.statement: The dragon can exhale necrotic energy in a 15-foot cone, but can use this breath again only when its recharge roll is 5 or 6. Each creature in the cone makes a DC 11 Constitution save; on a failure it takes 21 necrotic damage and is weakened until the end of its next turn, while a success deals half damage and avoids the weakening.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Desiccating Breath, p. 223 (dnd5e-fizban#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: 15-foot cone, DC 11, and the stated effects; dial: recharge on 5–6; limited reuse constrains its powerful area attack.

rules.statement: The dragon can cast bane once per day, without spell components, using Intelligence and a spell save DC of 12.
locators: Fizban's Treasury of Dragons: Spellcasting (Psionics), p. 223 (dnd5e-fizban#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one use per day and DC 12; dial: none stated; component-free casting is balanced by the daily limit.

rules.statement: A sticky filament can reach up to 60 feet and adheres to anything that touches it. A creature caught by it is grappled and has disadvantage on checks to escape; damaging the filament can end the grapple.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Cave Fisher, p. 74 (dnd5e-motm#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the filament binds on contact; dial: its 60-foot reach and vulnerability to damage limit the trap, fitting the creature’s hunting method.

rules.statement: A mechanical creature can have one randomly selected malfunction; the listed effects include faulty sensors that leave it blinded until its turn ends, or mistaking a nearby creature for its creator and refusing to harm it for 1 minute unless attacked or damaged.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Clockwork, p. 79 (dnd5e-motm#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a malfunction interferes with operation; dial: the specific fault and its duration determine how much control is lost.

rules.statement: A particular undead controller can have no more than 12 zombies under its control.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Death Lock, p. 88 (dnd5e-motm#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control is capped at 12; dial: the limit constrains the controller’s reach and reflects the burden of maintaining its force.

rules.statement: A subterranean warrior can turn invisible for up to 1 hour; the effect ends early if it attacks or casts a spell. The invisibility also covers equipment it wears or carries.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Duergar, pp. 108–111 (dnd5e-motm#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: concealment can last an hour; dial: attacking or spellcasting breaks it, trading offensive action for stealth.

rules.statement: A psychic master can change an object’s material type within a bounded area, with the difficulty set by size: DC 5 for Tiny, 10 for Small, 15 for Medium, and 20 for Large. It can also change the type of damage an effect deals, choosing from the listed energy types.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Githzerai, p. 143 (dnd5e-motm#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: material and damage types can be altered; dial: object size raises the difficulty, while the in-world limit is the master’s focused control.

rules.statement: A memory-draining creature can take memories from a target and use them to reproduce what that creature knows and feels. While drained, the target rolls a d4 and subtracts the result from ability checks and attack rolls; the drain lasts until the target is restored by a spell.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Adult Oblex, pp. 199–200 (dnd5e-motm#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: stolen memories can be copied and impose a d4 penalty; dial: the penalty persists until spell-based restoration, representing the victim’s depleted mind.

rules.statement: A necromantic leader can raise undead whose combined average hit points exceed 500, placing a total-capacity limit on the group summoned by that effect.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Orcus, p. 205 (dnd5e-motm#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the summoned group may exceed 500 combined average hit points; dial: that aggregate ceiling limits how much force can be raised at once.

rules.statement: A regenerating creature normally regains hit points, but when fire or acid prevents its regeneration it regains only 5 hit points at the start of its turn. If slain while that prevention applies, it remains unable to regenerate.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Troll, p. 247 (dnd5e-motm#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: regeneration restores health; dial: fire or acid reduces recovery to 5 and can leave regeneration disabled after death, reflecting its vulnerability.

rules.statement: A spore infection can transform a humanoid or beast into a servant after three failed saving throws; the victim dies and rises in that new state. The disease ends if cured or if the victim dies before completing the transformation.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Zuggtmoy, p. 283 (dnd5e-motm#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: infection can remake a victim after three failures; dial: the staged saves and possibility of cure or earlier death make the conversion contestable.

rules.statement: As an action, you can change your appearance and voice, including height, weight, and whether you appear Small or Medium. Your clothing and equipment stay the same, your game statistics do not change, and the form lasts until you change back or die.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Changeling Traits (p. 10) (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the disguise changes appearance, not abilities or carried gear; dial: broader impersonation could cost time or risk detection.

rules.statement: From 3rd level, you can use a bonus action to reveal one celestial aspect for 1 minute, ending it early as a bonus action; after using it, you must finish a long rest before using it again. The options grant flight and extra damage, frighten nearby non-allies while adding necrotic damage to one hit per turn, or radiate light and damage nearby creatures at the end of your turns while adding radiant damage to one hit per turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Aasimar Traits (p. 8) (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the revelation is limited to one minute and one use per long rest; dial: stronger or longer-lived celestial effects should carry a greater cost.

rules.statement: As an action, touch a creature and roll a number of d4s equal to your proficiency bonus; it regains hit points equal to the total. You can do this once per long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Aasimar Traits (p. 8) (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: healing is touch-range and once per long rest; dial: repeatable healing should consume a resource or impose another cost.

rules.statement: When you hit a creature with an attack roll before it has taken a turn in the current combat, the attack deals an extra 2d6 damage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Bugbear Traits (p. 9) (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bonus depends on acting before the target’s first turn; dial: extra damage outside that opening window should require another trigger or cost.

rules.statement: If you move at least 30 feet straight toward a target and hit it with a melee weapon attack on the same turn, you can use a bonus action to make one hoof attack against that target.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Centaur Traits (p. 10) (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the follow-up requires a 30-foot straight approach, a hit, and a bonus action; dial: remove any of those limits only if the added attack has another cost.

rules.statement: You can use a bonus action to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You can use this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses after a long rest; from 3rd level, the teleport also has an effect tied to your season.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Eladrin Traits (p. 14) (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: teleport is limited by sight, distance, and proficiency-bonus uses per long rest; dial: greater range or frequency should require a compensating cost.

rules.statement: When you finish a 4-hour trance, you can change your season and gain two weapon or tool proficiencies you lack; you keep them until your next long rest. You remain conscious during the trance, and magic cannot put you to sleep.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Eladrin Traits (p. 14) (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the borrowed proficiencies last only until the next long rest; dial: retaining them longer should require a lasting commitment or other cost.

rules.statement: Starting at 3rd level, you can cast disguise self once per long rest without a material component; starting at 5th level, you can also cast nondetection once per long rest without one. You can instead cast either spell using an appropriate spell slot.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Deep Gnome Traits (p. 12) (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each trait-based spell is limited to once per long rest; dial: repeated casting should consume spell slots or another resource.

rules.statement: Starting at 3rd level, you can cast enlarge/reduce on yourself once per long rest without a material component; starting at 5th level, you can also cast invisibility on yourself with the same limit. You can instead use an appropriate spell slot to cast either spell.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Duergar Traits (p. 13) (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: these spells affect only you and are each limited to once per long rest unless you spend a spell slot; dial: extending them to others or repeating them needs an added cost.

rules.statement: As a bonus action, you can become invisible until the start of your next turn, unless you attack, make a damage roll, or force someone to make a saving throw first. You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses after a long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Firbolg Traits (p. 16) (dnd5e-motm#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: invisibility lasts at most until your next turn and ends when you take specified hostile actions; dial: longer concealment should cost more uses or impose another limit.

rules.statement: A character can cast specified inherited spells without components, with access unlocking at the stated character levels; the spellcasting ability is chosen from Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. After casting an eligible spell through the trait, that spell cannot be cast through it again until a long rest, though appropriate spell slots can also power the listed spells.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Fire Genasi Traits; Water Genasi Traits; Githyanki Psionics; Githzerai Psionics; Triton Traits; Yuan-Ti Traits (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the specified spell list, level gates, and long-rest limit; dial: change the available spells or refresh interval to reflect how much inherited magic the world allows.

rules.statement: A githyanki finishing a long rest can choose one skill and one weapon or tool proficiency, gaining both until the end of the next long rest through a brief projection of consciousness into the Astral Plane. An elf finishing a four-hour conscious trance gains two weapon or tool proficiencies until the next long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Githyanki Traits, Astral Knowledge; Sea Elf Traits, Trance; Shadar-kai Traits, Trance (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: proficiencies expire at the next long rest; dial: vary their number or duration to make borrowed ancestral knowledge more or less potent.

rules.statement: Some inherited protections reduce incoming damage by resistance, while others grant advantage on saves against spells or on saves to avoid or end specified conditions. These defenses apply continuously, with no per-rest expenditure stated.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Fire Genasi Traits; Githzerai Traits; Goblin Traits; Satyr Traits; Yuan-Ti Traits (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep each protection limited to its named damage, spell, or condition; dial: broaden or narrow the protected categories to alter defensive strength.

rules.statement: A shifter can transform as a bonus action for up to 1 minute, until death, or until reverting as a bonus action, gaining temporary hit points equal to twice proficiency bonus and one chosen additional benefit. Uses equal proficiency bonus return after a long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Shifter Traits, Shifting (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the one-minute duration, chosen benefit, and rest-based uses; dial: alter duration or uses to represent greater or lesser control over the beast within.

rules.statement: A shadar-kai can teleport as a bonus action up to 30 feet to a visible unoccupied space, with uses equal to proficiency bonus restored by a long rest. From 3rd level, each such teleport also grants resistance to all damage until the start of the character's next turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Shadar-kai Traits, Blessing of the Raven Queen (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the 30-foot range, visible destination, uses, and brief resistance window; dial: adjust range or protection duration to change the risk of the escape.

rules.statement: A githzerai's innate mental defense gives advantage on saves to avoid or end charmed and frightened conditions on itself.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Githzerai Traits, Mental Discipline (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply only to those two conditions and only to the character; dial: expand the conditions covered if mental discipline is meant to be stronger.

rules.statement: A goblin that damages a larger creature with an attack or spell can add extra damage equal to its proficiency bonus, up to proficiency-bonus uses per long rest and at most once per turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Goblin Traits, Fury of the Small (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the size requirement, damage trigger, and use limits; dial: change the bonus or refresh rate to tune the payoff for exploiting a larger foe.

rules.statement: A hobgoblin using its Help trait can choose a benefit starting at 3rd level: both participants gain temporary hit points, both gain 10 feet of walking speed until the next turn begins, or the helped creature's first successful attack causes its target disadvantage on its next attack within 1 minute. The trait's Help use is a bonus action and refreshes after a long rest, with uses equal to proficiency bonus.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Hobgoblin Traits, Fey Gift (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the benefit requires helping another creature and is limited by proficiency-bonus uses; dial: adjust the reward or duration to set the value of reciprocal aid.

rules.statement: A hobgoblin that misses an attack or fails an ability check or saving throw can gain a bonus equal to visible allies within 30 feet, capped at +3; uses equal to proficiency bonus return after a long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Hobgoblin Traits, Fortune from the Many (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require a failed roll and nearby visible allies, with a +3 cap; dial: change the ally cap or range to make group support more or less decisive.

rules.statement: A tortle can withdraw into its shell as an action, gaining +4 AC and advantage on Strength and Constitution saves, but becomes prone, has speed 0, cannot take reactions, and can only use a bonus action to emerge. The shell state ends when the tortle emerges.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Tortle Traits, Shell Defense (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the strong defense and severe loss of mobility and actions; dial: change the defense bonus or restrictions to trade safety against helplessness.

rules.statement: A kenku can imitate sounds it has heard, including speech; a listener identifies the imitation only by succeeding on a Wisdom (Insight) check against a difficulty of 8 plus the kenku's proficiency bonus and Charisma modifier.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Kenku Traits, Mimicry (dnd5e-motm#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: imitation is limited to heard sounds and detectable by a successful check; dial: change the difficulty to make deception more or less reliable.

rules.statement: At least three arcanists create a soul-trapping container in a three-day rite, using arcane and psionic work and sacrificing the same number of living victims as participants; completing it grants the participants free-willed undeath.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Collaborative Undeath, p. 42 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: requires a group, equal-numbered living sacrifices, and three days; dial: changing any requirement alters how accessible this route to undeath is.

rules.statement: This undeath lasts only as long as the sacrificed victim would have lived. Repeating the rite with new victims resets the duration.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Collaborative Undeath, p. 42 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the victim's remaining lifespan limits the benefit; dial: changing the lifespan rule changes the sacrifice's cost and the duration gained.

rules.statement: When one of these undead is destroyed, it is not restored; its mind instead moves into the container and can commune there with other trapped minds and sacrificed souls.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Collaborative Undeath, p. 42 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: destruction transfers the mind but does not restore the body; dial: allowing restoration would make the anchor more protective.

rules.statement: A creature holding the container has advantage on attacks, checks, and saving throws against its associated undead, while those undead have disadvantage on the same rolls against the holder. The holder can communicate telepathically with trapped souls, and the undead can communicate telepathically with the holder; the holder can silence souls but cannot stop the undead from speaking.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Collaborative Undeath, p. 42 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: possession shifts leverage to the holder, but gives only limited control over communication; dial: changing the asymmetry adjusts the danger of entrusting someone with the anchor.

rules.statement: If a creature holds an iron token made from a hag's tooth or nail, it can whisper with her across up to 10 miles; each side hears only the other's voice, not surrounding sounds. The hag can have up to three active tokens, locate them approximately as an action, and deactivate any of them remotely without an action.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Iron Token, p. 47 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: communication is limited by 10-mile range and three active tokens; dial: changing those caps adjusts the hag's reach and monitoring.

rules.statement: An alkilith that continuously surrounds a door, window, or similar opening for 6d6 days turns it into a permanent portal to a random layer of the Abyss.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Abyssal Rift, p. 44 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the opening must remain covered for 6d6 days and the destination is random; dial: changing duration or destination control alters the threat and predictability.

rules.statement: An archdruid can transform into a Beast or Elemental of challenge rating 6 or lower twice per day, for up to 9 hours. The druid keeps current and maximum hit points, languages, speech, and spellcasting; equipment can drop, merge, or be worn, and the druid reverts on death, unconsciousness, or by using a bonus action.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Archdruid, p. 48 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: forms are limited by type, rating, uses, and duration, while preserving specified traits; dial: changing these limits shifts the transformation's versatility and risk.

rules.statement: A creature reduced to 0 hit points or incapacitated by an astral dreadnought's bite is swallowed and transported with its belongings to the dreadnought's sealed demiplane. A separate legendary action can send a Huge-or-smaller creature it sees within 60 feet there on a failed DC 19 Charisma save; the target returns after its next turn to its former space or the nearest open space.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Astral Dreadnought, p. 51 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: swallowing requires the stated bite outcome, while the ranged removal costs a legendary action and permits a save; dial: changing entry or exit conditions adjusts containment strength.

rules.statement: If the dreadnought dies, its demiplane disappears and its contents appear around its corpse; otherwise the demiplane cannot be damaged from within and is escapable only by planar-travel magic.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Astral Dreadnought, p. 51 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: escape is restricted, but the container's destruction releases everything; dial: changing the escape or release trigger changes the permanence of containment.

rules.statement: An amnizu can summon 2d4 bearded devils or 1d4 barbed devils once per day. They appear within 60 feet, serve as allies, cannot summon others, and remain for 1 minute unless dismissed by the summoner using an action or the summoner dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Variant: Devil Summoning, p. 46 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the summon is limited by daily use, duration, and a fixed set of creatures; dial: altering those limits changes the scale and persistence of recruited aid.

rules.statement: If a creature remains stunned by an amnizu for the full minute, it forgets everything it sensed, experienced, and learned during the previous 5 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Amnizu, p. 46 (dnd5e-motm#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: erasure requires an uninterrupted minute of stun and removes only the last 5 hours; dial: changing either threshold changes how severe the effect is.

rules.statement: A failed lich-making ritual can bind the would-be lich’s soul to a nearby person with a hate-filled heart, making the resulting creature that person’s servant. It can serve only an evil master; if the master genuinely turns away from evil, the servant is destroyed.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Boneclaw (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the failed ritual redirects the soul into a master-bound servant; dial: require an evil master and destroy the servant if the master sincerely changes.

rules.statement: A bound servant cannot be permanently destroyed while its master lives: if destroyed, it reforms with full hit points in 1d10 hours at a location within 1 mile of the master.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Boneclaw — Rejuvenation (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: destruction triggers a return; dial: the 1d10-hour delay and 1-mile limit constrain where and when it comes back.

rules.statement: A creature holding even a tiny piece of a target or an object connected to it knows the most direct route to that target or object while it is within 1 mile.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Banderhobb — Resonant Connection (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a physical remnant provides tracking; dial: it must be carried, and the target must remain within 1 mile.

rules.statement: A creature can swallow one grappled creature of Medium size or smaller. The captive is blinded and restrained, has total cover from outside effects, and takes 3d6 necrotic damage at the start of each of the swallower’s turns; the swallower can release it at will, and it is also released if the swallower dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Banderhobb — Swallow (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: swallowing creates a protected, harmful holding state; dial: only one captive fits, and release or the captor’s death ends it.

rules.statement: Within its lair, a creature can reshape nonliving terrain across an area up to 500 feet square to imitate a place desired by a humanoid whose desires it has sensed. The change takes 10 minutes, cannot create moving parts or magical properties, and lasts until the creature dies or reshapes the area again; close inspection reveals created objects as fakes.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Balhannoth — Lair Actions (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sensed desire supplies the model for a bounded reality alteration; dial: transformation is limited to nonliving terrain and is imperfect on inspection.

rules.statement: A creature in the lair’s region can sense the strongest desires of humanoids within 1 mile, including whether they seek a safe place to rest. Creatures within 1 mile also feel increasingly drawn toward what they most desire as they approach the lair; both effects end immediately when the creature dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Balhannoth — Regional Effects (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the lair exposes desires and projects a lure; dial: both effects are confined to a 1-mile region and cease with the source’s death.

rules.statement: A creature can create a temporary invisible rift in a visible opening within 5 feet, if that opening is no larger than 10 feet on any side. It links to a point within 30 feet; only the creator can use it, and it lasts until the end of the creator’s next turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Boggle — Dimensional Rift (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: an opening becomes a short-lived passage; dial: the destination is within 30 feet, the entry opening is size-limited, and use is exclusive to the creator.

rules.statement: A creature that devours the corpse of a Fey or humanoid it killed within the past 10 minutes traps the victim’s soul for 24 hours; the feeding takes at least 1 minute and destroys the corpse. During that period, magic that would restore the victim has a 50 percent chance to fail and be wasted; if the devourer dies before the soul is digested, the soul is released, but completed digestion prevents revival.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Barghest — Soul Feeding (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: consuming a fresh corpse temporarily captures its soul; dial: the 1-minute feeding, 24-hour interval, and 50 percent failure chance set the cost and rescue window.

rules.statement: A creature can take on a Small goblin form or return to its true form; only its size and speed change, its worn or carried equipment does not transform, and death restores its true form.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Barghest — Change Shape (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: shape change alters only the creature’s size and speed; dial: equipment remains unchanged and death ends the altered form.

rules.statement: A creature can project a duplicate within 60 feet; while it exists, the original is unconscious, and the creature can have only one duplicate. The duplicate shares the original’s statistics and knowledge, and its experiences are known to the original; it vanishes if either is reduced to 0 hit points or the original dismisses it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Berbalang — Spectral Duplicate (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a duplicate acts as a remote information-gatherer; dial: the original is unconscious, only one can exist, and damage or dismissal ends the projection.

rules.statement: A character who devotes themself to a powerful influence may gradually change into a minotaur, treated as the highest gift of that devotion.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Baphomet (dnd5e-motm#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sustained devotion can transform the devotee; dial: change is gradual and is framed as a rare culmination of service.

rules.statement: In dim light or darkness, a boneclaw can choose creatures within 15 feet to face a DC 14 Constitution save; failures take 34 necrotic damage. It then teleports up to 60 feet to a visible unoccupied dark space, optionally taking one creature it is grappling to a visible unoccupied space within 5 feet of its destination.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Boneclaw, Shadow Jump (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require dimness at both ends and expend a recharge; the shadow environment limits when and where the escape works.

rules.statement: A boneclaw's claw hit can pull a creature up to 10 feet toward it and grapple it (escape DC 14). Each of its two claws can hold a target, but a claw occupied with a grapple can attack only that target.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Boneclaw, Piercing Claw (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each claw has one target and loses attack flexibility while occupied; the cost is committing that limb to restraint.

rules.statement: A bulezau's tail hit can infect a creature, poisoning it until the disease ends unless it succeeds on a DC 13 Constitution save. While poisoned this way, it repeats the save every 24 hours; success ends the disease, while failure reduces its hit point maximum by 4, and it dies if that maximum reaches 0.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Bulezau, Barbed Tail (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the disease progresses only on failed daily saves and ends on a success; its cost is ongoing loss of the victim's maximum vitality.

rules.statement: A cadaver collector can release 1d4 spirits of creatures it has slain into unoccupied spaces within 15 feet. They act immediately after it, fight until destroyed, and disappear if the collector is destroyed; this ability returns after a short or long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Cadaver Collector, Summon Specters (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the spirits are limited to slain victims, a 1d4 group, and one use per rest; their continued existence depends on the collector.

rules.statement: A canoloth prevents other creatures from teleporting into or out of a space within 60 feet; an attempted teleport is wasted.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Canoloth, Dimensional Lock (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the lock covers a 60-foot radius around the canoloth; proximity to the guardian blocks escape and entry by teleportation.

rules.statement: A canoloth's tongue can hit a Medium or smaller target within 30 feet, grapple it (escape DC 15), pull it up to 30 feet closer, and restrain it while the grapple lasts. It can hold only one target with its tongue at a time.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Canoloth, Tongue (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the target-size ceiling and one-target limit constrain the capture; maintaining the hold ties up the tongue.

rules.statement: A catoblepas's death ray targets one visible creature within 30 feet; a failed DC 16 Constitution save deals 36 necrotic damage, or 64 if the failure is by 5 or more, while a successful save halves the damage. The target dies if this damage reduces it to 0 hit points; the ray recharges on a 5–6.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Catoblepas, Death Ray (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ray is restricted to a visible target within 30 feet and recharges only on 5–6; its lethal outcome requires reducing the target to 0 hit points.

rules.statement: When a cave fisher's filament adheres to a creature, that creature is grappled (escape DC 13), and escape checks have disadvantage. The filament has AC 15 and 5 hit points, is immune to poison and psychic damage, and a weapon that fails to sever it sticks to it; the fisher can use the filament action again to make the filament crumble.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Cave Fisher, Adhesive Filament (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the line can be escaped or destroyed, and using the ability again dissolves it; the fisher must invest in maintaining the restraint.

rules.statement: A choker's tentacle hit grapples a Large or smaller creature (escape DC 15) and restrains it; that tentacle cannot grapple another target until the hold ends. On a critical hit, the target also cannot breathe or speak until released.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Choker, Tentacle (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each tentacle is committed to one target, and the breath-and-speech restriction occurs only on a critical hit; restraint costs the choker that tentacle's use.

rules.statement: A cloud giant smiling one can transform to resemble a Beast or Humanoid it has seen, or return to its true form. Its statistics except size stay the same, its equipment is absorbed into the new form, and death restores its true form.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Cloud Giant Smiling One, Change Shape (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the disguise is limited to seen Beast or Humanoid forms and does not change statistics beyond size; death ends the disguise.

rules.statement: A cloud giant smiling one can teleport itself and its carried or worn equipment up to 60 feet to a visible unoccupied space; the ability recharges on a 4–6.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Cloud Giant Smiling One, Cloud Step (dnd5e-motm#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: it requires a visible unoccupied destination within 60 feet and recharges only on 4–6; the movement is limited by available space and readiness.

rules.statement: A corpse flower can contain up to nine humanoid remains; when first encountered it holds 1d6 + 3. Corpses inside it have total cover from outside attacks and effects, and can be removed if the flower dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: p. 83, Corpse Flower — Corpses (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the body shields stored remains; the nine-corpse limit bounds its capacity.

rules.statement: A creature that starts its turn within 10 feet of a corpse flower or one of its zombies must make a DC 14 Constitution save, except Constructs and Undead. Failure poisons it until its next turn; success grants immunity to this stench for 24 hours, and the stench fades 2d4 days after the flower dies.
