locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: p. 83, Corpse Flower — Stench of Death (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a short-range defensive field; a successful resistance prevents repeated exposure for a day.

rules.statement: As a bonus action, the corpse flower can digest one corpse stored inside it, regain 2d10 hit points, and leave no remains; equipment on the corpse is expelled into its space.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: p. 83, Corpse Flower — Digest (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one stored body is consumed per use, trading the corpse for immediate healing and expelled gear.

rules.statement: As a bonus action, the corpse flower can animate one stored corpse as a zombie in an unoccupied space within 5 feet. The zombie acts immediately after the flower, is its ally but not under its control, and carries the flower’s stench.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: p. 83, Corpse Flower — Reanimate (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: creating a nearby ally costs one stored corpse, but the flower does not control the resulting zombie.

rules.statement: A swarm of cranium rats shares one intelligence and the combined memories of its component rats; its heightened intelligence lasts only while the swarm persists. The swarm’s psionic spellcasting works only while it has more than half its hit points.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: p. 84, Cranium Rats (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: collective cognition and psionics depend on the swarm remaining intact and above the stated health threshold.

rules.statement: A cranium rat, and likewise a swarm, cannot have its emotions sensed or thoughts read, and is immune to divination spells.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: p. 84, Cranium Rat — Telepathic Shroud; p. 84, Swarm of Cranium Rats — Telepathic Shroud (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: mental privacy blocks both thought-reading effects and divination.

rules.statement: When a darkling dies, nonmagical light flashes in a 10-foot radius; its body and nonmetal, nonmagical possessions burn to ash. An elder instead releases magical light in that radius, and creatures there make a DC 11 Constitution save or take 2d6 radiant damage and be blinded until the end of their next turn; a success halves the damage and avoids blindness.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: p. 84, Darkling — Death Flash; p. 84, Darkling Elder — Death Burn (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: death triggers a one-time burst; the elder’s stronger magical flare has a saving throw and brief blindness.

rules.statement: When a darkling elder’s transformation ritual succeeds, the supplicant grows into a taller, elf-like form; failure kills the supplicant. Other elders mark the supplicant with glowing tattoos that channel away some accumulated light.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: p. 84, Darkling Elder (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a communal ritual changes the body, but failure is fatal and the process diverts some stored light.

rules.statement: When a deep scion dies in its aquatic form, it reverts to the corpse of the person it once was. It can switch between its human-like true form and a hybrid aquatic form as a bonus action; its equipment does not transform, and its movement statistics differ by form.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: p. 88, Deep Scion — Change Shape (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: changing form is quick, but equipment stays unchanged and death forces reversion.

rules.statement: In water, a deep scion’s psychic screech can transmit its memories from the last 24 hours to its master regardless of distance, provided both are in the same body of water. The screech can be used again after a short or long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: p. 88, Deep Scion — Psychic Screech (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the report covers only the previous day and requires shared water; reuse is limited by a rest.

rules.statement: If Demogorgon dies, the regional effects around his lair fade over 1d10 days rather than ending immediately.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: p. 91, Regional Effects (dnd5e-motm#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the source’s death begins a gradual dissipation, leaving the warped region in place temporarily.

rules.statement: A burst of light fills a 10-foot radius; the user and any creatures it chooses in the area each gain 11 temporary hit points. The burst is available again when a recharge roll shows 5 or 6.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Dolphin Delighter, p. 97 (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the burst affects only a limited radius and grants temporary rather than lasting protection; dial: widen the area or increase the buffer, at the cost of broader or stronger protection.

rules.statement: The user teleports up to 30 feet to a visible, unoccupied space. Just before moving, it may bring one creature within 5 feet, which appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the destination.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Dolphin Delighter, p. 97 (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the move is short and requires a visible destination with room for both travelers; dial: increase range or passengers, at the cost of fewer positional constraints.

rules.statement: The arachnomancer can change into a Large spider for up to 1 hour, or return to its usual form; it can still speak and cast spells while changed. Worn or carried equipment merges into the spider form and cannot be used, and death restores its usual form; the ability recharges after a short or long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Drow Arachnomancer, p. 99 (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation preserves speech and spellcasting but suppresses equipment use and has a one-hour limit; dial: extend duration or retain equipment benefits, at the cost of greater flexibility.

rules.statement: Once per day, the summoner attempts to call a demon, succeeding half the time. On failure it takes 5 psychic damage; on success the demon appears within 60 feet, serves as an ally for up to 10 minutes, and leaves if it or the summoner dies or the summoner dismisses it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Drow Inquisitor, p. 102, Variant: Demon Summoning (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the attempt is uncertain, can injure the summoner, and the ally is temporary; dial: improve reliability or duration, at the cost of increased summoning power or obligation.

rules.statement: Within her lair, the matron mother can project awareness throughout the place until the next round’s initiative count 20: hostile creatures cannot hide from her or gain the benefit of being invisible against her. She cannot use the same lair action in consecutive rounds.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Drow Matron Mother, p. 103, Lair Actions (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the awareness lasts only until the next round’s initiative count 20 and is confined to her lair; dial: expand its reach or duration, at the cost of stronger surveillance.

rules.statement: Once per day, the matron mother summons a glabrezu or yochlol into an unoccupied space within 60 feet. It acts as her ally for up to 10 minutes, leaving if it or she dies or if she dismisses it; the summoned creature cannot summon demons.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Drow Matron Mother, p. 104, Bonus Actions (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the servant is available once daily, temporary, and cannot summon others; dial: increase frequency or duration, at the cost of a stronger ongoing commitment.

rules.statement: When reduced to 0 hit points by a critical hit, the duergar despots’ psychic energy erupts, dealing 14 psychic damage to each creature within 5 feet.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Duergar Despot, p. 107, Psychic Engine (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the backlash occurs only on death from a critical hit and only nearby creatures are exposed; dial: increase its damage or radius, at the cost of making the user’s defeat more dangerous to those around it.

rules.statement: For 1 minute, the mind master becomes Tiny with its worn and carried gear; its weapon damage becomes 1 and its Strength-based rolls are disadvantaged, but it gains +5 to Dexterity (Stealth) checks and AC and may Hide as a bonus action each turn. It can use this again after a short or long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Duergar Mind Master, p. 109, Bonus Actions (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: shrinking improves concealment and defense but sharply reduces weapon damage and penalizes Strength-based rolls; dial: reduce the drawbacks or extend the minute, at the cost of a less constrained transformation.

rules.statement: The mind master can force a visible creature within 60 feet that fails a DC 12 Intelligence save to use its reaction, if available, either to make a weapon attack against a different creature the user can see or to move up to 10 feet in a direction the user chooses. Creatures immune to being charmed are unaffected.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Duergar Mind Master, p. 109, Mind Mastery (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect requires a failed save, an available reaction, and a nearby visible target; dial: broaden control or bypass those limits, at the cost of stronger influence.

rules.statement: The matron mother can inflict a debilitating condition on a target hit by the tentacle rod three times in one turn: for 1 minute, its speed is halved, it has disadvantage on Dexterity saves, cannot use reactions, and must choose between taking an action or a bonus action on its turn. It can repeat a DC 15 Constitution save at the end of each turn to end the effect.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Drow Matron Mother, p. 104, Tentacle Rod (dnd5e-motm#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect requires three hits in one turn, lasts at most a minute, and allows an end-of-turn save; dial: lengthen it or remove a restriction, at the cost of making it harder to escape.

rules.statement: The hammerer deals double damage to objects and structures. Immediately after a creature within 5 feet hits it with an attack, it can make a hammer attack against that creature.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Page 113, Duergar Hammerer (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the bonus limited to objects and structures; dial: broaden eligible targets. Its pain-powered counterstrike makes getting close costly.

rules.statement: A dybbuk can enter an intact corpse within 5 feet if it belonged to a Large-or-smaller Beast or Humanoid; it gains 20 temporary hit points and takes the corpse’s size, but loses incorporeal movement. Possession ends when those temporary hit points are gone or the dybbuk ends it as a bonus action, after which it appears within 5 feet of the corpse.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Page 114, Dybbuk (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require a nearby eligible corpse and use temporary hit points as the possession’s limit; dial: change the host or termination condition. The corpse is a vulnerable, temporary vehicle.

rules.statement: While possessing a corpse, the dybbuk can make it behave unnaturally; creatures of the Beast or Humanoid type that see this must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom save or become frightened for 1 minute. Affected creatures can retry at the end of each turn, and a successful save prevents that creature from being affected again for 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Page 114, Dybbuk (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require a witnessed display and allow repeated saves; dial: change the audience, duration, or immunity window. The supernatural spectacle causes terror.

rules.statement: When an eidolon enters a space occupied by a sacred statue, it can disappear into it and use the statue’s statistics instead of its own. It remains inside until the statue reaches 0 hit points, it leaves as a bonus action, or an effect turns or forces it out; on leaving, it appears within 5 feet of the statue.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Page 115, Eidolon / Sacred Statue (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require a specially prepared statue and let damage, choice, or an expulsion effect end the union; dial: alter the vessel or exit triggers. The spirit is tied to a sacred physical anchor.

rules.statement: An eladrin that is not incapacitated can choose a different seasonal form after finishing a long rest, replacing its statistics with that season’s stat block. Damage, conditions, and other ongoing effects carry over from the previous form.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Page 116, Changeable Natures (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow change only after a long rest and carry existing harm and effects across; dial: change the interval or what carries over. The form responds to emotional temperament.

rules.statement: An elder brain can detect creatures with Intelligence 4 or higher within 5 miles, learning each creature’s distance, direction, and Intelligence score, but nothing else about it. Mind blank, nondetection, or similar protection blocks this sense.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Page 121, Elder Brain (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limit detection to a broad five-mile area and a few facts; dial: widen the range or detail. Protective magic can conceal a creature from the brain.

rules.statement: An elder brain can maintain telepathic conversations with up to 10 creatures at once and can let those participants hear one another. It can form psychic links with up to 10 incapacitated creatures it senses; through a link it perceives the target’s senses, can inspect its emotions and foremost thoughts, and can end the link at will. A target can spend an action to attempt a DC 18 Charisma save to break the link, taking 10 (3d6) psychic damage on a success; a separation of more than 5 miles also ends it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Page 121, Elder Brain (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: cap links and conversations at 10, require incapacitation to establish a link, and impose distance and escape limits; dial: adjust capacity or resistance. The psychic connection exposes perception and thoughts.

rules.statement: Within 5 miles, an elder brain causes creatures to feel watched; it also can overhear telepathic conversations in that area. When telepathic contact is first made, its initiator makes a DC 18 Wisdom save to notice the eavesdropping; success reveals that someone is listening, not who. These regional effects end if the elder brain dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Page 121, Regional Effects (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: confine the influence and eavesdropping to five miles, with a save that reveals only the intrusion; dial: change range or disclosure. The effects are sustained by the brain’s presence.

rules.statement: An elder tempest is always at the center of a storm 1d6 + 4 miles in diameter. Heavy rain or snow lightly obscures the area; heavy rain also extinguishes open flames and hinders sight-based Perception, while strong winds hinder ranged attacks, extinguish flames, and disperse fog.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Page 122, Elder Tempest (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: center the weather on the tempest and use a variable storm size; dial: change its radius or weather effects. The storm accompanies the living elemental.

rules.statement: A flail snail’s shell can be made into three shields; for 1 month, each shield gives its wielder the snail’s Antimagic Shell trait. When that magic fades, the shield remains an exotic shield suitable for making a spellguard shield.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Page 126, Using the Shell of a Flail Snail (dnd5e-motm#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limit the yield to three shields and the borrowed trait to one month; dial: change quantity or duration. The shell’s antimagic property is a finite material resource.

rules.statement: The snail’s shell can emit dazzling light through the end of its next turn, illuminating brightly for 30 feet and dimly for another 30 feet. Creatures that can see it have disadvantage on attacks against it; creatures within the bright light that can see it when the effect starts must pass a DC 15 Wisdom save or be stunned until the light ends; the ability recharges after a short or long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Flail Snail — Scintillating Shell (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limited to a short-lived burst; dial: longer light or more frequent use; the shell needs time to recharge.

rules.statement: The flail snail can retreat into its shell, gaining +4 AC while becoming restrained; it can emerge as a bonus action on its turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Flail Snail — Shell Defense (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: stronger defense trades away movement; dial: increase the defense or remove the restraint; the shell is protective but confines its user.

rules.statement: While the flind is not incapacitated, creatures with the Rampage trait within 10 feet can make a Bite attack as a bonus action.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Flind — Aura of Blood Thirst (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the benefit is restricted to nearby creatures with a particular trait; dial: widen its reach or eligibility; allies must stay close and meet the condition.

rules.statement: When the flind’s chaos flail hits, its target must pass a DC 16 Wisdom save or use its reaction to attack a random nearby creature other than the flind; if none is in reach, it moves half its speed in a random direction instead.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Flind — Flail of Chaos (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failure causes a brief, uncontrolled action; dial: change the save or the action’s severity; the effect disrupts the target’s control.

rules.statement: A flind’s paralysis flail hit deals its normal weapon damage and forces a DC 16 Constitution save; failure paralyzes the target until the end of its next turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Flind — Flail of Paralysis (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the restraint lasts only until the target’s next turn ends; dial: alter the duration or save; the effect is limited to a single successful strike.

rules.statement: Within the lair, Fraz-Urb’luu can change up to five existing doors into walls and create the same number of doors in walls that had none; he can’t use the same lair action on consecutive rounds.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Fraz-Urb’luu’s Lair — Lair Actions (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the changes are confined to the lair and limited to five doors per use; dial: expand the count or area; the lair’s layout is warped by its ruler.

rules.statement: A gauth’s magic-draining ray can make one randomly selected magic item carried by its target lose its magical properties until the start of the gauth’s next turn; a charged item also loses 1d4 charges. Single-use items such as potions and scrolls are excluded.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Gauth — Eye Rays, Devour Magic Ray (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the drain is temporary and selects an eligible item at random; dial: extend it or choose the item; the ray feeds on magic without permanently consuming it.

rules.statement: A swallowed creature in a froghemoth’s gullet is blinded and restrained, has total cover against attacks and other effects from outside, and takes 3d6 acid damage at the start of each froghemoth turn. The gullet holds at most two creatures; if an internal creature deals at least 20 damage to the froghemoth in one turn, it must pass a DC 20 Constitution save or regurgitate all swallowed creatures into spaces within 10 feet, prone.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Froghemoth — Bite (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: capacity is two and escape can be triggered by damage from within; dial: vary capacity or the escape threshold; swallowing protects the predator but risks a forced release.

rules.statement: A willing master who is at least a 3rd-level spellcaster can form a telepathic bond with a gazer familiar and sense what it senses while they are within 1 mile. If the master physically harms the gazer, the gazer ends its familiar service and breaks the bond.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Gazer — Variant: Gazer Familiar (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sensing is limited by a 1-mile range and the bond depends on the gazer’s willingness; dial: extend sensing or relax the requirement; mistreatment ends the service.

rules.statement: Geryon can restrain one visible creature within 60 feet for up to 1 minute after it fails a DC 21 Wisdom save. The creature can end the effect on itself by dealing any damage to one or more of its allies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Geryon’s Lair — Lair Actions, Hateful Restraints (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the restraint has a one-minute limit and an ally-harming escape condition; dial: alter the duration or escape cost; breaking free requires harming others.

rules.statement: A gazer familiar can relay its senses to its bonded master only while they are within 1 mile, and physical harm from the master ends the service and breaks their telepathic bond.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Gazer — Variant: Gazer Familiar (dnd5e-motm#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bond is local and ends upon physical harm; dial: change its range or termination condition; the familiar retains the choice to withdraw.

rules.statement: In Limbo, the anarch can cast creation using the plane’s unformed substance; the created object lasts while the anarch concentrates, regardless of its composition, and concentration ends if the anarch moves more than 120 feet away.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Anarch’s Lair — Create Object (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the object is temporary and concentration-bound; dial: its composition is unrestricted because it is made from Limbo’s mutable substance.

rules.statement: In Limbo, the anarch can spend 10 minutes stabilizing an area with a 5-mile radius centered on itself, shaping the unformed substance there into any inanimate forms it chooses.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Anarch’s Lair — Form Substance (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect takes 10 minutes and is limited to a 5-mile area; dial: the anarch’s control over Limbo permits broad shaping.

rules.statement: An anarch can stabilize objects created in Limbo and brought to the Material Plane, but that stability lasts only while the anarch remains alive. On its death, the regional effects end after 1d6 rounds; formed matter then becomes chaotic energy and dissipates 1d6 rounds later.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Anarch’s Lair — Regional Effects (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: created matter depends on the anarch; dial: the delay of 1d6 rounds gives the effect an aftermath before it disappears.

rules.statement: When the enlightened’s Temporal Strike hits, the target must make a DC 16 Wisdom save or vanish for 1 round. When the effect ends, it reappears where it left from, or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Githzerai Enlightened — Temporal Strike (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the target gets a save and the displacement lasts 1 round; dial: it returns near its departure point rather than choosing a new destination.

rules.statement: A creature poisoned by a grung can suffer an extra effect based on the grung’s color, lasting until that grung’s poison no longer poisons it. The effects include forced noise, charm and the ability to speak Grung, movement or action restrictions, fear of allies, seeking liquid or mud, or eating when food is within reach.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Variant: Grung Poison (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the extra effect lasts only as long as the poison; dial: color determines the effect because the toxin varies by grung type.

rules.statement: A creature that grapples a grung or otherwise touches its skin must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution save or be poisoned for 1 minute. Once it is no longer touching the grung, it can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the poison on a success.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Grung — Poisonous Skin (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: contact triggers a save and the condition has a 1-minute limit; dial: leaving contact allows repeated saves to end it sooner.

rules.statement: If a grung is not immersed in water for at least 1 hour during a day, it gains 1 level of exhaustion at that day’s end. It can recover from this only through magic or by immersing itself for at least 1 hour.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Grung — Water Dependency (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the daily requirement is 1 hour of immersion; dial: failure imposes exhaustion, and recovery has the same immersion cost or requires magic.

rules.statement: A guard drake is made through a ritual lasting several days that requires a chromatic dragon’s aid, 10 pounds of fresh dragon scales, fresh meat, and an iron cauldron. The resulting egg hatches within a few hours, and the hatchling bonds to the first creature that feeds it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Guard Drake (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: creation requires a multi-day ritual and specified materials; dial: the bond forms through first feeding, giving the hatchling an initial focus for trust and aggression.

rules.statement: When a hellfire engine’s chosen weapon kills a creature, the creature’s soul rises in the River Styx as a lemure in Avernus after 1d4 hours. Revival before that happens prevents the change; afterward, restoration requires a wish, or killing the lemure and casting true resurrection on the original body.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Hellfire Engine — Hellfire Weapons (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the soul changes after 1d4 hours and only specified powerful remedies reverse the result; dial: the delay leaves a short window for revival.

rules.statement: When a hobgoblin devastator casts a spell that deals damage or forces saves, it can choose itself and any number of allies to take none of that spell’s damage and automatically succeed on its required saves.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Hobgoblin Devastator — Army Arcana (dnd5e-motm#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the protection applies only to the caster’s own spell and chosen allies; dial: it prevents friendly casualties by exempting them from that spell’s harm and saves.

rules.statement: The hobgoblin can move itself and its worn or carried equipment up to 30 feet to a visible, unoccupied space, but both the departure and arrival spaces must be dimly lit or dark.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Shadow Jaunt, page 155 (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit short-range relocation only between visible spaces with the required lighting; the environment limits its use.

rules.statement: In a 60-foot cone, creatures that fail a DC 13 Wisdom save take 16 psychic damage and are frightened until the howler’s next turn ends; while frightened this way, their speed is halved and they are incapacitated. A successful save grants immunity to this ability from all howlers for 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Howler — Mind-Breaking Howl, page 155 (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed save causes a brief, severe disruption; a successful save prevents repeat exposure for a day.

rules.statement: Hutijin regains 20 hit points at the start of each turn, but taking radiant damage disables this recovery at the start of his next turn. He dies only if he starts a turn at 0 hit points without regenerating.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Hutijin — Regeneration, page 158 (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: recovery is steady but can be interrupted by radiant harm, and reaching zero is not immediately fatal.

rules.statement: A bite that hits can poison its target unless it succeeds on a DC 22 Constitution save. While poisoned, the target cannot regain hit points and takes 10 poison damage at the start of each turn; it can repeat the save at each turn’s end to end the effect.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Hutijin — Bite, page 158 (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bite imposes an ongoing, recoverable condition; repeated saves provide an exit while healing is blocked.

rules.statement: Once per day, the hydroloth can target a visible creature within 60 feet, dealing 14 psychic damage and forcing a DC 16 Intelligence save. On a failure, the target loses proficiencies, spellcasting, and language comprehension, and its Intelligence and Charisma become 5 if either was higher; it can retry the save after each long rest, and specified restorative magic ends the effect early. A successful save grants immunity to that hydroloth’s ability for 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Hydroloth — Steal Memory, page 159 (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a severe memory-linked loss is limited to once daily and can be ended by recovery, restorative magic, or a successful save.

rules.statement: In its lair, Juiblex can make a visible ground area up to 10 feet square slippery or sticky. Slippery slime makes creatures there save against DC 21 Dexterity or fall prone and slide 10 feet randomly; sticky slime instead requires a DC 21 Strength save or restrains them, with an action and DC 21 Strength check to break free. The slime lasts an hour unless burned away, which takes one round; creatures starting their turn in burning slime take 22 fire damage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Juiblex’s Lair — Lair Actions, pages 160–161 (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the lair gains a bounded hazard with a one-hour duration, a specific escape check, and fire as a countermeasure.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of Juiblex’s lair, small bodies of water become acidic and corrode objects that touch them; within 6 miles, surfaces are often slick with clinging slime and Medicine and Survival checks are disadvantaged. These effects fade over 1d10 days after Juiblex dies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Juiblex — Regional Effects, page 161 (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the lair’s influence alters nearby terrain and checks, then dissipates over a defined period after its source dies.

rules.statement: A dragonshield’s damage resistance depends on the dragon color that empowered it: choose or roll a d10 to determine the associated damage type. If frightened or paralyzed by an effect that permits a save, it can retry the save at the start of its turn; ending the condition also ends it for kobolds within 30 feet, who gain advantage on their next attack roll.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Kobold Dragonshield — Dragon’s Resistance and Heart of the Dragon, page 164 (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: an invested gift has a provenance-linked resistance, while recovery from a mental or bodily condition can rally nearby kin.

rules.statement: A kobold inventor can use each improvised weapon option repeatedly, but each device is fragile: it typically lasts only one or two attacks and may work only for its maker. Some options release creatures that act independently and can disperse or lose their effect over time.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Kobold Inventor — Weapon Invention, pages 163–164 (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: improvised devices offer varied short-lived effects, limited by breakage, maker-specific use, or a summoned creature’s uncertain duration.

rules.statement: A korred can command a woven hair rope within 30 feet to move up to 20 feet and try to grapple a visible Large or smaller creature; a failed DC 13 Dexterity save leaves the target grappled and restrained. The korred can release it as a bonus action, and the target is freed if the korred dies or is incapacitated; the rope has AC 20, 20 hit points, and regains 1 hit point at the start of the korred’s turn while both it and the korred remain alive.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Korred — Command Hair, page 166 (dnd5e-motm#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a living maker controls and repairs a durable binding tool, but the binding ends if its controller is disabled or the target is released.

rules.statement: A kruthik can burrow through solid rock at half its burrowing speed, leaving a tunnel behind; the tunnel is 2½ feet wide for a young kruthik, 5 feet for an adult, and 10 feet for a hive lord.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Tunneler, pp. 169–170 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial tunnel width by growth stage; larger creatures leave more room but also a more conspicuous passage.

rules.statement: After six months of steady eating, a young kruthik reaches adult size. When a hive lord dies, the largest kruthik in the hive can form a cocoon and emerge several weeks later as a larger, smarter hive lord.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Adult Kruthik / Kruthik Hive Lord, p. 170 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; food and time gate ordinary growth, while the vacant leadership role prompts the more dramatic change.

rules.statement: A leucrotta can imitate Beast sounds and Humanoid voices it has heard; listeners recognize the imitation as false only with a successful DC 14 Wisdom (Insight) check.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Leucrotta, p. 170 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; imitation can deceive but does not perfectly conceal its artificial nature.

rules.statement: A non-leucrotta, non-gnoll creature that starts its turn within 5 feet of a leucrotta must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution save or be poisoned until its next turn; success grants immunity to leucrottas’ stench for 1 hour.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Leucrotta, p. 170 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; close exposure risks a brief impairment, while surviving the exposure grants temporary protection.

rules.statement: If the leviathan takes at least 50 cold damage during one turn, it partially freezes until the end of its next turn: its speed becomes 20 feet and its attack rolls have disadvantage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Leviathan, p. 172 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; concentrated cold temporarily impairs it, with the effect ending after one turn.

rules.statement: A marut is bound to enforce the terms of a contract recorded in its chest until the contract is fulfilled, punishing parties who break them; it follows the written wording rather than presumed intent, and the contract maker rejects vague, contradictory, or unenforceable terms.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Marut, p. 173 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; enforcement is powerful but limited to clear written terms, and punishment is lethal only under specified conditions.

rules.statement: After eating a Medium Humanoid, a maurezhi can take that creature’s appearance for 1d6 days; the borrowed form gradually decays and then sloughs away.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Maurezhi, p. 175 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; taking another’s appearance requires consuming a corpse and the disguise is temporary.

rules.statement: A maurezhi’s bite can reduce a Humanoid’s Charisma by 1d4 until the victim finishes a short or long rest; if this reduces Charisma to 0, the victim dies and rises 24 hours later as a ghoul unless revived or destroyed.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Maurezhi, p. 175 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; the weakening can wear off with rest, but reaching zero causes death followed by a delayed transformation.

rules.statement: A meazel can teleport itself, its gear, and a creature it is grappling up to 500 feet between dimly lit or dark spaces, provided it has seen the destination; another creature it brings is cursed for 1 hour, allowing Undead and Shadowfell-native creatures within 300 feet to sense it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Meazel, p. 177 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; transporting a victim requires a grapple and suitable known shadowed locations, and the curse exposes the victim to nearby pursuers.

rules.statement: Up to four meenlocks can torment one incapacitated creature telepathically; if it remains incapacitated for 1 hour, it takes 3d6 psychic damage on a failed Wisdom save (DC 10 plus participating meenlocks still in sight throughout), or half on success. A Humanoid reduced to 0 hit points by this damage becomes a full-health meenlock under the game master’s control, reversible only by a wish or divine intervention.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Telepathic Torment, p. 178 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; the process requires prolonged helplessness and coordinated torment, and permanent transformation is difficult to undo.

rules.statement: A merrenoloth’s vessel stays on a destination it names and cannot sink even with a breached hull; if the merrenoloth dies, these effects fade over 1d6 hours. While captaining a vessel, it can also use one lair effect at initiative count 20: create difficult terrain and a flight hazard within 60 feet, add 30 feet to the vessel’s speed for a round, or restore 4d10 hit points to it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Merrenoloth, p. 180 (dnd5e-motm#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; the vessel receives navigation, survival, or repair benefits while its captain lives, with its magic fading after the captain’s death.

rules.statement: A molydeus can replace a failed saving throw with a success up to 3 times per day, and it has advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Molydeus — Traits (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the limited automatic successes and magical resistance; dial down the defenses if the creature should be easier to affect.

rules.statement: On a natural 20 against a creature with a head, the molydeus's weapon can decapitate it if it cannot live without that head, except that creatures taking no damage, with legendary actions, or Huge or larger are immune to decapitation and instead take 27 extra force damage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Molydeus — Demonic Weapon (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated instant-death trigger and exceptions; dial it down if a critical hit should not end a character's life.

rules.statement: A failed Constitution save against Snakebite reduces the target's hit point maximum by the poison damage dealt; the reduction lasts until a long rest, and reaching zero transforms the target into a manes, reversible only by a wish spell.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Molydeus — Snakebite (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the rest-based recovery and severe transformation endpoint; dial down by removing the transformation or shortening the reduction.

rules.statement: Once per day, the molydeus can attempt to summon a chosen group of demons, succeeding with a 50 percent chance; the summoned creatures appear within 60 feet of one of its allies and remain for 1 minute, until either the summoner or a summoned creature dies, or until dismissed as an action.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Molydeus — Variant: Demon Summoning (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the once-daily chance, placement limit, and short duration; dial the odds or summoned force to adjust the benefit.

rules.statement: A morkoth can locate one creature or object on its island as an action, and automatically knows when a new creature or object arrives on the island or in its sanctum.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Morkoth — Regional Effects (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: awareness is bounded to the island and active location finds are limited to one target per action; dial the area or precision to make concealment more viable.

rules.statement: A recent island visitor who fails a DC 10 Intelligence save after a short or long rest misplaces one possession; it stays concealed nearby briefly, but moves to the morkoth's lair after an hour if unrecovered, and is readily noticed by its owner there.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Morkoth — Regional Effects: Lost Possessions (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the rest-triggered risk and one-hour relocation; dial the save, duration, or destination to soften the island's theft pressure.

rules.statement: A visible lair entrance can draw creatures within 30 feet that fail a DC 15 Wisdom save to use their movement each turn to approach the morkoth by the most direct route; they can repeat the save when they see it, at each turn's end, or whenever damaged, and the effect ends on a success.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Morkoth — Regional Effects: Supernatural Lure (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the entrance-based range and repeat-save escape points; dial the range or frequency of saves if compelled movement is too restrictive.

rules.statement: A creature that fails the morkoth's DC 17 Wisdom save against its 30-foot cone is charmed for 1 minute and spends its turns Dashing toward the morkoth; it may retry its save at each turn's end or after taking damage, and a creature that succeeds or ends the effect gains advantage against this ability for 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Morkoth — Hypnosis (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the short duration, escape checks, and 24-hour resistance; dial duration or escape opportunities to reduce forced approach.

rules.statement: When a neogi's Enslave ability is used, one visible creature within 30 feet that fails a DC 14 Wisdom save is charmed for a day, unless the neogi dies or moves more than a mile away; the target obeys commands, cannot react, and can communicate telepathically with the neogi within a mile, while damage lets it retry its save.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Neogi — Enslave (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the range, one-day limit, distance/death breaks, and damage-triggered save; dial duration or loosen command control to reduce the burden.

rules.statement: A neothelid can swallow a Large or smaller target it hits with its tentacles if the target fails a DC 18 Strength save; inside, the target is blinded and restrained, has total cover from outside effects, and takes 21 acid damage at the start of each neothelid turn. If the neothelid takes at least 30 damage in a turn and fails a DC 18 Constitution save, it regurgitates all swallowed creatures; a swallowed creature can escape a dead neothelid using 20 feet of movement and exits prone.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Neothelid — Tentacles (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the size and escape conditions, ongoing damage, and damage-triggered release chance; dial the damage or escape threshold to change the danger of being held.

rules.statement: A narzugon's infernal tack lets its wearer call a bound nightmare as an action; it appears within 20 feet at the start of the wearer's next turn, acts as an ally on the wearer's initiative, and remains for a day, until either dies, or until dismissed. A dead nightmare reforms in the Nine Hells within 24 hours and can be summoned again; the tack requires an evil attuned wearer and the nightmare must first be subdued to equip it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Magic Item: Infernal Tack (dnd5e-motm#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the item, alignment, and subduing requirements alongside the one-day service limit; dial the companion's return or availability if the bond is too reliable.

rules.statement: A spirit can leave a possessed goblin whenever it chooses; once the spirit departs, the goblin returns to its ordinary statistics and loses the benefits it gained from possession. The spirit then seeks another goblin host.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Nilbog, page 195 (passage fragment) (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: possession ends at the spirit’s choice; dial: restrict departure or host-seeking; in-world reason: the spirit prefers to find another goblin before abandoning its host.

rules.statement: A nupperibo’s vermin cloud affects non-devils that start their turn within 20 feet of one or more nupperibos: a DC 11 Constitution save prevents 5 (2d4) acid damage. If a creature is in the area of at least two nupperibos, it rolls that save with disadvantage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Nupperibo, page 197 (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the cloud damages nearby non-devils each turn; dial: change its radius, damage, or stacking penalty; in-world reason: the vermin swarm becomes more dangerous when several creatures’ clouds overlap.

rules.statement: In the Nine Hells, a nupperibo can perfectly track a creature that took damage from any nupperibo’s vermin cloud during the previous 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Nupperibo, page 197 (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the tracking works only in the Nine Hells and for 24 hours after cloud damage; dial: change the place or duration; in-world reason: the vermin’s attack leaves a trail the fiend can follow.

rules.statement: An adult or elder oblex can drain memories from a visible creature within 5 feet. On a failed Wisdom save (DC 15 for an adult, DC 18 for an elder), the target takes 18 (4d8) or 44 (8d10) psychic damage, respectively, and suffers memory drain until a short or long rest or specified powerful healing; while drained, it subtracts a d4 roll from attack rolls and ability checks. Each later drain increases the die one size, through d20, after which the target falls unconscious for 1 hour and the effect ends; constructs, oozes, plants, and undead automatically succeed.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Adult Oblex and Elder Oblex, pages 198–199 (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the penalty persists until rest or qualifying healing, and repeated drain escalates to unconsciousness; dial: alter its duration or escalation; in-world reason: the oblex feeds on memories, weakening its victim as it takes more.

rules.statement: After memory-draining a target, an oblex learns all languages the target knows and gains all its skill proficiencies.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Adult Oblex and Elder Oblex, pages 198–199 (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: knowledge and proficiencies are copied from a drained victim; dial: narrow what can be copied; in-world reason: the oblex takes useful memories as part of feeding.

rules.statement: An adult or elder oblex can extrude a simulacrum of a creature whose memories it stole. It can maintain 1d4 + 1 such imitations as an adult or 2d6 + 1 as an elder, each within 120 feet and connected by an undamageable slime strand; the imitation disappears if no passage at least 1 inch wide remains between it and the oblex.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Adult Oblex and Elder Oblex, pages 198–199 (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each copied body remains tethered within 120 feet and vanishes if the strand’s route is blocked; dial: change the number or tether limits; in-world reason: the apparent person is an extension of the oblex, not an independent creature.

rules.statement: An oinoloth can blight a 30-foot-radius area around itself for 24 hours. Plants there die; creatures entering or starting a turn in the area save against DC 16 Constitution or take 14 (4d6) poison damage and become poisoned, preventing hit-point recovery; every 24 hours they can save again, and three successful saves end the poison, while failures reduce maximum hit points by 5 (1d10), potentially killing the target at zero.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Oinoloth, page 202 (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the blight lasts 24 hours and poison escalates through repeated failed daily saves; dial: change its area, duration, or progression; in-world reason: the oinoloth’s plague sickens creatures and kills vegetation.

rules.statement: Orcus can make up to six corpses in his lair rise as skeletons, zombies, or ghouls; they obey his telepathic commands anywhere in the lair. His undead he creates with specified spells remain under his control indefinitely.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Orcus’s Lair Actions and Master of Undeath, pages 203–204 (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: lair-raised undead are limited to six corpses, while spell-created undead remain controlled indefinitely; dial: change the count or duration; in-world reason: Orcus’s dominion over undeath supplies both animation and command.

rules.statement: A retriever’s master assigns one quarry at a time: a personally known creature or object, or a general kind the master has seen. The construct always knows the quarry’s direction and distance while both are on the same plane, and it always knows where its master is.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Retriever, page 209 (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the construct tracks one assigned quarry across the same plane and its master without fail; dial: vary quarry breadth or tracking range; in-world reason: the retriever is a purpose-built hunting construct.

rules.statement: A phoenix that dies explodes in a 60-foot-radius area; creatures there make a DC 20 Dexterity save, taking 22 (4d10) fire damage on a failure or half on a success, and unattended flammable objects ignite. Its body becomes an indestructible 5-pound cinder that deals 21 (6d6) fire damage to a toucher at most once per round and hatches a new phoenix after 1d6 days.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Phoenix, page 205 (dnd5e-motm#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: death triggers an area blast and eventual rebirth from an indestructible cinder after 1d6 days; dial: alter the blast or recovery time; in-world reason: the phoenix’s fiery death is the start of its rebirth.

rules.statement: A bite can infect a creature: it makes a DC 13 Constitution save or becomes poisoned, repeating the save after each long rest to end the condition. If it reaches 0 hit points while poisoned this way, it dies and immediately becomes a living manes; only a wish spell can undo that transformation.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Rutterkin, p. 210 (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the illness can cause death and permanent transformation; dial: require a wish to reverse it, reflecting the Abyss’s corrupting influence.

rules.statement: A non-demon that starts its turn within 30 feet of one or more rutterkins must make a DC 11 Wisdom save or become frightened of them for 1 minute and restrained while frightened. At the end of its turns it can repeat the save; a successful initial save grants immunity to all rutterkins’ fear for 24 hours, and being within 30 feet of six or more imposes disadvantage on the save.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Rutterkin, p. 210 (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: proximity can immobilize susceptible creatures; dial: demons are exempt and a successful save grants a day’s immunity.

rules.statement: A sea spawn breathes air and water, but must be submerged in the sea for at least 1 minute each day or it begins to suffocate.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Sea Spawn, p. 212 (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the altered body functions in either medium; dial: survival still requires daily contact with the sea.

rules.statement: A sea spawn’s poison-quill attack deals 1d6 poison damage and can poison its target for 1 minute on a failed DC 12 Constitution save; the target can repeat the save at the end of each turn. Its tentacle can grapple a Medium or smaller target hit by the attack, and it cannot use that tentacle on another target until the grapple ends.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Sea Spawn, p. 212 (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: body parts inflict a condition or hold a target; dial: the target gets recurring saves, and the tentacle’s use is occupied by the grapple.

rules.statement: In dim light or darkness, a shadow dancer can teleport up to 30 feet to a visible unoccupied space; both its starting and destination spaces must be dimly lit or dark.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Shadar-kai Shadow Dancer, p. 214 (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: short-range teleportation is available; dial: darkness or dim light must connect both ends.

rules.statement: When a shadow mastiff is in dim light or darkness, it can become invisible, including its carried equipment. The invisibility ends if it uses a bonus action to end it, attacks, enters bright light, or becomes incapacitated; sunlight-created bright light also gives it disadvantage on attacks, checks, and saves.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Shadow Mastiff, p. 215 (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: darkness enables concealment; dial: attacking or exposure to bright light ends it, and sunlight impairs the creature.

rules.statement: A shoosuva’s tail sting can poison a target on a failed DC 14 Constitution save; while poisoned this way, the target is also paralyzed. The target repeats the save at the end of each turn, ending the effect on a success.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Shoosuva, p. 216 (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a successful sting can immobilize a target; dial: the target receives an end-of-turn save to recover.

rules.statement: A creature that starts its turn within a sibriex’s 30-foot corruption aura must make a DC 20 Constitution save or take 4d6 poison damage. A creature that succeeds becomes immune to that sibriex’s aura for 24 hours; vegetation withers and the ground becomes difficult terrain within the aura.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Sibriex, p. 218 (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the aura harms creatures and alters its surroundings; dial: a successful save protects against that source for a day.

rules.statement: A sibriex can target up to three visible creatures within 120 feet with a DC 20 Constitution save. On a failure, a target is poisoned and gains one exhaustion level, then repeats the save at the start of each turn; three successes end the poison and remove exhaustion caused by it, while each failure adds another level. At six levels, the target dies and becomes a living manes controlled by the sibriex; only a wish spell can undo the bodily transformation.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Sibriex, p. 218 (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: repeated failed saves worsen the effect toward death and controlled transformation; dial: repeated successes end it, but reversing the final change requires a wish.

rules.statement: A creature can willingly undergo a sibriex’s flesh warping while remaining within 30 feet of it for at least 1 hour; afterward, one permanent bodily change is chosen or randomly determined. If the effect is temporary, it vanishes when Warp Creature ends, except that a target transformed into a manes retains the change.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Variant: Flesh Warping, p. 219 (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a willing subject can obtain a lasting bodily alteration; dial: the process takes at least an hour nearby and is agonizing.

rules.statement: A ritual can summon a skulk and bind it to obey the summoner for 30 days; while summoned, it is visible and resembles its master vaguely. Its usual invisibility can be bypassed by children aged 10 or younger, a corpse-fat candle made from an unidentified person, or seeing its reflection in a reflective surface.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Skulk, p. 220 (dnd5e-motm#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the summoned creature is compelled for a fixed term; dial: the term is 30 days, and several specific means expose its otherwise hidden form.

rules.statement: A spawn of Kyuss regains 10 hit points at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 hit point and is not in sunlight or running water. Acid, fire, or radiant damage disables this recovery until the start of its next turn; it is destroyed only if it starts its turn at 0 hit points without recovering.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Spawn of Kyuss — Regeneration, p. 225–226 (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: recovery is conditional and repeatable; dial: change the damage types or environmental blockers to suit what disrupts the creature’s vitality.

rules.statement: A worm launched at a visible Humanoid within 10 feet attaches unless the target succeeds on a DC 11 Dexterity save. If not removed or killed before the target’s next turn ends, it burrows in; each worm then deals 2d6 necrotic damage at the end of each of the target’s turns, up to 10d6 per turn, and a target reduced to 0 hit points dies and rises 10 minutes later as a spawn. A disease-curing or curse-removing effect kills all the worms infesting a target.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Spawn of Kyuss — Burrowing Worm, p. 225–226 (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the infestation escalates over time and has specific countermeasures; dial: adjust the damage cap or conversion delay to set the threat’s urgency.

rules.statement: A cultist can transform into a Tiny slug-like form and teleport onto a visible Humanoid within 30 feet; unless the target succeeds on a DC 15 Charisma save, it is charmed and controlled by the cultist on its next turn. At the end of that turn the cultist teleports to a visible unoccupied space within 30 feet and returns to normal; direct attacks and effects cannot target it in slug form, though area effects can affect it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Elder Evil Blessings — Cult of Haask, p. 226 (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control lasts for one turn and the transformed user is protected from direct targeting; dial: vary the control window or exposure to limit the possession-like intrusion.

rules.statement: When the larva mage reaches 0 hit points, it breaks apart into a swarm in the same space and reforms after 24 hours unless the swarm is destroyed.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Star Spawn Larva Mage — Return to Worms, p. 228 (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the return requires the intermediary swarm to survive; dial: change the delay or what must be destroyed to determine how durable the anchor is.

rules.statement: When the larva mage uses its worm plague, each non-star-spawn creature within 10 feet must succeed on a DC 19 Dexterity save or take 5d8 necrotic damage and become blinded and restrained. An affected creature takes 5d8 more damage at the start of each of the mage’s turns, and can end the effect by succeeding on a DC 19 save at the end of its turn.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Star Spawn Larva Mage — Plague of Worms, p. 228 (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect applies in a bounded radius and persists with recurring damage until a successful save; dial: alter the area, recurrence, or escape condition to tune its pressure.

rules.statement: When the star spawn hulk takes psychic damage, each creature within 10 feet takes that damage instead and the hulk takes none. Magic cannot discern the hulk’s thoughts or location.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Star Spawn Hulk — Psychic Mirror, p. 227 (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: incoming psychic harm is redirected to nearby creatures; dial: adjust the radius or whether allies are exempt to change the cost of attacking it.

rules.statement: The seer can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain without provoking opportunity attacks; each creature it passes through takes 1d10 psychic damage at most once per turn. If it ends its turn inside an object, it takes 1d10 force damage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Star Spawn Seer — Out-of-Phase Movement, p. 231 (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: passage through matter causes harm and ending inside matter is costly; dial: change the damage or frequency limits to regulate how freely it phases.

rules.statement: The seer can warp space around a visible creature within 30 feet; on a failed DC 19 Wisdom save, the target and its carried equipment teleport up to 60 feet to a space the seer can see, and creatures within 10 feet of the target’s former location take 6d12 psychic damage. On a successful save, the target instead takes 3d12 psychic damage without teleporting.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Star Spawn Seer — Collapse Distance, p. 231 (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resistance avoids forced movement but not all harm; dial: tune the teleport distance and collateral radius to control the spatial disruption.

rules.statement: A stone cursed’s claw hit can force a DC 12 Constitution save; on failure the target is restrained while beginning to turn to stone, then repeats the save at the end of its next turn. Failing that second save petrifies the target for 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Stone Cursed — Petrifying Claws, p. 233 (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the transformation progresses through a brief restraint stage and has a fixed duration; dial: alter the stages, resistance checks, or duration to set how reversible it is.

rules.statement: At the end of a short rest, a character can make a DC 20 Intelligence (Arcana) check to extract from a stone cursed’s skull a memory answering a spoken question. Whether the check succeeds or fails, the skull cannot be used this way again.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Stone Cursed — Cryptic Whispers, p. 233 (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one question draws on the remnant’s memories and exhausts the skull; dial: vary the check or number of uses to set the reliability and scarcity of this information.

rules.statement: A storm giant quintessent can disperse into the storm surrounding its lair, becoming untargetable and unable to take actions other than lair actions. It can end the state at the start of one of its turns and reappear at any location it chooses within its lair; it cannot use the ability outside its lair or while another creature is suppressing the storm.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Storm Giant Quintessent — One with the Storm, p. 235 (dnd5e-motm#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the storm form grants protection but restricts actions and depends on the lair; dial: change its duration, permitted actions, or required environment to balance escape against agency.

rules.statement: A warrior can make one weapon attack as a bonus action, but until its next turn begins, attacks against it have advantage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Sword Wraith Warrior, Bonus Actions (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: this is a repeatable extra attack; dial: taking the offensive exposes the warrior to easier hits.

rules.statement: A demonic ritual or a power granted by Baphomet can turn a subject into a tanarukk; the transformation corrupts the subject and produces a vicious fiend.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Tanarukk (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ritual or granted power changes the subject’s nature; dial: demonic corruption and volatility are the price.

rules.statement: A tanarukk can move up to its speed toward a creature it sees as a bonus action.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Tanarukk, Bonus Actions (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the movement is limited to its own speed and requires a visible target; dial: none stated.

rules.statement: When a melee attack hits Titivilus, he can use a reaction to attack the attacker with a bite or sword strike, with advantage on the attack roll.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Tanarukk, Reactions (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the counterattack is triggered by being hit in melee and costs a reaction; dial: none stated.

rules.statement: A creature failing a DC 21 save against Titivilus’s frightening speech must flee by the safest route using its turn to Dash for up to 1 minute; it can retry the save at each turn’s end to end the effect.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Titivilus, Actions (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failure compels movement for up to 1 minute; dial: repeated saves provide an exit, and no movement is required if no route exists.

rules.statement: A creature failing a DC 21 save against Titivilus’s persuasive words is charmed for 1 minute; it may retry its save if he damages it, and success makes it immune to this effect for 24 hours.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Titivilus, Actions (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the charm lasts up to 1 minute; dial: damage permits a new save, while a successful save blocks repeat use for 24 hours.

rules.statement: Titivilus can choose to make his voice sound as if it comes from a point within 60 feet whenever he speaks.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Titivilus, Traits (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the false point must be within 60 feet; dial: none stated.

rules.statement: A creature failing a DC 14 save against a tlincalli sting is poisoned for 1 minute; if it misses the save by at least 5, it is also paralyzed while poisoned, and it can retry the save at each turn’s end.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Tlincalli, Actions (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: poison lasts up to 1 minute and severe failure adds paralysis; dial: repeated saves can end the condition.

rules.statement: A tortle that withdraws into its shell gains +4 AC and advantage on Strength and Constitution saves, but becomes prone, has speed 0, has disadvantage on Dexterity saves, cannot react, and can only use a bonus action to emerge.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Tortle, Actions (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: shell defense trades mobility, reactions, and Dexterity protection for stronger defense; dial: emerging costs a bonus action.

rules.statement: A trapper can conceal itself by changing its outward color and texture to resemble stone, earth, or wood; if it remains motionless on a surface at combat’s start, it has advantage on initiative, and an observer that has not seen it move must pass a DC 18 Investigation check to recognize it.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Trapper (dnd5e-motm#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: disguise works for stone, earth, or wood and relies on remaining motionless; dial: careful scrutiny can expose it.

rules.statement: Once per day, the vegepygmy emits toxic spores in a 5-foot-radius cloud that spreads around corners. Non-Plant creatures in the area that fail a DC 12 Constitution save become poisoned, take 2d8 poison damage at the start of each turn, and can repeat the save at the end of each turn to end the effect.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Thorny Vegepygmy — Spores (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the cloud affects nearby non-Plants and can be cleared by repeated saves; dial: adjust its area, frequency, or damage; its daily use limits exposure.

rules.statement: The thorny vegepygmy regains 5 hit points at the start of its turn, but cold, fire, or necrotic damage prevents this recovery at the start of its next turn. It dies if it starts a turn at 0 hit points without regenerating.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Thorny Vegepygmy — Regeneration (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: recovery is automatic but vulnerable to three damage types; dial: change the recovery or interruption; its resilience comes from its plant nature.

rules.statement: When the conjurer uses its daily summon, an elemental appears in an empty space it chooses within 60 feet and obeys it, taking its turn immediately afterward. The elemental lasts for 1 hour, or until it or the conjurer dies or the conjurer dismisses it as a bonus action.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Conjurer Wizard — Summon Elemental (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one obedient elemental can be maintained for up to an hour; dial: alter the creature or duration; the daily limit restrains the conjurer’s access.

rules.statement: The diviner can use its reaction up to 3 times per day when it or a creature it sees makes an attack roll, save, or ability check, rolling a d20 and choosing whether to substitute that result for the roll.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Diviner Wizard — Portent (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the diviner can replace a roll with a newly rolled d20; dial: change the number of uses or eligible rolls; limited uses constrain its influence over chance.

rules.statement: When the abjurer or a creature it can see within 30 feet takes damage, the abjurer can use its reaction to create a barrier that reduces that damage by 4d10 + 4, to a minimum of 0, then disappears. The ability recharges on a roll of 4–6.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Abjurer Wizard — Arcane Ward (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one reaction can sharply reduce a single instance of damage; dial: change the reduction or recharge; the barrier vanishes after absorbing a hit.

rules.statement: At the end of each long rest, the transmuter chooses one benefit for its crafted stone to grant while it bears the stone: 60-foot darkvision, Constitution-save proficiency, resistance to one of five damage types, or 10 feet of extra walking speed. Its transmute ability can change the stone’s benefit when available.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Transmuter Wizard — Transmuter’s Stone (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the carried stone grants one selected benefit at a time; dial: change the menu or when selection occurs; the benefit depends on possessing the crafted item.

rules.statement: Once on each of its turns, the wood woad can spend 10 feet of movement to enter a living tree within 5 feet and emerge beside a visible living tree within 60 feet. Both trees must be Large or bigger, and the destination must have an unoccupied space within 5 feet.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Wood Woad — Tree Stride (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: this is a once-per-turn route between nearby qualifying trees; dial: change the range or tree requirements; the power depends on suitable living trees.

rules.statement: Water exposed within 30 feet of the wastrilith becomes corrupted at the start of each of its turns; container water remains so until it evaporates. A creature that drinks it or swims in it saves against DC 18 Constitution: success grants immunity for 24 hours, while failure deals 4d6 poison damage and poisons it for 1 minute; at the end, another failed save deals 4d8 poison damage and extends the poisoned condition until a long rest.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Wastrilith — Corrupt Water (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: nearby water and stored container water become hazardous, with repeat exposure governed by a save; dial: adjust radius, duration, or harm; the effect spreads through the demon’s corrupted essence.

rules.statement: When the warlock of the Great Old One starts its turn while not incapacitated, each creature of its choice within 10 feet must make a DC 15 Wisdom save or take 3d6 psychic damage.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Warlock of the Great Old One — Whispering Aura (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the aura affects chosen nearby creatures at the start of each turn; dial: change its reach or harm; being incapacitated suppresses it.

rules.statement: When a yagnoloth damages an incapacitated creature within 15 feet, it can deal 7d8 + 4 necrotic damage and gain temporary hit points equal to half the damage. The target also saves against DC 16 Constitution; on failure, its hit point maximum falls by half the necrotic damage until a long rest, and it dies if that maximum reaches 0.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yagnoloth — Life Leech (dnd5e-motm#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the attack requires an incapacitated nearby target and can cause lasting maximum-hit-point loss; dial: change the damage or duration; the drain is tied to a vulnerable victim.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of Yeenoghu’s lair, iron spikes emerge from the ground and stone, impaling the slain; if Yeenoghu dies, the effect fades over 1d10 days.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yeenoghu, Spiky Terrain (p. 271) (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect is fixed to the lair and lasts until its owner dies; dial: set the radius or decay interval to fit the threat. Its cost is a hazardous landscape that endures after the creature’s death.

rules.statement: A devoted Yeenoghu follower that drops a creature to 0 hit points with a melee attack on its turn may use a bonus action to move up to half its speed and make one special jaw attack. A leader’s aura lets any creature with this ability use that jaw attack as a bonus action while within 10 feet of the leader, provided the leader is not incapacitated.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Cultists of Yeenoghu (p. 271) (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the attack-triggered follow-up and aura range are limited; dial: alter the trigger or radius. The cost is dependence on a qualifying kill or nearby leader.

rules.statement: A yeth hound that begins its turn in sunlight is sent to the Ethereal Plane and cannot return to the Material Plane until after sunset. It returns at its former location, and can cross back earlier only as an action when adjacent to its Material-Plane master or pack mate.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yeth Hound, Sunlight Banishment (p. 271) (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sunlight forces the displacement and sunset sets the earliest ordinary return; dial: change the trigger or return condition. The cost is separation from the Material Plane and inability to interact across planes.

rules.statement: A yeth hound and its master can communicate telepathically and share what the hound senses while they are on the same plane. A target that hears the hound’s bay must save against DC 13 or become frightened until the hound’s next turn ends or it is incapacitated; affected targets must flee by their movement while within 30 feet, and a successful save grants 24-hour immunity to all yeth hounds’ baying.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yeth Hound, Telepathic Bond and Baleful Baying (p. 271) (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bond works only on the same plane and the fear is temporary with a defined immunity; dial: vary range or duration. The costs are proximity for communication and a successful save to resist the bay.

rules.statement: A yuan-ti abomination can undergo a quick but painful ritual transformation into an anathema, requiring the sacrifice of hundreds of snakes and bathing in enemies’ blood. The resulting anathema does not age.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yuan-ti Anathema (p. 272) (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
