rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation requires a costly ritual and specific sacrifices; dial: change the ingredients or their quantity. The cost is hundreds of lives and exposure to a painful rite.

rules.statement: A yuan-ti anathema can change shape as a bonus action between its true form and a Huge constrictor snake, retaining the same statistics; carried and worn equipment does not transform.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yuan-ti Anathema, Change Shape (p. 272) (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the shift is limited to two forms and equipment is excluded; dial: add forms or change what carries over. The cost is that gear does not adapt to the new body.

rules.statement: A yuan-ti broodguard transformation takes 1d6 + 6 days after the subject drinks a special potion; a forced subject can make a DC 15 Constitution save, taking 4d6 poison damage on success and otherwise avoiding the change. Lesser restoration or remove curse can stop the process before completion, while wish can reverse it afterward.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Making a Broodguard (p. 273) (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the change is delayed, resistible, and has different remedies before and after completion; dial: alter its duration or countermeasures. The costs are the potion, a possible poison injury, and limited post-transformation reversal.

rules.statement: When a yuan-ti mind whisperer reduces an enemy to 0 hit points, it gains 9 temporary hit points.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yuan-ti Mind Whisperer, Sseth’s Blessing (p. 274) (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the reward is a fixed buffer triggered by defeating an enemy; dial: vary its amount or trigger. The cost is that it requires the enemy to be reduced to 0 hit points.

rules.statement: A yuan-ti nightmare speaker can, once per short or long rest, target a visible creature within 60 feet with an illusory image of its deepest fears. On a failed DC 13 Intelligence save, the target takes 4d10 psychic damage and is frightened; the speaker must concentrate, for up to 1 minute, and the target repeats its save at each turn’s end, taking 2d10 psychic damage on failure or ending the effect on success.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Yuan-ti Nightmare Speaker, Invoke Nightmare (p. 275) (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: it is limited-use, requires concentration, and permits repeated saves; dial: change its recovery or duration. Its costs are the rest-based recharge and the caster’s concentration.

rules.statement: A zaratan can retract into its shell, becoming restrained but gaining resistance to all damage until it emerges; it may spend 2 legendary actions to revitalize while retracted, regaining 5d20 hit points, and must emerge the next time it uses a legendary action after revitalizing. Emerging costs 2 legendary actions and includes a rock-spit attack.
locators: Monsters of the Multiverse: Zaratan, Legendary Actions: Retract, Revitalize, Emerge (p. 278) (dnd5e-motm#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: defense trades mobility for protection, and recovery consumes actions and forces a later emergence; dial: adjust protection or recovery. The cost is restraint and a constrained sequence of actions.

rules.statement: At 1st level, a character has one Hit Die of the type set by their class and starts with hit points equal to its maximum roll plus their Constitution modifier. After resting, they can spend Hit Dice to regain hit points.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 1, “Hit Points and Hit Dice” (p. 12) (dnd5e-phb-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one die sets starting durability; spending it after rest trades a limited resource for recovery.

rules.statement: A 1st-level character has a proficiency bonus of +2, which applies to specified attacks, proficient ability checks and saves, and spell save DCs. A bonus can affect a given roll only once, even if circumstances would multiply or halve it more than once.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 1, “Proficiency Bonus” (p. 12) (dnd5e-phb-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: proficiency improves trained actions but cannot stack repeatedly on one roll.

rules.statement: The optional ability-score point-buy method gives 27 points to spend; scores must be from 8 to 15 before racial increases, and the listed costs rise from 0 points for 8 to 9 for 15.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 1, “Variant: Customizing Ability Scores” (p. 13) (dnd5e-phb-2014#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: point-buy replaces random assignment with controlled choices, bounded by a fixed budget.

rules.statement: A character can choose the class-and-background starting gear or buy starting gear using the gold allotment for their class; they may also take one trinket at no cost. The suggested carrying limit is total gear weight no greater than Strength × 15 pounds.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Step 5: Choose Equipment (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: gear is limited by a Strength-based load; dial: allow heavier loads if the setting supports them, at the cost of burdening the carrier.

rules.statement: Without armor or a shield, Armor Class is 10 + Dexterity modifier. If several features offer different ways to calculate Armor Class, choose one calculation rather than combining them.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Armor Class (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use one defense calculation; dial: permit stacking only if the setting’s defenses are meant to compound.

rules.statement: A weapon attack roll adds the relevant ability modifier and, if the wielder is proficient with that weapon, their proficiency bonus. Melee weapons normally use Strength, finesse melee weapons may use Dexterity instead, and ranged weapons use Dexterity unless thrown, which may use Strength.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Weapons (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: weapon use is constrained by weapon properties and training; dial: broaden the usable abilities if the world has different combat practices.

rules.statement: When a character gains a level, they gain one Hit Die’s worth of hit points, adding their Constitution modifier; they may instead take the class’s listed fixed value. Each level gained adds 1 more maximum hit point for every 1-point increase in Constitution modifier, and an ability score cannot rise above 20.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Beyond 1st Level (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: advancement increases durability and is limited by the ability-score cap; dial: change growth rates to set a different power curve.

rules.statement: A dwarf’s walking speed is 25 feet and is not reduced by heavy armor. The dwarf can see in dim light within 60 feet as though it were bright, and in darkness within that range as dim light, but cannot distinguish color there.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Dwarf Traits (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: inherited traits set movement and sensory limits; dial: adjust range or armor interaction to fit the ancestry.

rules.statement: A dwarf has advantage on saving throws against poison and resistance to poison damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Dwarf Traits: Dwarven Resilience (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ancestry mitigates poison; dial: weaken or strengthen the defense to tune the species’ resilience.

rules.statement: A hill dwarf’s hit point maximum increases by 1, then increases by 1 again each time the dwarf gains a level.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Hill Dwarf: Dwarven Toughness (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a subrace grants steady durability; dial: change the per-level increase to alter long-term toughness.

rules.statement: An elf can see in dim light within 60 feet as though it were bright, and in darkness within that range as dim light, but cannot distinguish color there. Elves also gain the benefit of a human’s 8 hours of sleep by meditating for 4 hours.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Elf Traits (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ancestry provides limited dark sight and a shorter rest practice; dial: vary the range or rest duration to establish different biological needs.

rules.statement: A halfling can reroll a 1 on an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, and must use the new result. Halflings also have advantage on saves against being frightened and can move through the space of any creature larger than themselves.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Halfling Traits (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ancestry grants a narrow reroll and situational defenses; dial: change the trigger or reroll frequency to tune the luck effect.

rules.statement: A stout halfling has advantage on saving throws against poison and resistance to poison damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Stout: Stout Resilience (dnd5e-phb-2014#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: this subrace reduces poison’s impact; dial: adjust the protection to distinguish its resilience from other ancestries.

rules.statement: A dragonborn chooses one dragon ancestry, which sets the damage type and whether its breath covers a 5-by-30-foot line or a 15-foot cone. As an action, it exhales; creatures in the area save against DC 8 + Constitution modifier + proficiency bonus, taking 2d6 damage on a failure or half on a success; damage rises to 3d6 at level 6, 4d6 at 11, and 5d6 at 16, and the breath cannot be used again until a short or long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Dragonborn Traits, p. 35 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one ancestry-defined area attack, with damage scaling by level and a rest-based reuse limit.

rules.statement: A dragonborn has resistance to the damage type associated with its chosen ancestry.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Dragonborn Traits, p. 35 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resistance is limited to one inherited damage type, reflecting the chosen ancestry.

rules.statement: A rock gnome can spend 1 hour and 10 gp of materials to make a Tiny clockwork device with AC 5 and 1 hit point. It lasts 24 hours unless the gnome spends 1 hour repairing it; the gnome can dismantle it with an action to recover its materials, and can have no more than three active devices.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Rock Gnome, p. 38 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: small devices require time and materials, expire without upkeep, and are capped at three active builds.

rules.statement: A clockwork toy moves 5 feet on each of its turns in a random direction and makes fitting noises; a fire starter produces a miniature flame usable to light a candle, torch, or campfire with an action; a music box plays one song at moderate volume when opened and stops at the song’s end or when closed.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Rock Gnome, p. 38 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each device has a narrow, specified function rather than general-purpose capability.

rules.statement: A forest gnome knows the minor illusion cantrip, using Intelligence as its spellcasting ability. It can also communicate simple ideas to Small or smaller beasts through sounds and gestures.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Forest Gnome, p. 38 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: illusion is a limited spell, while animal communication is restricted to simple ideas and small creatures.

rules.statement: A gnome has advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws against magic.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Gnome Traits, p. 38 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: magical resistance applies only to three kinds of saving throw, not to all harm.

rules.statement: A half-orc reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright can instead remain at 1 hit point; after using this ability, it cannot do so again until finishing a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Half-Orc Traits, p. 42 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a single near-fatal recovery is available per long rest, but does not prevent outright death.

rules.statement: When a half-orc scores a critical hit with a melee weapon attack, it rolls one of the weapon’s damage dice one additional time and adds that die to the critical hit’s extra damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Half-Orc Traits, p. 42 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the damage bonus requires both a critical hit and a melee weapon attack.

rules.statement: A tiefling resists fire damage and knows the thaumaturgy cantrip. At level 3 it can cast hellish rebuke once per day as a 2nd-level spell; at level 5 it can also cast darkness once per day, using Charisma for these spells.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Tiefling Traits, p. 44 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: inherited magic grants a cantrip and level-gated spells with a once-per-day limit.

rules.statement: A half-elf has advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic cannot put it to sleep.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Half-Elf Traits, p. 40 (dnd5e-phb-2014#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: inherited protection covers charm and magical sleep only.

rules.statement: You can enter a rage as a bonus action. While raging and not wearing heavy armor, you gain advantage on Strength checks and saves, extra damage on Strength-based melee weapon attacks according to your level, and resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage; you cannot cast spells or maintain concentration.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Barbarian: Rage, p. 49 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial duration and availability; rage is a limited combat reserve that suppresses spellcasting.

rules.statement: A rage lasts up to 1 minute, but ends sooner if you fall unconscious, or if your turn ends without your having attacked a hostile creature or taken damage since your previous turn. You can end it yourself as a bonus action; uses are limited by level and return after a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Barbarian: Rage, p. 49 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial the duration and recovery; sustained fury requires ongoing danger and rest replenishes it.

rules.statement: At 3rd level, when you rage, you may enter a frenzy; for the rest of that rage, you can make one melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after the turn you began it. When the rage ends, you gain one level of exhaustion.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Path of the Berserker: Frenzy, p. 50 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial the added attacks against the aftermath; pushing fury further leaves lasting fatigue.

rules.statement: While raging, you cannot be charmed or frightened; if either condition is already affecting you when the rage begins, its effect is suspended until the rage ends.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Path of the Berserker: Mindless Rage, p. 50 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial protection to the rage’s duration; fury temporarily overrides mental influence.

rules.statement: At 10th level, you can use an action to target one creature you can see within 30 feet that can see or hear you. It must pass a Wisdom save or be frightened until your next turn ends; you can use later actions to extend the effect, but it ends if the creature ends its turn out of sight or more than 60 feet away. After a successful save, that creature is immune to this feature for 24 hours.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Path of the Berserker: Intimidating Presence, pp. 50–51 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial reach, persistence, and repeat use; fear depends on the target perceiving the threat and can be resisted.

rules.statement: At 11th level, if you are raging when reduced to 0 hit points but do not die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution save to fall to 1 hit point instead. Each later use raises the DC by 5; a short or long rest resets it to 10.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Barbarian: Relentless Rage, p. 50 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial repeatability through an escalating save; surviving repeated grievous wounds becomes less reliable until rest.

rules.statement: At 15th level, your rage ends early only if you fall unconscious or choose to end it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Barbarian: Persistent Rage, p. 50 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial the usual early-ending conditions; exceptional rage persists until unconsciousness or a deliberate choice.

rules.statement: A creature within 60 feet that can hear you can receive one inspiration die when you use a bonus action. Within 10 minutes, it may add the die to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw, choosing after rolling the d20 but before the outcome is announced; a creature can hold only one such die, and the die is lost when rolled. Uses equal your Charisma modifier, minimum one, return after a long rest; the die grows from d6 to d8 at 5th level, d10 at 10th, and d12 at 15th.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Bard: Bardic Inspiration, pp. 54–55 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial the limited pool and short-lived token; encouragement is handed to an ally and expended when used.

rules.statement: A bard regains all spent spell slots after a long rest. When gaining a bard level, the bard may replace one known bard spell with another from that list of a level for which they have spell slots.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Bard: Spell Slots; Spells Known, p. 53 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial recovery and repertoire flexibility; magical capacity returns with rest, while learning reshapes a limited set of known spells.

rules.statement: A cleric prepares a number of cleric spells equal to Wisdom modifier plus cleric level, minimum one, choosing only spells for which they have slots. The list can be changed after a long rest, with at least 1 minute of prayer and meditation per spell level for every spell prepared; prepared spells remain available to cast using an appropriate slot.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Cleric: Preparing and Casting Spells, p. 58 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial preparation capacity and ritual time; access is flexible but requires focused prayer after rest.

rules.statement: A cleric can cast a prepared cleric spell as a ritual if it has the ritual tag. A bard can do so with any known bard spell bearing that tag.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Cleric: Ritual Casting, p. 58; Bard: Ritual Casting, p. 53 (dnd5e-phb-2014#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dial eligibility to prepared or known ritual-tagged spells; ritual use is restricted by prior access to the spell.

rules.statement: As an action, you can affect undead that see or hear you within 30 feet. Each must make a Wisdom save; on a failure it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage, and must flee from you, cannot approach within 30 feet or take reactions, and has sharply limited actions.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Channel Divinity: Turn Undead, p. 60 (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a short-lived area effect; dial: range and duration; the target’s successful save or taking damage ends the restraint.

rules.statement: At 6th level, you can target a visible creature within 60 feet as an action; on a failed Wisdom save, you read its surface thoughts for 1 minute. During that time, you can end the effect as an action to cast suggestion on it without spending a spell slot, and it automatically fails that spell’s save.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Channel Divinity: Read Thoughts, p. 61 (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: brief access to current thoughts; dial: range and duration; the target can resist the initial intrusion.

rules.statement: When you use a 1st-level-or-higher spell to restore another creature’s hit points, that creature regains extra hit points equal to 2 plus the spell’s level. From 6th level, you also regain that many hit points.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Life Domain: Disciple of Life and Blessed Healer, p. 61 (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: healing is amplified by a fixed amount tied to spell level; dial: bonus size; the self-healing benefit requires healing someone else.

rules.statement: As an action, you distribute healing among creatures within 30 feet, with a total pool of hit points equal to five times your cleric level. No target can be healed above half its hit-point maximum, and undead and constructs are ineligible.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Life Domain: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life, p. 61 (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a level-scaled healing pool; dial: pool size and range; the half-health ceiling and target exclusions limit its use.

rules.statement: As an action, you can call for divine aid and roll percentile dice; the call succeeds if the result is no greater than your cleric level, with success producing an effect chosen by the game master. After success, you cannot call again for 7 days; after failure, you can try again after a long rest. At 20th level, it succeeds automatically.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Divine Intervention, p. 60 (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: help is uncertain and controlled by the sponsor; dial: success odds and cooldown; failure or successful intervention limits further appeals.

rules.statement: When you take damage, you can use a reaction to grant yourself or a creature within 30 feet resistance to that instance of acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Tempest Domain: Dampen Elements, p. 63 (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resistance applies only to one qualifying damage instance; dial: eligible types and range; it consumes a reaction.

rules.statement: As an action, you can assume the shape of a beast you have seen before, twice between rests. The form’s challenge rating is limited by your level and other restrictions; it lasts up to half your druid level in hours, and you can revert early as a bonus action or automatically when unconscious, reduced to 0 hit points, or dead.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Shape, pp. 67–68 (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: temporary animal forms with restricted eligibility; dial: uses, duration, and form limits; reverting restores the prior hit points, subject to excess damage carrying over.

rules.statement: In beast form, your game statistics become those of the beast, but you keep your personality and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores, along with your proficiencies. You cannot cast spells or use speech or hand-dependent actions unless the form allows them; equipment may fall, merge, or be worn, and merged equipment has no effect until you revert.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Shape, p. 68 (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation changes physical capabilities while preserving core mental traits; dial: retained abilities and equipment handling; the chosen body restricts actions and gear.

rules.statement: During a short rest, you can recover expended spell slots whose combined levels are no more than half your druid level, rounded up; none can be 6th level or higher. You can use this recovery once per long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Circle of the Land: Natural Recovery, p. 68 (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limited reserve replenishment during rest; dial: total levels recovered; the 6th-level cap and once-per-long-rest limit constrain recovery.

rules.statement: At 10th level, you can spend two uses of Wild Shape together to become an air, earth, fire, or water elemental.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Circle of the Moon: Elemental Wild Shape, p. 70 (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: an enhanced form costs two transformation uses; dial: eligible forms and use cost; the choice consumes a scarce reserve.

rules.statement: At 18th level, you can cast druid spells in beast form and provide their verbal and somatic components, but not material components. At 20th level, Wild Shape uses become unlimited, and you can omit verbal and somatic components and material components without a cost that are not consumed.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Beast Spells and Archdruid, pp. 68–69 (dnd5e-phb-2014#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spellcasting in an altered body is progressively less restricted; dial: which components can be omitted; material costs and consumed components remain constraints.

rules.statement: Choose one fighting specialty; its benefit is limited to its stated situation. For example, ranged attacks gain +2 to hit, while wearing armor grants +1 AC.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Fighting Style, p. 73 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one specialty; dial: its trigger and bonus; the benefit applies only in the stated combat circumstances.

rules.statement: On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain 1d10 hit points plus your fighter level. After using this once, you must finish a short or long rest before using it again.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Second Wind, p. 73 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one use per rest; dial: the healing amount; recovering stamina is limited by rest.

rules.statement: On your turn, you can take one extra action. You regain this ability after a short or long rest; from fighter level 17, you can use it twice between rests, but no more than once on a turn.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Action Surge, p. 73 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one extra action per rest; dial: a second use at level 17; exertion is constrained by recovery and turn limits.

rules.statement: A Battle Master spends one superiority die to fuel a maneuver, and can apply no more than one maneuver to an attack. The fighter starts with four d8 dice, regains spent dice after a short or long rest, and gains one die each at levels 7 and 15; the dice become d10s at level 10 and d12s at level 18.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Combat Superiority, pp. 74–75 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: four dice and one maneuver per attack; dial: die size and pool growth; techniques consume a finite reserve that returns with rest.

rules.statement: After a one-hour ritual with a weapon within reach, an Eldritch Knight bonds to it and cannot be disarmed of it unless incapacitated. If the weapon is on the same plane, the knight can summon it to hand as a bonus action; the knight can bond up to two weapons and summon only one at a time.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Weapon Bond, p. 76 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: two bonds and one summon per bonus action; dial: ritual duration and plane restriction; the bond requires deliberate time and proximity to establish.

rules.statement: A monk has ki points equal to monk level and spends them to use ki techniques; spent points return after a short or long rest that includes at least 30 minutes of meditation. The save DC for a technique is 8 plus proficiency bonus plus Wisdom modifier.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Ki, p. 79 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one point per monk level; dial: recovery requires meditation during rest; techniques draw on a finite inner reserve.

rules.statement: When a ranged weapon attack hits you, you can use your reaction to reduce its damage by 1d10 plus your Dexterity modifier and monk level. If this reduces the damage to zero, you can catch a hand-sized missile with a free hand and spend 1 ki point to make a ranged attack with it as part of the same reaction.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Deflect Missiles, p. 79 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one reaction to reduce damage; dial: the reduction and counterattack; catching requires a free hand and the counterattack spends ki.

rules.statement: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can spend 1 ki point to force a Constitution save. On a failure, the creature is stunned until the end of your next turn.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Stunning Strike, p. 80 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one target and a save; dial: the duration; the effect costs ki and may be resisted.

rules.statement: In dim light or darkness, you can use a bonus action to teleport up to 60 feet to a visible, unoccupied space that is also in dim light or darkness. You then have advantage on your first melee attack before the turn ends.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Shadow Step, p. 81 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: up to 60 feet between qualifying shadows; dial: distance and required visibility; the route is limited by lighting and a free destination.

rules.statement: After hitting a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 3 ki points to set harmless vibrations in its body for a number of days equal to your monk level. You can end them harmlessly, or use an action while on the same plane to force a Constitution save: failure reduces the creature to 0 hit points, while success deals 10d10 necrotic damage; only one creature can carry the vibrations at a time.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Quivering Palm, p. 81 (dnd5e-phb-2014#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one creature and a level-based duration; dial: the delayed outcome; the effect costs ki, requires a later action, and can be resisted.

rules.statement: Using an action, sense celestial, fiend, or undead creatures within 60 feet that are not behind total cover, learning their type but not identity; also sense consecrated or desecrated places and objects in that radius. You can do this a number of times equal to 1 plus your Charisma modifier, regaining all uses after a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Divine Sense, p. 85 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limited detection; dial: uses per rest and 60-foot range; the user must spend an action and has only a bounded number of uses.

rules.statement: A healing reserve replenishes on a long rest and holds hit points equal to five times your paladin level. As an action, touch a creature to restore up to the reserve remaining, or spend 5 points to cure one disease or neutralize one poison; this has no effect on undead or constructs.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Lay on Hands, p. 85 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: healing is transferable from a personal reserve; dial: reserve size and the 5-point cure cost; the reserve cannot replenish until a long rest.

rules.statement: When a melee weapon attack hits, expend a spell slot to add radiant damage: 2d8 for a 1st-level slot, plus 1d8 per slot level above that, to a maximum of 5d8. Add another 1d8 against an undead or fiend.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Divine Smite, p. 86 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: stored spell capacity can amplify a successful weapon hit; dial: slot level sets damage, capped at 5d8, with a target-type bonus.

rules.statement: A paladin’s oath is sworn at 3rd level and permanently binds the character; its choice grants features at levels 3, 7, 15, and 20. Oath spells are always prepared and do not count against the normal preparation limit, while Channel Divinity can be used once and refreshes after a short or long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Sacred Oath, p. 86 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a sworn commitment grants powers; dial: oath features arrive at set levels and Channel Divinity has a rest-based limit; the vow is permanent.

rules.statement: While conscious, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet gain a bonus to saving throws equal to your Charisma modifier, with a minimum of +1. At 18th level the radius becomes 30 feet.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Aura of Protection, p. 86 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: protection affects allies in a bounded nearby area; dial: bonus follows Charisma and radius expands at 18th level; unconsciousness ends the benefit.

rules.statement: At 10th level, while conscious, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet cannot be frightened; at 18th level the radius becomes 30 feet.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Aura of Courage, p. 86 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a field blocks a specified mental effect for nearby allies; dial: range grows at 18th level; the protection depends on the paladin remaining conscious.

rules.statement: At 14th level, use an action to end one spell affecting yourself or a willing creature you touch. You can do this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, minimum one, and regain all uses after a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Cleansing Touch, p. 86 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: touch removes a spell effect; dial: action and Charisma-based daily uses; uses return only after a long rest.

rules.statement: A paladin who breaks a vow may seek forgiveness through confession and penitential acts such as an all-night vigil or fasting. A willful violation without repentance can, at the DM’s discretion, require abandoning the class or adopting an oathbreaker path.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Breaking Your Oath, p. 87 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: misconduct triggers a path to absolution; dial: consequences depend on willfulness, repentance, and the DM’s judgment; penitence costs time or self-denial.

rules.statement: At 3rd level, an action can imbue one held weapon for 1 minute: add your Charisma modifier, minimum +1, to its attack rolls, make it magical if it was not already, and emit bright light for 20 feet plus dim light for another 20 feet. The effect ends if you stop holding or carrying it or fall unconscious, and can be ended early on your turn as part of another action.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Oath of Devotion: Channel Divinity, p. 87 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a temporary blessing is bound to one weapon; dial: one-minute duration and a Charisma-based attack bonus; dropping it or losing consciousness ends the effect.

rules.statement: At 3rd level, an action presents a holy symbol and affects each fiend or undead that can see or hear you within 30 feet. A creature that fails a Wisdom save is turned for 1 minute or until damaged, must move away, cannot willingly approach within 30 feet, and cannot take reactions; it can Dash or try to escape a movement-blocking effect, or Dodge if it cannot move.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Oath of Devotion: Turn the Unholy, p. 87 (dnd5e-phb-2014#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a bounded declaration can drive specified creatures away; dial: 30-foot range and a save gate the effect, which ends on damage or after 1 minute.

rules.statement: Once on each of your turns, when you make a weapon attack, you may make one more attack with that weapon against a different creature within 5 feet of the first target and within the weapon’s range.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Horde Breaker (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the extra attack is limited to once per turn and requires a nearby second target; dial its availability by changing that spacing or frequency.

rules.statement: After a creature hits you, you gain +4 AC against its later attacks for the rest of that turn. Alternatively, when an attacker you can see hits you, you may use your reaction to halve that attack’s damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Defensive Tactics; Uncanny Dodge (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the defense lasts only through the attacker’s turn or reduces one hit, with a reaction cost for the latter; the reason is rapid but limited defense.

rules.statement: When a creature misses you with a melee attack, you may use your reaction to make it repeat that attack against a different creature of your choice, other than itself.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Superior Hunter’s Defense — Stand Against the Tide (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: redirection requires a miss and consumes a reaction; the cost is the narrow opening created by the attacker’s failure.

rules.statement: When an effect allows a Dexterity save for half damage, you take no damage on a success and half damage on a failure. If you can hear, you also know the location of hidden or invisible creatures within 10 feet.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Evasion; Blindsense (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: improved avoidance applies only to qualifying area effects, while nearby detection requires hearing and is limited to 10 feet.

rules.statement: A bonded beast must be Medium or smaller and have challenge rating 1/4 or lower; it adds your proficiency bonus to its AC, attacks, damage, proficient saves, and proficient skills, and its hit-point maximum is at least four times your ranger level. It acts on your initiative, moves when directed without an action cost, but needs your action to take most commanded actions; after its death, you can bond a replacement over 8 hours with a nonhostile beast.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Beast Master — Ranger’s Companion (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one limited-size, low-rank companion is tied to the ranger and depends on commands; replacement costs eight hours of bonding.

rules.statement: A companion that does not attack can be commanded with a bonus action to Dash, Disengage, Dodge, or Help. At 11th level it can make two attacks when commanded to Attack, and at 15th level it can share a spell that targets its ranger if within 30 feet.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Beast Master — Exceptional Training; Bestial Fury; Share Spells (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: command options and spell sharing are restricted by the companion’s activity, level, target, and 30-foot proximity.

rules.statement: Once per turn, an attack using a finesse or ranged weapon deals an extra 1d6 damage if you have advantage, or if another non-incapacitated enemy of the target is within 5 feet and you lack disadvantage. The extra damage increases with rogue level, reaching 10d6 at level 19.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Sneak Attack; Rogue table (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: bonus damage needs a qualifying weapon and opening, is limited to once per turn, and scales with training.

rules.statement: At 20th level, you may turn a missed attack against a target in range into a hit, or treat a failed ability-check die roll as 20; after using this, you must finish a short or long rest to use it again.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Stroke of Luck (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a near-certain success is a single-use resource recovered only through rest.

rules.statement: A spellcaster with this innate casting system regains expended slots on a long rest and can exchange sorcery points for one slot as a bonus action, up to 5th level, using costs of 2, 3, 5, 6, or 7 points for slots of levels 1 through 5. As a bonus action, the caster can instead expend a slot to gain points equal to its level; the point reserve cannot exceed the class-level limit.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Sorcerer — Font of Magic (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: power is converted between a capped point reserve and slots, with higher-level slots costing more and normal recovery requiring a long rest.

rules.statement: When casting, the sorcerer can spend points to modify a spell: 1 point can protect a number of chosen save-targets up to Charisma modifier, double range, make touch range 30 feet, reroll up to that many damage dice, double a duration of at least 1 minute up to 24 hours, or remove verbal and somatic components. Other options cost 3 points to impose disadvantage on one target’s first save, 2 points to change a 1-action casting to a bonus action, or points equal to spell level (1 for a cantrip) to add a second target to a spell that targets only one creature and is not self-range; normally only one such modification applies per spell.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Metamagic (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: defined alterations spend a limited point reserve, and generally only one alteration may shape each casting.

rules.statement: After casting a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, the game master may trigger a wild surge: on a d20 result of 1, a random effect occurs. A luck feature grants advantage on one attack, check, or save, then recharges on a long rest; before it recharges, the game master may trigger a surge after a qualifying spell, which restores that feature.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Wild Magic — Wild Magic Surge; Tides of Chaos (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: unpredictable effects are contingent on the game master and a low-probability roll; using the luck benefit risks triggering a surge but can restore it.

rules.statement: A spell cast on a creature while the caster is hidden gives that creature disadvantage on its saves against the spell that turn. When a spell targets or includes the trickster, the trickster may use a reaction to contest it; on the target’s failed save, the spell has no effect on the trickster and the trickster learns it for 8 hours if it is at least 1st level and castable with available slots, while its caster cannot cast it for those 8 hours; this can be used once per long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Arcane Trickster — Magical Ambush; Spell Thief (dnd5e-phb-2014#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the first effect depends on being hidden, while spell theft requires a reaction and failed save, has an 8-hour limit, and recharges after a long rest.

rules.statement: A warlock can cast a known spell of 1st level or higher by spending one of their spell slots; all their slots are the same level, and all spent slots return after a short or long rest. When a slot is higher level than the spell, the spell is cast at the slot’s level.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Pact Magic, p. 108 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: slots limit output; dial: slot level and rest cadence; the warlock’s borrowed magic replenishes through rest.

rules.statement: At 3rd level, a warlock chooses one boon. The familiar boon grants a familiar and lets the warlock trade one attack from their Attack action for one of its attacks; the weapon boon creates a proficient magical melee weapon, which vanishes if more than 5 feet away for at least 1 minute, if recreated, dismissed, or if the warlock dies. The book boon grants three chosen cantrips usable at will while the book is carried; a lost book can be replaced by a 1-hour ceremony that destroys the previous one, and the book turns to ash when the warlock dies.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Pact Boon, pp. 108–109 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one boon limits the grant; dial: the boon’s form and persistence; the patron’s gift remains tied to the warlock and its pact.

rules.statement: A warlock can bind a magic weapon to their pact through a 1-hour ritual, performed during a short rest. The weapon can then be dismissed into an extradimensional space and appears when the warlock creates their pact weapon; artifacts and sentient weapons cannot be bound, and death or another binding ritual ends the bond, returning a stored weapon to the warlock’s feet.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Pact of the Blade, p. 109 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one bound weapon; dial: the ritual’s duration and eligible objects; a death or deliberate replacement breaks the connection.

rules.statement: At 20th level, a warlock can spend 1 minute appealing to their patron to restore all expended Pact Magic slots. After using this ability, they must finish a long rest before using it again.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Eldritch Master, p. 109 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one restoration per long rest; dial: the appeal’s time and scope; replenishment depends on the patron’s aid.

rules.statement: A wizard starts with six 1st-level spells in a spellbook and adds two chosen wizard spells to it whenever they gain a wizard level, if the spells are of a level for which they have slots. They can also copy a found wizard spell of an eligible level into the book, taking 2 hours and spending 50 gp per spell level.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Spellbook; Learning Spells of 1st Level and Higher, pp. 115–116 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the spellbook holds learned formulas; dial: copying time and expense per level; acquiring another wizard’s knowledge takes practice and costly materials.

rules.statement: After a long rest, a wizard prepares a list of spells from their spellbook, numbering Intelligence modifier plus wizard level, with a minimum of one; each must be a level for which they have slots. They can change the list after another long rest, spending at least 1 minute per spell level for each prepared spell, and can cast a ritual-tagged spell from the book without preparing it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Preparing and Casting Spells; Ritual Casting, p. 115 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preparation is limited by intellect and level; dial: the daily list and study time; usable magic depends on memorized formulae.

rules.statement: A wizard regains expended spell slots after a long rest. Once per day after a short rest, they can recover slots whose combined levels total at most half their wizard level, rounded up; no recovered slot can be 6th level or higher.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Arcane Recovery, p. 116 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: recovery is capped by level and once daily; dial: the recovered slot mix; studying the spellbook restores only a limited reserve.

rules.statement: A warlock’s 1st-level fey presence affects creatures in a 10-foot cube from the warlock: each makes a Wisdom save against the warlock’s spell save DC, and those that fail are charmed or frightened, chosen by the warlock, until the end of the warlock’s next turn. Use requires an action, and it recharges after a short or long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: The Archfey: Fey Presence, p. 110 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a brief effect in a bounded area; dial: the chosen emotional state and recharge; the fey influence is temporary and takes focused effort.

rules.statement: At 6th level, a Fiend-pact warlock can add a d10 to an ability check or saving throw after seeing its initial roll but before its effects occur. The ability recharges after a short or long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: The Fiend: Dark One’s Own Luck, p. 110 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one adjustment between rests; dial: when to invoke it after seeing the roll; the warlock calls on the patron to turn fate.

rules.statement: At 14th level, a Great Old One warlock can touch an incapacitated humanoid to charm it until remove curse is cast, the charm is removed, or the warlock uses this feature again. The warlock can communicate telepathically with the target while they remain on the same plane.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: The Great Old One: Create Thrall, p. 111 (dnd5e-phb-2014#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one thrall at a time; dial: the release conditions and plane limit; the alien influence persists until dispelled or displaced.

rules.statement: When you cast an abjuration spell of 1st level or higher, you can create a ward on yourself until you finish a long rest. It has hit points equal to twice your wizard level plus your Intelligence modifier, absorbs damage you would take before you take it yourself, and regains hit points equal to twice the level of each qualifying abjuration spell you cast; you can create it only once per long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Arcane Ward, p. 116 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one personal ward, replenished through abjuration and limited to once per long rest; its hit-point pool determines how much damage it can absorb.

rules.statement: From 6th level, when a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage, you can use your reaction to have your ward absorb that damage instead. Any damage exceeding the ward's remaining hit points still affects that creature.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Projected Ward, p. 116 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: redirect one nearby creature’s damage into your existing ward; the ward’s finite capacity limits protection.

rules.statement: From 14th level, you have advantage on saving throws against spells and resistance to damage from spells.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Spell Resistance, p. 116 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell-based threats are harder to impose and deal reduced damage; this protection applies only against spells.

rules.statement: From 2nd level, you can use an action to create a visibly magical, nonmagical-form object in your hand or in a visible unoccupied space within 10 feet. It must be no larger than 3 feet on a side and weigh at most 10 pounds, and it vanishes after 1 hour, when you create another this way, or when it takes any damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Minor Conjuration, p. 116 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: create one small, familiar object temporarily; size, weight, visibility, and fragility bound its utility.

rules.statement: From 6th level, you can use an action to teleport up to 30 feet to a visible unoccupied space, or swap places with a willing Small or Medium creature in a visible space within range. After using this ability, you cannot use it again until a long rest or until you cast a conjuration spell of 1st level or higher.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Benign Transposition, p. 116 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: short-range relocation, limited by visibility, destination occupancy, target consent, and a rest or spell-based recharge.

rules.statement: From 2nd level, after a long rest you record two d20 results. Before a roll, you may substitute one recorded result for an attack roll, saving throw, or ability check made by you or a creature you can see; each result is usable once, no more than once per turn, and unused results vanish at your next long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Portent, p. 117 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limited foreknowledge lets you set a roll’s result in advance; the small daily reserve and timing requirement constrain use.

rules.statement: From 6th level, when you cast a divination spell of 2nd level or higher using a spell slot, you regain one expended spell slot lower in level than the spell cast, but no higher than 5th level.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Expert Divination, p. 117 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: divination partly refunds casting effort, but only a lower-level slot is restored and the replacement cannot exceed 5th level.

rules.statement: From 2nd level, as an action you can try to charm a creature you can see within 5 feet if it can see or hear you; on a failed Wisdom save it is charmed, incapacitated, visibly dazed, and has speed 0 until the end of your next turn. You can spend later actions to extend the effect one turn at a time, but it ends if you move more than 5 feet away, the target can neither see nor hear you, or it takes damage; after it ends or the target succeeds initially, you cannot use this on it again until a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Hypnotic Gaze, p. 117 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: close-range, attention-dependent control lasts briefly and requires repeated actions; damage or separation breaks it.

rules.statement: From 10th level, when you cast an enchantment spell of 1st level or higher that targets only one creature, you may have it target a second creature as well.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Split Enchantment, p. 117 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: expand a single-target enchantment to two targets, with the spell’s own level and targeting rules still limiting the effect.

rules.statement: From 14th level, when you cast an enchantment spell that charms one or more creatures, you can make one affected creature unaware that it was charmed. Once before the spell ends, you may use an action to make that creature forget up to a number of hours equal to 1 plus your Charisma modifier, minimum 1, but never more than the spell’s duration; an Intelligence save prevents the memory loss.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Alter Memories, p. 117 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: conceal a charm and attempt limited memory removal, bounded by spell duration and resisted by an Intelligence save.

rules.statement: From 14th level, when you cast a damaging wizard spell of 5th level or lower, you can deal maximum damage. The first use after a long rest has no adverse effect; each further use before that rest deals immediate necrotic damage of 2d12 per spell level, increasing by 1d12 per spell level for every additional use, and this damage ignores resistance and immunity.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Overchannel, p. 118 (dnd5e-phb-2014#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: maximize a qualifying spell’s damage, with escalating unavoidable bodily harm for repeated use before resting.

rules.statement: You can call in a favor to get yourself and your companions free passage on a sailing ship, but the route and timing are not guaranteed; the group is expected to help the crew during the voyage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Sailor: Feature—Ship’s Passage (p. 39) (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: passage is available through a real relationship; dial: the crew’s needs and the ship’s route limit the favor; in-world cost: travelers work during the voyage.

rules.statement: Soldiers who recognize your rank defer to you if they hold a lower rank. You can use that standing to influence other soldiers, borrow simple equipment or horses temporarily, and usually enter friendly encampments and fortresses.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Soldier: Feature—Military Rank (p. 141) (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: rank carries weight among members of the former organization; dial: recognition and access depend on affiliation and standing; in-world limit: borrowed goods are for temporary use.

rules.statement: When not in combat, you and companions you lead can travel between any two city locations in half the time your speed would ordinarily require, by using routes others miss.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Urchin: Feature—City Secrets (p. 142) (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the benefit works within a city outside combat; dial: it applies only to urban travel and companions being led; in-world reason: knowledge of hidden passages and routes.

rules.statement: Armor grants its listed base protection; light armor adds the wearer’s Dexterity modifier, medium armor adds up to +2, and heavy armor adds none. A shield adds 2 to Armor Class, and only one shield can provide this benefit at a time.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Armor and Shields (pp. 145–146) (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: protection follows armor category and listed values; dial: Dexterity contribution varies by category; in-world limit: a shield must be wielded in one hand and only one counts.

rules.statement: Wearing armor without proficiency imposes disadvantage on Strength or Dexterity checks, saving throws, and attack rolls that involve either ability, and prevents spellcasting. Some heavy armor reduces speed by 10 feet unless the wearer meets its Strength requirement; armor marked as stealth-disadvantaging imposes disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Armor and Shields (p. 145) (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: armor’s restrictions apply while it is worn; dial: penalties depend on proficiency, Strength, and the armor’s listed properties; in-world reason: unfamiliarity, bulk, or noise hampers the wearer.

rules.statement: Armor provides its protection only if it is donned for the full time: 1 minute for light, 5 minutes for medium, or 10 minutes for heavy armor. Removing it takes 1 minute for light or medium armor and 5 minutes for heavy armor; help halves removal time. A shield takes one action to put on or remove.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Getting Into and Out of Armor (p. 147) (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the listed times govern wearing and removal; dial: help speeds only removal; in-world reason: armor takes time to fit, fasten, and unfasten.

rules.statement: An attack with an ammunition weapon expends one piece of ammunition; after battle, spending 1 minute searching recovers half the pieces expended. A loading weapon can fire only one piece of ammunition when used for an action, bonus action, or reaction, regardless of how many attacks are normally available.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Weapon Properties (pp. 147–148) (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each ammunition attack consumes one piece, and loading caps each listed action at one shot; dial: half the spent ammunition can be recovered by searching; in-world reason: ammunition is used up, lost, or damaged.

rules.statement: A creature Large or smaller hit by a net is restrained, unless it is formless; Huge or larger creatures are unaffected. The target or an adjacent creature can use an action to free it with a successful DC 10 Strength check, or 5 slashing damage to the net (AC 10) frees the target and destroys the net.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Special Weapons—Net (p. 148) (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a successful hit restrains eligible targets; dial: size and form limit which creatures are affected; in-world cost: escape takes an action and a check, or damages the net.

rules.statement: A creature hit by alchemist’s fire takes 1d4 fire damage at the start of each of its turns until it uses an action to succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity check to extinguish the flames.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Adventuring Gear—Alchemist’s Fire (pp. 148–152) (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the damage repeats at the start of each turn; dial: the target can end it with an action and a successful check; in-world reason: the burning fluid adheres until put out.

rules.statement: A creature that drinks antitoxin has advantage on saving throws against poison for 1 hour; undead and constructs gain no benefit.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Adventuring Gear—Antitoxin (p. 152) (dnd5e-phb-2014#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the benefit lasts 1 hour after drinking; dial: it protects only against poison saves and excludes undead and constructs; in-world limit: the substance does not help those creature types.

rules.statement: A flask of oil spread over a level 5-foot-square burns for 2 rounds when lit, dealing 5 fire damage to a creature that enters the square or ends its turn there; a creature can take this damage only once per turn.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Equipment, p. 153 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the hazard is limited to one small square and two rounds; dial its damage or duration to change the danger of crossing it.

rules.statement: Applying a vial of basic poison to one slashing or piercing weapon, or up to three pieces of ammunition, takes an action. For 1 minute, a hit requires the target to succeed on a DC 10 Constitution save or take 1d4 poison damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Equipment, p. 153 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one dose coats only a small number of weapons and dries after 1 minute; change coverage or potency to tune the consumable's value.

rules.statement: Drinking or administering a healing potion takes an action and restores 2d4 + 2 hit points.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Equipment, p. 153 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the potion is consumed for a fixed, limited recovery; adjust the healing amount or action cost to tune access to recovery.

rules.statement: Proficiency with a tool adds the character's proficiency bonus to ability checks made using it, for tasks within that tool's use; some tools, such as an herbalism kit, also have specific tasks that require proficiency.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Tools, p. 155 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: training improves relevant checks rather than granting automatic success; change which tasks require proficiency to tune who can perform specialized work.

rules.statement: When multiple animals pull one vehicle, their carrying capacities combine; the vehicle and its load can weigh up to five times the combined base carrying capacity of the animals pulling it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Mounts and Vehicles, p. 156 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: capacity scales with the pullers but is capped at five times their combined base capacity; change the multiplier to tune transport limits.

rules.statement: When you gain a level in another class, you must meet the ability-score prerequisites for both your current class and the new class; character level is the sum of levels across all classes.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Multiclassing, p. 164 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: minimum scores gate entry into a new class, while total character level still advances; alter prerequisites to make cross-training easier or harder.

rules.statement: With spellcasting features from multiple classes, determine spells known or prepared separately for each class, but calculate spell slots from the combined class levels using the multiclass slot table. Higher-level slots can cast lower-level spells, but do not grant knowledge of higher-level spells.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Multiclassing: Spellcasting, pp. 165–166 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: slot capacity combines while spell access stays class-specific; change either limit to tune versatility without granting broader spell knowledge.

rules.statement: Gaining Channel Divinity from another class grants that class's effects but does not add another use; additional uses come only from class levels that explicitly grant them. Each use can choose among the effects available from the character's classes.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Multiclassing: Channel Divinity, p. 165 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: class features broaden the available effects but do not multiply uses; granting extra uses would increase the power's frequency.

rules.statement: If a character gains Extra Attack from more than one class, the features do not stack; this feature permits no more than two attacks unless its own description explicitly allows more.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Multiclassing: Extra Attack, p. 165 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: duplicate sources do not increase the attack limit; allow stacking only if the intended combat output should rise.

rules.statement: A character with the Elemental Adept feat chooses acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder: their spells ignore resistance to that type, and damage dice for those spells treat a 1 as a 2. The feat can be taken more than once, with a different type chosen each time.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Feats: Elemental Adept, p. 167 (dnd5e-phb-2014#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the benefit applies only to one chosen damage type and to spells; allowing more types broadens the protection bypass.

rules.statement: A character with inexplicable luck has 3 points, spending 1 after a d20 roll but before its outcome is known to roll another d20 and choose which result applies. A point can also be spent when attacked to roll a d20 and choose whether the attack uses the attacker’s roll or that roll; opposing spends cancel, and all spent points return after a long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Lucky, p. 168 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: 3 points per long rest; dial the pool or recovery interval to change how often luck can intervene.

rules.statement: When a creature within 5 feet casts a spell, a trained fighter can use a reaction to make a melee weapon attack against it. Damage to a creature concentrating on a spell gives it disadvantage on the save to maintain concentration, and the fighter has advantage on saves against spells cast by creatures within 5 feet.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Mage Slayer, p. 168 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reactions and close range limit the counterattack; the concentration penalty and save benefit apply only in specified situations.

rules.statement: A character learns two cantrips and one 1st-level spell from a chosen class’s list, and can cast that spell at its lowest level once before needing a long rest to cast it again. The chosen class determines the spellcasting ability.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Magic Initiate, p. 168 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one leveled casting per long rest; dial the spell level or recharge to alter the grant’s strength.

rules.statement: A trained combatant learns two special maneuvers, fueled by a superiority die; without an existing pool, the character has one d6 die. The die is spent when a maneuver is used and regained after a short or long rest; maneuver save DC is 8 plus proficiency bonus plus the chosen Strength or Dexterity modifier.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Martial Adept, p. 168 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one die if no pool exists, with rest-based recovery; the die limits maneuver use.

rules.statement: A mounted combatant has advantage on melee attacks against unmounted creatures smaller than the mount, can redirect an attack aimed at the mount to themself, and improves the mount’s damage outcome on a successful Dexterity save from half damage to none. These benefits require being mounted and not incapacitated.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Mounted Combatant, p. 168 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: benefits depend on the mount being present and the rider able to act; the mount relationship enables protection and coordinated offense.

rules.statement: A character can make a cipher that others cannot decipher unless taught, they succeed on an Intelligence check against a DC equal to the creator’s Intelligence score plus proficiency bonus, or they use magic to decipher it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Linguist, p. 168 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the cipher resists ordinary reading but can be taught, overcome by a set check, or bypassed with magic.

rules.statement: A character can spend a reaction to cast a spell instead of making an opportunity attack when a hostile creature’s movement provokes one. The spell must take 1 action to cast and target only that creature.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: War Caster, p. 171 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the reaction replaces the opportunity attack and is limited to an action-time spell against the provoking creature.

rules.statement: When a creature hides, its Dexterity (Stealth) check is contested by the Wisdom (Perception) check of anyone actively searching, and is also compared against passive Perception for creatures not searching. It cannot hide from a creature that can see it, and making noise reveals its position.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Hiding, p. 178 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: concealment ends upon discovery or stopping, and sight or noise can prevent it.

rules.statement: A passive check equals 10 plus the modifiers normally used for the check; advantage adds 5 and disadvantage subtracts 5. This provides a score without rolling, including for repeated tasks or checks the DM wants to resolve secretly.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Passive Checks, p. 176 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: fixed scores replace rolls for passive or secret resolution; advantage and disadvantage shift the score by 5.

rules.statement: In a group ability check, every participant rolls, and the whole group succeeds if at least half succeed; otherwise the group fails.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Group Checks, p. 176 (dnd5e-phb-2014#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: success requires at least half the group; dial the threshold to change how collective competence or weakness affects the result.

rules.statement: Overland travel has three paces: fast covers 400 feet per minute, 4 miles per hour, or 30 miles per day and imposes a −5 penalty on passive Perception; normal covers 300 feet, 3 miles, or 24 miles; slow covers 200 feet, 2 miles, or 18 miles and permits stealth. The daily distances assume 8 hours of travel.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Travel Pace, p. 181 (dnd5e-phb-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: set travel distance and alertness trade-offs; dial: pace; in-world reason: hurried travel reduces attention, while deliberate movement allows concealment.

rules.statement: For each travel hour beyond 8 in a day, a traveler covers the pace's hourly distance and makes a Constitution save at the hour's end, starting at DC 10 and increasing by 1 for every additional hour past the eighth. Failure adds one exhaustion level.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Travel Pace — Forced March, p. 181 (dnd5e-phb-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: extra travel risks accumulating exhaustion; dial: hours beyond eight; in-world reason: continued exertion wears the traveler down.

rules.statement: Difficult terrain halves movement: each foot traveled costs 2 feet of speed. Climbing or swimming also costs 1 extra foot per foot, or 2 extra feet per foot in difficult terrain, unless the creature has the matching movement speed.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Difficult Terrain; Climbing, Swimming, and Crawling, p. 181 (dnd5e-phb-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: terrain and movement mode reduce travel; dial: movement cost; in-world reason: obstacles and exertion slow progress.

rules.statement: A fast-moving group takes a −5 penalty to passive Perception when noticing hidden threats; characters occupied with other travel tasks do not contribute their passive scores to the group's detection. A slow-moving group can attempt stealth if it is not in the open.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Activity While Traveling, pp. 182–184 (dnd5e-phb-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: travel choices trade alertness against stealth or other work; dial: pace and attention; in-world reason: travelers cannot focus equally on every task.

rules.statement: At the end of a fall, a creature takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet fallen, up to 20d6, and lands prone unless it avoids fall damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: The Environment — Falling, p. 184 (dnd5e-phb-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: falling causes escalating harm and a loss of footing; dial: height, capped at 20d6; in-world reason: impact grows with the distance fallen.

rules.statement: A creature can hold its breath for minutes equal to 1 + its Constitution modifier, with a minimum of 30 seconds. Once it runs out of breath, it survives for rounds equal to its Constitution modifier, minimum 1; at the start of the next turn it drops to 0 hit points and is dying.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: The Environment — Suffocating, p. 184 (dnd5e-phb-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: lack of breathable air progresses to collapse; dial: Constitution-based time; in-world reason: endurance and remaining air run out.

rules.statement: A character needs 1 pound of food daily and can stretch supplies by eating half rations, which counts as half a day without food. After days without food equal to 3 + Constitution modifier, minimum 1, each further day adds one exhaustion level; a full day's eating resets the count.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Food and Water — Food, p. 186 (dnd5e-phb-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: prolonged hunger accumulates exhaustion; dial: Constitution and ration size; in-world reason: inadequate nourishment weakens the body.

rules.statement: A character needs 1 gallon of water daily, or 2 gallons in hot weather. Drinking half the required amount calls for a DC 15 Constitution save or adds one exhaustion level at day's end; drinking less than half automatically adds one. If already exhausted, either case adds two levels instead.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Food and Water — Water, p. 186 (dnd5e-phb-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: insufficient water worsens exhaustion; dial: climate, amount, and existing exhaustion; in-world reason: dehydration compounds physical strain.

rules.statement: A short rest lasts at least 1 hour; at its end a character may spend Hit Dice, up to their available total, rolling each and adding Constitution modifier to regain that many hit points. A long rest lasts at least 8 hours, and an interruption by at least 1 hour of strenuous activity requires restarting it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Resting, p. 187 (dnd5e-phb-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: rest restores hit points through spent reserves, while strenuous interruption cancels long-rest progress; dial: rest duration and Hit Dice; in-world reason: recovery requires time and quiet.

rules.statement: At the end of a long rest, a character regains all lost hit points and spent Hit Dice up to half their total. A character can benefit from only one long rest in 24 hours and must have at least 1 hit point when it begins.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Resting — Long Rest, p. 187 (dnd5e-phb-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: extended rest restores health and part of the spent reserve; dial: once per 24 hours and half the Hit Dice; in-world reason: recovery has limits and requires surviving until rest begins.

rules.statement: In combat, a turn allows movement up to speed and one action; a qualifying feature may grant one bonus action, and a reaction can be taken only once before the start of the creature's next turn.
