A turn may include one free object interaction, while a second generally costs the action.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Your Turn; Bonus Actions; Reactions; Other Activity on Your Turn, pp. 190–191 (dnd5e-phb-2014#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: cap actions and object handling per turn; dial: special features can grant a bonus action; in-world reason: combatants have limited time to act.

rules.statement: A caster can use a spell only if it is fixed in mind or available through a magic item, and casting usually spends a slot of that spell’s level or higher. A long rest restores spent slots; a spell cast with a higher-level slot takes on that level, and may gain extra effects if its description says so.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 10: Spellcasting — Spell Slots (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: finite casting output; dial: how many slots return after a rest; the caster is taxed by channeling magical energy.

rules.statement: A cantrip is a level 0 spell that can be cast at will without a slot or advance preparation. A qualifying ritual takes 10 minutes longer than normal, uses no slot, and cannot be cast at a higher level; the caster must have access to the spell and a feature that permits ritual casting.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Chapter 10: Spellcasting — Cantrips; Rituals (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: repeated minor effects and slower slot-free rituals; dial: which spells qualify; practice or preparation limits access.

rules.statement: A readied spell must normally take 1 action to cast; the caster casts it first, holds its energy, then releases it as a reaction when a chosen perceivable trigger occurs. Holding it requires concentration, and if concentration breaks, the spell dissipates without taking effect.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Page 194 — Ready (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: delayed release tied to a trigger; dial: eligible spells and trigger conditions; interruption can waste the held magic.

rules.statement: A spell that requires concentration ends if the caster begins concentrating on another spell, takes damage and fails the required Constitution save, becomes incapacitated, or dies. The caster may also end concentration at any time without using an action.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Pages 203–204 — Duration; Concentration (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one concentration effect at a time; dial: the damage-save threshold and environmental hazards; keeping magic active demands focus.

rules.statement: A spell can affect only a target within its range and normally requires a clear path; total cover blocks direct targeting. For an area spell, blocked straight lines from its origin exclude locations from the effect, and its specified shape and dimensions determine the area.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Pages 203–206 — Range; Targets; Areas of Effect (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: range, cover, and the spell’s geometry constrain reach; dial: the area’s shape and size; obstacles shield locations.

rules.statement: A target may make the saving throw named by a spell to avoid some or all of its effect, with success and failure outcomes set by that spell. The save difficulty is 8 plus the caster’s spellcasting ability modifier, proficiency bonus, and any special modifiers.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Page 206 — Saving Throws (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a target gets a resistance chance; dial: spell difficulty and success outcome; the target’s ability helps resist the effect.

rules.statement: Effects from different spells add together while their durations overlap, but repeated castings of the same spell do not combine; only the strongest effect, such as the highest bonus, applies.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Page 206 — Combining Magical Effects (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: distinct spells can accumulate but duplicate castings cannot; dial: how potency is compared; overlapping magic does not multiply its own benefit.

rules.statement: A successful grapple binds a target no more than one size larger than the grappler, using a free hand and a contested Strength check against the target’s Strength or Dexterity. The target can spend an action to contest an escape, the grappler may release it freely, and dragging it halves the grappler’s speed unless it is at least two sizes smaller.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Pages 195–197 — Grappling (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a successful contest restrains a size-limited target; dial: escape and movement costs; holding someone occupies a hand and slows movement.

rules.statement: Damage resistance halves damage of its type, while vulnerability doubles it; apply these after other damage modifiers, and multiple instances of either do not stack. Healing adds hit points up to the target’s maximum, and excess healing is lost.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Pages 197–198 — Damage Resistance and Vulnerability; Healing (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: damage traits halve or double harm and healing cannot exceed the maximum; dial: which damage types are affected; protection and recovery are bounded.

rules.statement: When a creature starts its turn at 0 hit points, it makes a death save: 10 or higher succeeds, and three successes stabilize it while three failures kill it; a 1 counts as two failures and a 20 restores 1 hit point. Damage at 0 causes a failure, or two for a critical hit, and damage at least equal to the hit point maximum kills outright; stable creatures remain unconscious and recover 1 hit point after 1d4 hours if not healed.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Pages 198–199 — Death Saving Throws; Stabilizing a Creature (dnd5e-phb-2014#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: death is tracked through accumulated successes and failures; dial: recovery and damage thresholds; aid or time can avert death, but further harm worsens the danger.

rules.statement: If two castings of the same spell affect one target during overlapping durations, the target receives the benefit only once; for example, overlapping castings of bless do not grant a second bonus die.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Spellcasting rules, page 207 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: duplicate effects do not stack, so repeating a spell cannot multiply its benefit.

rules.statement: Mortals access raw magic through an interface; where that interface is torn, magic may fail or behave unpredictably. Arcane casters access it through learned or intuitive understanding, while divine casters’ access is mediated by divine power, nature, or an oath.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: The Weave of Magic, page 207 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: magic requires a functioning interface, with distinct routes of access tied to the source of the caster’s power.

rules.statement: A creature affected by antipathy or sympathy toward a chosen target must resist when it sees the target or comes within 60 feet. Antipathy drives it toward the nearest safe place out of sight; sympathy makes it move toward and remain near the target. It can retry after a turn spent away from the target and every 24 hours; success ends the effect, and a successful initial resistance grants immunity for 1 minute.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Antipathy/Sympathy, page 215 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: the effect lasts 10 days but allows repeated resistance; the target’s behavior is compelled by a strong attraction or aversion.

rules.statement: An arcane lock secures a touched closed entryway until dispelled. Designated creatures can open it normally, a spoken password within 5 feet suppresses it for 1 minute, and knock suppresses it for 10 minutes; breaking or picking the locked object is 10 points harder.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Arcane Lock, page 214 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: access is limited by designation or password, with force and lockpicking made harder rather than impossible.

rules.statement: An antimagic field moves with its caster as a 10-foot-radius sphere for up to 1 hour with concentration. Within it, spells and other magical effects are suppressed, magic items become mundane, magical travel fails, and magically summoned or created creatures and objects disappear temporarily; suppressed durations continue to run, and artifacts and deities’ effects are exceptions.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Antimagic Field, pages 213–214 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: the field suppresses most magic in a limited moving area, but consumes the caster’s concentration and does not stop exceptional divine or artifact effects.

rules.statement: A creature that fails to resist animal friendship is charmed for 24 hours. The spell works only on a beast with Intelligence below 4, and the charm ends if the caster or an ally harms it; higher-level slots affect one additional beast per slot level above 1st.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Animal Friendship, page 213 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control is limited to low-intelligence beasts, lasts a day, and ends when the caster’s side harms the target.

rules.statement: Animate dead raises a Small or Medium humanoid corpse as a zombie or a pile of bones as a skeleton. The caster can command creatures made by the spell within 60 feet; control lasts 24 hours unless the caster recasts before it ends, which can reassert control over up to four such creatures. Each slot level above 3rd adds two creatures animated or brought back under control.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Animate Dead, page 213 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: the servant requires a suitable body and recurring recasting to maintain control.

rules.statement: Alter self lasts up to 1 hour with concentration and offers aquatic adaptation, appearance change, or natural weapons. The caster can switch options as an action; appearance changes preserve basic body shape and size, while the weapon option grants proficient magical unarmed strikes dealing 1d6 damage and a +1 attack and damage bonus.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Alter Self, pages 211–212 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: bodily changes are temporary and constrained by the chosen option; appearance changes cannot alter size or basic shape.

rules.statement: Astral projection sends the caster and up to eight willing nearby creatures’ astral bodies to the Astral Plane, leaving their physical bodies unconscious and suspended. A silver cord links each astral form to its body; if cut by an effect that can cut it, the creature dies, while ending the spell or reducing either body to 0 hit points returns the astral form if its cord remains intact.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Astral Projection, page 215 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: travel is separated from the physical body but depends on a vulnerable tether and costly consumed materials for each participant.

rules.statement: Arcane gate creates two linked 10-foot portals at visible ground points, one within 10 feet and the other within 500 feet; they last up to 10 minutes with concentration. Creatures and objects entering the active side of either portal exit from the other, and the caster can rotate their active sides as a bonus action.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Arcane Gate, page 214 (dnd5e-phb-2014#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: the passage is a paired, visible-position gateway with limited range and duration, maintained by concentration.

rules.statement: A mature duplicate takes 120 days to grow in a sealed vessel and lasts indefinitely if undisturbed. When the original dies, its willing, unbound soul can transfer into the duplicate, which has the original’s body, memories, personality, and abilities but none of its equipment; the original remains cannot then be restored to life.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: CLONE, p. 222 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one prepared duplicate and a willing, free soul; dial: 120-day growth and costly vessel; the soul’s transfer leaves the original remains inert.

rules.statement: If concentration on the summoned elemental breaks, the caster loses control rather than ending the summon: the elemental becomes hostile and cannot be dismissed by the caster, then vanishes after 1 hour. While controlled, it follows verbal commands that do not conflict with its alignment.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: CONJURE ELEMENTAL, pp. 225–226 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control lasts while concentration holds; dial: a break risks hostility for up to an hour, reflecting the danger of calling a servant.

rules.statement: After a successful hit, the inflicted disease requires three failed Constitution saves for its effects to persist for the spell’s 7-day duration, or three successful saves for recovery and the spell to end. The chosen disease sets the consequences, which include impaired abilities, blindness, vulnerability to damage, or damage-triggered stunning.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: CONTAGION, p. 228 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: three successes cure and three failures lock in the illness; dial: seven days of possible effects; disease-removing effects can still help.

rules.statement: The caster can prepare one spell of 5th level or lower, with a 1-action casting time and the caster as its target, to trigger on a circumstance specified in advance. It takes effect immediately the first time that circumstance occurs, whether wanted or not, and the preparation ends; only one can be held at a time, and losing its material component also ends it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: CONTINGENCY, p. 229 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one spell and one trigger; dial: up to 10 days of readiness; the stored effect consumes resources and may fire at an inconvenient moment.

rules.statement: A 30-foot-radius moving field gives the caster and friendly creatures in it advantage on saves against spells and magical effects. If a protected creature succeeds on a save that would halve such an effect’s damage, it instead takes none.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: CIRCLE OF POWER, p. 222 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a 30-foot field centered on the caster; dial: concentration for up to 10 minutes; protection is limited to allies inside it.

rules.statement: A successful save against a group emotion-suppression effect avoids its influence, and a target may choose to fail. The caster can instead make a failed target indifferent toward selected creatures it was hostile to; harm to it or witnessed harm to its friends ends that indifference, and hostility can return when the spell ends.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: CALM EMOTIONS, p. 220 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: concentration for up to 1 minute; dial: targets can resist or consent to the effect; witnessed harm can break the imposed indifference.

rules.statement: The caster can move chosen freestanding water within a cube up to 100 feet on each side into a raised flood, a trench, a redirected flow, or a whirlpool. The whirlpool requires water at least 50 feet wide and 25 feet deep, pulls nearby creatures or objects 10 feet toward it, and can catch and damage creatures that fail its save.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: CONTROL WATER, pp. 227–228 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one selected water effect at a time; dial: concentration for up to 10 minutes; the whirlpool needs a sufficiently large body of water.

rules.statement: A blade wall can be a straight barrier up to 100 feet long or a ring up to 60 feet across, and either form is 20 feet high and 5 feet thick. Its space is difficult terrain; a creature entering it for the first time on a turn or starting there saves against 6d10 slashing damage, taking half on a success.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: BLADE BARRIER, p. 219 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a fixed wall that lasts while concentration holds, up to 10 minutes; dial: its dimensions cap coverage; crossing it risks damage.

rules.statement: At the end of each of the caster’s turns during the 1-minute spell, a roll of 11 or higher sends the caster to the Ethereal Plane until the start of the next turn. The caster then returns to a visible unoccupied space within 10 feet of the departure point, or to a nearest available space if needed; the spell can also be dismissed as an action.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: BLINK, p. 220 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each end-of-turn roll gives a 50% chance to shift planes; dial: separation lasts only until the next turn; destination space must be available.

rules.statement: A summoned group of beasts, elementals, or fey is friendly and follows verbal commands without requiring an action from the caster; without commands, it only defends itself. If the summoning effect ends or the creatures reach 0 hit points, they disappear; some single-creature summons instead become hostile when concentration breaks and remain for up to an hour.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: CONJURE ANIMALS, pp. 224–225; CONJURE ELEMENTAL, pp. 225–226 (dnd5e-phb-2014#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: summons obey simple verbal direction and otherwise self-defend; dial: concentration and duration constrain service; a broken elemental binding can turn hostile.

rules.statement: You can interrupt a creature you can see casting a spell within 60 feet: a spell of 3rd level or lower fails automatically; for a 4th-level or higher spell, a successful spellcasting-ability check against DC 10 plus its level makes it fail. Using a slot at least as high as the interrupted spell makes it fail automatically.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Page 229, spell interruption entry (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by expending a higher-level slot; the caster spends greater stored power to reliably disrupt stronger magic.

rules.statement: Create up to 45 pounds of food and 30 gallons of clean water, enough for 15 humanoids or five steeds for 24 hours. The food spoils after 24 hours, while the water remains good.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Page 230, Create Food and Water (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; no scaling stated; nourishment is temporary because the food spoils.

rules.statement: Create or destroy up to 10 gallons of water in an open container, or create rain or remove fog in a 30-foot cube; created rain also extinguishes exposed flames. Each slot level above 1st adds 10 gallons or expands the cube by 5 feet.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Page 230, Create or Destroy Water (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by slot level; greater volume or area requires greater magical investment.

rules.statement: At night, turn up to three nearby corpses into ghouls, each costing a 150 gp black onyx stone plus specified ritual materials. They obey mental orders within 120 feet for 24 hours; recasting before that period ends renews control, and higher-level slots raise the number or allow stronger undead.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Page 230, Create Undead (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by slot level and costly corpse-bound materials; command is limited in time and range.

rules.statement: A creature charmed by you must spend its action before moving to attack a different creature you mentally select. You must use your action on later turns to maintain control, and the target can end the effect with a successful Wisdom save at the end of its turn.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Page 230, Crown of Madness (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; no scaling stated; control costs continuing attention and can be resisted each turn.

rules.statement: Create a nonliving object no larger than a 5-foot cube, using a material type you have seen before; the required small matter sample must match that type. The object lasts according to its material: vegetable matter 1 day, stone or crystal 12 hours, precious metals 1 hour, gems 10 minutes, and adamantine or mithral 1 minute; mixed materials use the shortest duration.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Page 230, Creation (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by material choice; rarer and more valuable substances persist for less time.

rules.statement: A touched weapon becomes magical for up to 1 hour of concentration, gaining +1 to attack rolls and +1d4 damage of a chosen elemental type. At 5th–6th-level slots the bonuses become +2 and 2d4, and at 7th level or higher they become +3 and 3d4.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Page 238, Elemental Weapon (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by slot level; stronger weapon enhancement requires higher-tier power and sustained concentration.

rules.statement: A creature or unattended object can be doubled in size and multiplied by eight in weight, or halved in size and reduced to one-eighth weight, for up to 1 minute of concentration. Growth improves Strength checks and saves and adds 1d4 weapon damage; reduction worsens them and subtracts 1d4 damage, to a minimum of 1.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Page 238, Enlarge/Reduce (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; no scaling stated; the change lasts only while concentration is maintained and unwilling targets can resist.

rules.statement: A creature in a 20-foot-square area of summoned plants can be restrained on a failed Strength save; it can use an action to escape with a successful Strength check against the caster’s save DC. The plants make the area difficult terrain and wither when the spell ends.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Page 239, Entangle (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; no scaling stated; restraint is confined to the area and can be broken through effort.

rules.statement: Enter the Border Ethereal for up to 8 hours, moving through objects and avoiding interaction with creatures and effects on the originating plane. When the effect ends, return at the current corresponding location; if it is occupied, move to the nearest free space and take force damage equal to twice the distance moved in feet.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Page 239, Etherealness (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by higher-level slots to include additional willing travelers; return can injure you if your destination is obstructed.

rules.statement: A touched object weighing no more than 10 pounds and measuring no more than 6 feet can be marked and linked to a sapphire worth 1,000 gp. Later, crush the sapphire while speaking the item’s name to bring it to your hand across any distance or plane; if someone else holds it, you instead learn that holder’s identity and rough location.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Page 236, Drawmij’s Instant Summons (dnd5e-phb-2014#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; no scaling stated; a costly linked sapphire is consumed, and a held item cannot be taken directly.

rules.statement: A healing effect restores 70 hit points to one visible creature within 60 feet and ends its blindness, deafness, and diseases; it cannot affect constructs or undead. Using a spell slot above 6th adds 10 hit points per slot level above 6th.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: HEAL (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: restoration is immediate and limited to one visible target; dial: higher slots add healing, while creature type excludes some targets.

rules.statement: A brief healing effect restores one visible creature within 60 feet for 1d4 plus the caster’s spellcasting modifier; it cannot affect undead or constructs. Each slot level above 1st adds another 1d4.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: HEALING WORD (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: low-cost rapid recovery is small and target-limited; dial: higher slots increase the amount restored.

rules.statement: A visible manufactured metal object within 60 feet becomes red-hot while concentration lasts, up to 1 minute. Contact deals 2d8 fire damage when cast, and the caster can spend a bonus action on later turns to repeat the damage; a creature holding or wearing it must pass a Constitution save or drop it, and if unable to drop it suffers disadvantage on attacks and ability checks until its next turn.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: HEAT METAL (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: repeated damage requires concentration and later bonus actions; dial: higher slots add 1d8 damage per level above 2nd.

rules.statement: A creature that damages the caster from within 60 feet can be targeted as a reaction; it makes a Dexterity save, taking 2d10 fire damage on failure or half on success. Each slot level above 1st adds 1d10 damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: HELLISH REBUKE (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: damage is a limited retaliatory response requiring a qualifying attack; dial: higher slots increase its damage.

rules.statement: Up to twelve creatures can eat a conjured feast over 1 hour; its benefits begin only after the meal and last 24 hours. Each eater is cured of diseases and poison, gains immunity to poison and fear, has advantage on Wisdom saves, and gains 2d10 hit points to both current and maximum hit points.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: HEROES' FEAST (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: powerful group benefits require a costly consumed vessel and a one-hour meal; dial: the feast's reach is capped at twelve creatures.

rules.statement: A willing touched creature becomes immune to fear and gains temporary hit points equal to the caster’s spellcasting modifier at the start of each turn, for up to 1 minute while concentration lasts. Any temporary hit points remaining from this effect disappear when it ends; each slot level above 1st adds one target.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: HEROISM (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: protection and recurring temporary vitality last only while concentration holds; dial: higher slots extend the effect to more willing targets.

rules.statement: A visible creature within 90 feet is cursed for up to 1 hour while concentration lasts: attacks against it deal an extra 1d6 necrotic damage, and checks using one ability chosen at casting have disadvantage. If it reaches 0 hit points, the caster can use a later bonus action to curse another creature; removing the curse ends the effect, and higher slots extend its duration to 8 hours or 24 hours.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: HEX (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the curse requires concentration and can be ended by curse removal; dial: higher slots extend duration, while a defeated target permits a bonus-action transfer.

rules.statement: A visible creature is paralyzed for up to 1 minute if it fails a Wisdom save; it can repeat the save at the end of each turn, ending the effect on a success. The creature must not be undead; each slot level above 5th adds one target, with targets within 30 feet of each other.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: HOLD MONSTER (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control is resistible and concentration-bound; dial: higher slots add nearby targets.

rules.statement: A humanoid visible within 60 feet is paralyzed for up to 1 minute after failing a Wisdom save, and can repeat the save at the end of each turn to end the effect. Higher slots add one humanoid target per level above 2nd, with targets within 30 feet of one another.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: HOLD PERSON (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the restraint has a humanoid-only target and repeat chances to escape; dial: higher slots add nearby targets.

rules.statement: A 30-foot-radius aura centered on the caster lasts up to 1 minute with concentration. Chosen creatures in it gain advantage on all saves and dim light; other creatures have disadvantage on attacks against them, and a fiend or undead that hits one with a melee attack must pass a Constitution save or be blinded for the effect’s duration.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: HOLY AURA (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: protection applies only to chosen creatures in the nearby aura and requires concentration; dial: the caster chooses recipients, while hostile creature types face an added blindness risk.

rules.statement: A 20-foot-radius sphere within 150 feet becomes a dark, cold void for up to 1 minute while concentration lasts. It blocks all light and blinds creatures fully inside; the area is difficult terrain, deals 2d6 cold damage to creatures starting their turn there, and forces creatures ending a turn there to save against 2d6 acid damage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: HUNGER OF HADAR (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the hazardous zone is stationary, bounded, and concentration-limited; dial: damage depends on where creatures are at turn boundaries.

rules.statement: A visible creature within 90 feet is marked for up to 1 hour with concentration; weapon hits against it deal an extra 1d6 damage, and the caster has advantage on checks to find it using Perception or Survival. If it reaches 0 hit points, the caster can mark another creature with a later bonus action; higher slots extend the duration to 8 or 24 hours.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: HUNTER'S MARK (dnd5e-phb-2014#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the mark improves pursuit and damage against one target while concentration lasts; dial: higher slots extend the duration, and a defeated target allows reassignment.

rules.statement: A 7th-level casting reshapes the apparent sound, smell, feel, and look of terrain in an area up to 1 mile square for 10 days, but preserves its general shape and does not affect creatures. The sensory changes can impede movement; pieces taken outside the area disappear, and true-sight reveals the real terrain while leaving the illusion physically interactive.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: MIRAGE, p. 260 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: terrain can be disguised and movement affected; dial: the area is capped at 1 mile square and the effect lasts 10 days because it is a sustained illusion.

rules.statement: A 4th-level ward protects a cube from 5 to 100 feet per side for 24 hours, with the caster choosing any combination of listed barriers to sound, sight, divination, teleportation, or planar travel. Recasting it daily at the same location for a year makes it permanent; each higher slot level increases the cube's side length by 100 feet.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: MORDENKAINEN'S PRIVATE SANCTUM, p. 263 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: selected forms of detection and travel are blocked; dial: the ward has a bounded area and usually expires after 24 hours, with permanence requiring a year of daily recasting.

rules.statement: A 7th-level casting creates a furnished extradimensional dwelling for 24 hours, with a floor plan of at most fifty 10-foot cubes and one chosen entrance. Designated creatures may enter while the portal is open; the caster can open or close it within 30 feet, and when the effect ends occupants are expelled to open spaces nearest the entrance.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: MORDENKAINEN'S MAGNIFICENT MANSION, pp. 262–263 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a private interior can be created and entered through one portal; dial: its capacity and 24-hour duration are limited, and occupants are expelled when it ends.

rules.statement: A failed Wisdom save lets the caster reshape one visible creature's memory of an event from the last 24 hours that lasted no more than 10 minutes. The caster must describe the change in an understood language while the target is incapacitated and unaware; damage or another spell ends the attempt, while a completed alteration takes hold when the spell ends and can be restored by remove curse or greater restoration. Higher slots extend the event's age limit to 7 days, 30 days, 1 year, or any time in the target's past at levels 6 through 9.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: MODIFY MEMORY, p. 262 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed save allows a specific memory to be changed; dial: the event's duration and age are limited, and interruption prevents the change from taking hold.

rules.statement: A 4th-level casting can enclose a Large-or-smaller creature or object in a force sphere for up to 1 minute with concentration; an unwilling creature can avoid it with a successful Dexterity save. Nothing passes through the sphere, it takes no damage, and occupants cannot affect things outside; an enclosed creature can roll it at up to half speed, while disintegrate destroys it without harming what is inside.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: OTILUKE'S RESILIENT SPHERE, p. 265 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the sphere isolates its occupant from outside effects; dial: it lasts at most 1 minute and can be ended by a specific destructive effect.

rules.statement: A 5th-level casting can bind a celestial, elemental, fey, or fiend that remains within range for the full hour-long casting; on a failed Charisma save it must follow instructions for 24 hours. Higher-level slots extend service to 10, 30, or 180 days, or a year and a day; the creature follows instructions literally and may twist them if hostile.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: PLANAR BINDING, p. 266 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed save creates compelled service; dial: the binding requires an hour, a consumed jewel worth at least 1,000 gp, and has a set term.

rules.statement: A 7th-level casting transports the caster and up to eight willing hand-linked creatures to another plane, aiming at a broadly described destination or a known teleportation-circle sequence. Alternatively, the caster can attempt to banish an unwilling creature within reach with a melee spell attack; a hit followed by a failed Charisma save sends it to a random location on the specified plane.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: PLANE SHIFT, p. 267 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: travel between planes is possible; dial: willing group travel is capped at eight companions, while unwilling travel requires a hit and a failed save and has an uncertain destination.

rules.statement: A 4th-level casting transforms a visible creature into a beast whose challenge rating does not exceed the target's, or its level if it has no challenge rating; an unwilling target can resist with a Wisdom save, and a shapechanger succeeds automatically. The change lasts up to 1 hour with concentration or until the target reaches 0 hit points or dies; the beast's statistics and hit points replace the target's, while personality and alignment remain, and its gear melds into the form.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: POLYMORPH, p. 267 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a target can be changed into a bounded beast form; dial: the form's challenge rating is capped, concentration limits duration, and damage can end the change.

rules.statement: A 6th-level casting creates an illusion no larger than a 30-foot cube that remains dormant until a specified visual or audible condition occurs within 30 feet. It then performs a script of up to 5 minutes and goes dormant for 10 minutes before it can trigger again; physical interaction exposes it, and successful examination lets a creature see through it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: PROGRAMMED ILLUSION, p. 270 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a preset sensory illusion responds to a chosen trigger; dial: its size, trigger range, performance length, and reactivation interval are fixed limits.

rules.statement: A 2nd-level casting places a visible, mind-only phantasm of an object, creature, or phenomenon no larger than a 10-foot cube in one creature's perception after it fails an Intelligence save. The target treats it as real and can take 1d6 psychic damage on the caster's turn when near a logically harmful phantasm; a successful action to investigate ends the effect, which requires concentration and lasts at most 1 minute.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: PHANTASMAL FORCE, p. 265 (dnd5e-phb-2014#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed save makes one target perceive and react to a private illusion; dial: the effect is limited in size, duration, and damage, and investigation can end it.

rules.statement: A touch can restore a dead creature that has been dead no more than 10 days, if its soul is willing and free to return; it comes back with 1 hit point. The casting consumes a diamond worth at least 500 gp, cannot restore undead or a creature lacking a vital body part, and leaves a −4 penalty to attacks, saves, and checks that decreases by 1 after each long rest.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Raise Dead (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: returning a soul requires its consent and freedom; dial: the 10-day limit, costly diamond, and recovery penalty; reason: death is difficult to reverse.

rules.statement: A dead humanoid, or a piece of one, can be used to form a new adult body and call its soul into it, provided death occurred within 10 days and the soul is willing and free. The soul’s former memories and capabilities remain, but its ancestry and related traits change according to a d100 result or the game master’s choice; rare materials worth at least 1,000 gp are consumed.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Reincarnate, p. 272 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: identity survives bodily replacement; dial: the new body’s ancestry is variable and the materials are costly; reason: restoration does not guarantee the same form.

rules.statement: A one-hour casting can bind up to eight willing creatures within 30 feet into a telepathic group for one hour. They can communicate across any distance, even without a shared language, but the link cannot cross between planes and does not affect creatures with Intelligence 2 or lower.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Rary’s Telepathic Bond, p. 272 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: willing participants share a private communication link; dial: the group size, duration, and plane boundary; reason: the connection is bounded and excludes minds too limited to participate.

rules.statement: A casting can hide a willing creature or an object from sight and divination until dispelled; a creature is also suspended so it does not experience time or age. The caster may set an early-ending condition that must occur or be visible within one mile, and any damage to the target ends the effect; valuable gem dust worth at least 5,000 gp is consumed.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Sequester, p. 275 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: concealment protects its target from detection; dial: damage breaks it and any custom release condition is limited to one mile; reason: the protection is costly and vulnerable to disruption.

rules.statement: The caster takes the form of a seen creature whose challenge rating is no higher than the caster’s level, replacing most game statistics while retaining specified mental scores, proficiencies, and eligible features. The caster can change forms during the spell, which lasts up to an hour with concentration; equipment may fall, merge, or be worn, and changing to a form with more hit points does not increase current hit points.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Shapechange, pp. 275–276 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation grants a creature’s physical capabilities; dial: forms must be known and within the rating limit, while equipment and retained features constrain use; reason: borrowed bodies have limits.

rules.statement: A touch can open an extradimensional space at the upper end of a rope up to 60 feet long; the space holds up to eight Medium or smaller creatures for one hour. The rope can be pulled inside, attacks and spells cannot cross the opening, and everything inside falls out when the effect ends.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Rope Trick, p. 273 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a bounded pocket space provides temporary shelter; dial: capacity, duration, access through the rope, and forced release limit its use; reason: the refuge is temporary, not a permanent hiding place.

rules.statement: The caster can observe a chosen creature on the same plane for up to 10 minutes, with the target’s saving throw adjusted by familiarity and the strength of a physical connection. On a failed save, an invisible sensor stays within 10 feet of the creature and transmits sight and hearing; alternatively, the caster can place a stationary sensor at a previously seen location.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Scrying, p. 274 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: remote observation can reveal a target’s surroundings; dial: familiarity and physical links affect resistance, while the effect is limited to the same plane; reason: observation is neither certain nor universal.

rules.statement: A suggestion of one or two sentences can influence a creature that hears and understands it for up to eight hours, if it fails a Wisdom save. The action must sound reasonable, cannot be obviously harmful, and ends if the caster or an ally damages the target; if the task finishes sooner, the effect ends then.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Suggestion, p. 279 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed save lets a persuasive instruction guide behavior; dial: reasonableness, duration, and harm or interference constrain it; reason: influence cannot compel plainly self-destructive conduct.

rules.statement: A glyph can be hidden on a surface up to 10 feet across or inside an object that remains within 10 feet of where it was inscribed. Its creator sets a trigger and can specify exclusions; when triggered, it affects creatures in or entering a 60-foot-radius sphere for 10 minutes, using one selected harmful effect. The inscription consumes materials worth at least 1,000 gp, and moving its container too far breaks the effect without triggering it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Symbol, p. 280 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a concealed, conditional rule activates an area effect; dial: trigger conditions, exclusion criteria, radius, duration, and costly materials bound it; reason: the prepared hazard is powerful but fixed in place.

rules.statement: A touch can restore a dead creature to life with all hit points if it has been dead no more than a century, did not die of old age, is not undead, and its soul is willing and free. The casting consumes a diamond worth at least 1,000 gp; the returning creature suffers a −4 penalty to attacks, saves, and checks, reduced by 1 after each long rest, and the caster cannot cast spells and has disadvantage on attacks, checks, and saves until finishing a long rest if the death occurred at least a year earlier.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Resurrection, p. 272 (dnd5e-phb-2014#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a willing, available soul can be restored to its body; dial: age of death, costly components, recovery burden, and caster exhaustion limit the return; reason: reversing long-standing death exacts a price.

rules.statement: A telekinetic effect can target one visible creature or object within 60 feet, and the caster spends an action each round to choose or maintain the target. A Huge-or-smaller creature can be moved up to 30 feet after a successful contest against its Strength; an object up to 1,000 pounds moves automatically if unattended, while a carried object requires the contest and can be pulled free.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Telekinesis, p. 281 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one target and action-by-action control; dial: target size, weight, and 30-foot movement; the target can resist, and changing targets releases the former one.

rules.statement: Teleportation moves the caster and up to eight willing visible creatures, or one visible object fitting inside a 10-foot cube, to a known destination on the same plane. Arrival reliability depends on familiarity: a known permanent circle or very familiar place is certain, while poorer familiarity can cause a miss, a similar destination, or a damaging mishap; a mishap deals 3d10 force damage to each traveler or the object and rerolls the outcome.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Teleport, pp. 281–282 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: destination knowledge constrains safe travel; dial: familiarity categories and up to eight companions; uncertainty can misplace or injure travelers.

rules.statement: A one-minute casting and 50 gp of consumed materials open a portal for one round between the caster's location and a known permanent circle on the same plane. Anyone entering appears within 5 feet of the destination circle, or in its nearest unoccupied space; repeating the casting in one place daily for a year makes a circle permanent.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Teleportation Circle, p. 283 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: passage requires a known, established endpoint; dial: one-round opening and a year of daily work to establish permanence; materials are consumed.

rules.statement: The caster and up to eight willing creatures can spend 1 action to travel instantly to a previously designated sanctuary linked to the caster's deity. Without preparing that sanctuary by casting the spell there, or if the place lacks the required religious connection, the spell has no effect.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Word of Recall, p. 290 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: return is anchored to a designated sacred place; dial: caster plus five companions and prior preparation; unsuitable locations make the attempt fail.

rules.statement: A telepathic link lasts up to 24 hours between the caster and one familiar, willing creature on the same plane. They can instantly exchange words and sensory messages; the target recognizes the caster, and a creature with Intelligence 1 or higher can understand the meaning of messages.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Telepathy, p. 281 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: two familiar, consenting parties share a private channel; dial: one target, same-plane limit, and 24-hour duration.

rules.statement: A willing creature touched by the caster gains underwater breathing for 24 hours while retaining its usual breathing method; the effect can cover up to ten creatures.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Water Breathing, p. 288 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: add a temporary survival capability; dial: up to ten willing targets for 24 hours; normal breathing remains available.

rules.statement: Up to ten willing visible creatures can move across liquid surfaces as if they were harmless solid ground for one hour, though crossing molten lava still causes heat damage. A submerged target is carried to the surface at 60 feet per round.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Waterwalk, p. 288 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: grant a bounded movement adaptation; dial: ten targets, one hour, and a 60-foot-per-round surfacing rate; dangerous heat is not negated.

rules.statement: A willing creature can be transformed into another creature, or into or from an object, for up to one hour; maintaining the effect for the full duration makes it permanent. An unwilling creature can resist, and a creature transformed into another creature is limited by its new form and cannot use its old equipment.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: True Polymorph, pp. 284–285 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation is temporary and concentration-bound; dial: full-hour maintenance makes it permanent; resistance, form limits, and lost access to gear constrain it.

rules.statement: A willing creature linked to the caster by paired rings gains +1 to AC and saving throws and resistance to all damage while within 60 feet. Whenever it takes damage, the caster takes the same amount; the link ends if either reaches 0 hit points, they separate beyond 60 feet, the effect is recast on either, or the caster dismisses it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Warding Bond, p. 288 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: protection is purchased by sharing harm; dial: +1 defenses, resistance, and 60-foot range; the caster bears equal damage and the bond has explicit break conditions.

rules.statement: An effect imposing a condition lasts until countered or until its stated duration expires. Multiple applications track their durations separately but do not intensify the condition; a creature either has the condition or does not.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix A: Conditions, p. 291 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: repeated applications do not worsen a condition; dial: independent durations; countering or expiry ends each instance.

rules.statement: Exhaustion has six cumulative levels: ability-check disadvantage, halved speed, attack-roll and save disadvantage, halved hit-point maximum, speed 0, then death. A long rest reduces exhaustion by one level only if the creature has also had food and drink; other effects can remove specified levels.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix A: Conditions, p. 292 (dnd5e-phb-2014#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: accumulated strain worsens in six ordered stages; dial: one level per qualifying rest; recovery requires food and drink, and the highest level is fatal.

rules.statement: A restrained creature has its speed reduced to 0 and cannot benefit from speed increases. Attacks against it have advantage, its own attacks have disadvantage, and it has disadvantage on Dexterity saves.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix A: Conditions, p. 293–294 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the condition applies its full movement and defense penalties; dial: decide how it is imposed and how long it lasts, since this passage only defines its effects.

rules.statement: A stunned creature is incapacitated, cannot move, can speak only falteringly, automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves, and is easier to hit: attacks against it have advantage.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix A: Conditions, p. 293–294 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: stun blocks movement and effective action and makes two save types automatic failures; dial: the passage gives no cause or duration for the state.

rules.statement: An unconscious creature is incapacitated, cannot move or speak, and is unaware of its surroundings; it drops held items and falls prone. It automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves, attacks against it have advantage, and a hit from an attacker within 5 feet is a critical hit.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix A: Conditions, p. 293–294 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: unconsciousness removes awareness and action and exposes the creature to close critical hits; dial: the passage does not specify how the condition begins or ends.

rules.statement: Planar travel can be accomplished by spells or portals: some spells transport travelers directly, while others let them enter a transit plane and travel onward. A portal links a particular place on one plane to a particular place on another, and crossing it may be as simple as stepping through.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix C: The Planes of Existence, p. 301 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: travel follows a spell’s reach or a portal’s fixed endpoints; dial: precision and access depend on the spell or on finding and using the relevant portal.

rules.statement: A demiplane is a small extradimensional space with its own rules, entered through a single point where it touches another plane. A plane-shift spell might reach one, but requires an exceptionally difficult-to-obtain tuning fork; a gate spell is more dependable if the caster knows of the demiplane.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix C: The Planes of Existence, p. 302 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each demiplane has its own rules and a single entry point; dial: access is constrained by rare tuning requirements or prior knowledge.

rules.statement: The Ethereal Plane overlaps the Material Plane and Inner Planes at corresponding locations, and certain creatures and senses can perceive into its border region. Some magical effects, especially force-based ones, extend from the Material Plane into that region.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix C: The Planes of Existence, p. 301 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: only specified perception abilities reveal the border region and some effects cross into it; dial: the passage does not specify the full list of eligible creatures or effects.

rules.statement: A plane’s alignment is part of its essence; a visitor whose alignment does not match it feels profound dissonance, while a matching visitor feels in tune with the plane.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix C: The Planes of Existence, p. 302 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: mismatched alignment causes discomfort and matching alignment creates ease; dial: the passage provides no further mechanical penalty or benefit.

rules.statement: The Dire Wolf has advantage on attacks against a creature when one of the wolf’s allies is within 5 feet of that creature and is not incapacitated.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix D: Creature Statistics, Dire Wolf, p. 306 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: an active nearby ally enables the attack advantage; dial: the benefit depends on ally position and condition.

rules.statement: A crocodile hit with its bite grapples the target; while the grapple lasts, the target is restrained and the crocodile cannot bite another target.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix D: Creature Statistics, Crocodile, p. 305 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bite binds one target and occupies the crocodile’s bite capacity until the grapple ends; dial: the excerpt does not state how the grapple ends.

rules.statement: A constrictor snake hit with its constrict attack grapples one creature; while the grapple lasts, that creature is restrained and the snake cannot constrict another target.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix D: Creature Statistics, Constrictor Snake, p. 305 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one ongoing grapple prevents the snake from constricting another target; dial: the excerpt does not state how the grapple ends.

rules.statement: A giant eagle understands Common but cannot speak it; it can speak Giant.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix D: Creature Statistics, Giant Eagle, p. 307 (dnd5e-phb-2014#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: comprehension and speech are separate capabilities; dial: the passage does not provide any way for the eagle to overcome its speech limit.

rules.statement: A shapechanging creature can use an action to take one of its listed beast forms or return to its usual form; its statistics mostly stay the same, its attacks may differ, and carried equipment does not change. If it dies, it returns to its usual form.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix D, Shapechanger (pp. 307–310) (dnd5e-phb-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: form changes preserve most capabilities; dial: restrict available forms or change which traits persist, because equipment and some attacks do not follow the transformation.

rules.statement: An invisible creature remains so until it attacks or uses a specified ability, or until its concentration ends; anything it carries or wears is also invisible while in contact with it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix D, Invisibility (pp. 308–310) (dnd5e-phb-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: concealment ends on a listed action or failed concentration; dial: broaden or narrow the ending triggers, because attacking reveals the creature.

rules.statement: A creature with magic resistance has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix D, Magic Resistance (pp. 307–310) (dnd5e-phb-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resistance improves defense without preventing the effect; dial: limit the kinds of magic resisted, because the protection is broad.

rules.statement: While touching a web, a spider knows the exact location of any other creature touching that same web; it also ignores movement restrictions caused by webbing.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix D, Giant Spider (p. 306) (dnd5e-phb-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sensing works only through the shared web; dial: change the medium or what it reveals, because contact is required.

rules.statement: A spider can climb difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix D, Giant Spider (p. 306) (dnd5e-phb-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: difficult surfaces impose no check; dial: limit the surfaces or duration, because the passage grants unrestricted climbing.

rules.statement: Some bites or stings make the target attempt a Constitution save; on failure, the target takes the stated poison damage or becomes poisoned for a stated duration, with some effects allowing repeat saves to end early. A specified sting can also render a target unconscious if its save result is 6 or lower, until the duration ends, it takes damage, or another creature uses an action to wake it.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix D, Giant Spider, Poisonous Snake, Pseudodragon, Quasit, and Sprite (pp. 306–311) (dnd5e-phb-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: saving throws, durations, and listed escape conditions bound the poison; dial: adjust severity or recovery, because poison can disable a target.

rules.statement: A quasit can frighten one chosen creature within 20 feet once per day; the target can repeat its Wisdom save at the end of each turn, with disadvantage while the quasit is in line of sight, and a success ends the effect.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix D, Quasit (p. 310) (dnd5e-phb-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect allows repeated saves and lasts at most 1 minute; dial: change its reach or recovery, because fear is imposed on a target.

rules.statement: A raven can imitate simple sounds it has heard; a listener can identify the sounds as imitations with a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Insight) check.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix D, Raven (p. 310) (dnd5e-phb-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: imitation is limited to simple sounds already heard; dial: change what can be copied or how easily it is detected, because listeners can recognize the deception.

rules.statement: When damage would reduce a zombie to 0 hit points, it instead drops to 1 hit point if it succeeds on a Constitution save with a DC of 5 plus the damage taken; radiant damage and critical hits prevent this check.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix D, Zombie (p. 311) (dnd5e-phb-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: survival is a one-time check at the point of defeat and excludes specified damage; dial: alter the DC or exclusions, because the creature resists being brought down.

rules.statement: A lion or similar creature knocks a target prone if it moves at least 20 feet straight toward it immediately before a claw hit and the target fails a Strength save; against a prone target, it can then use a bonus action to make a bite attack.
locators: D&D 5e Player's Handbook 2014: Appendix D, Lion and Panther (pp. 307–308) (dnd5e-phb-2014#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the knockdown requires both a charge and a failed save; dial: change the distance or save, because the follow-up attack depends on the target being prone.

rules.statement: A portal can open only at its assigned time, when its condition is met, after a command, or while a traveler carries its key. Once a keyed traveler crosses, it stays open until the start of that traveler’s next turn.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Chapter 2: Sigil — Portal Basics (dnd5e-planescape#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: portals have a condition or key and may be inactive; dial: set the trigger and opening duration; in-world reason: the gateway is controlled by its own magical terms.

rules.statement: Inactive portals are usually invisible, even to magic detection; true seeing or warp sense can reveal them. When activated, a portal is typically outlined by light and shows its destination.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Chapter 2: Sigil — Portal Basics (dnd5e-planescape#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: conceal inactive gateways; dial: allow specialized senses to find them; in-world reason: the portal becomes apparent when it activates.

rules.statement: A portal key may be an object, a particular created key, or—in rarer cases—a creature type, memory, or whistled tune; it works from either side of the portal.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Chapter 2: Sigil — Portal Keys (dnd5e-planescape#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: access is bound to a key; dial: choose whether that key is a thing, a remembered fact, or an action; in-world reason: the key matches the portal’s destination.

rules.statement: A one-way portal works only in its stated direction and cannot be seen or detected from its exit side. A shifting portal moves one end between locations, while a tumbling-lock portal requires a different key each time it opens.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Chapter 2: Sigil — Portal Quirks (dnd5e-planescape#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: portals may impose directional, location, or key restrictions; dial: choose which restriction applies; in-world reason: each portal has its own unusual magical behavior.

rules.statement: A slow portal holds an entrant in unaware stasis for 2d4 days before arrival. A taxing portal requires a DC 10 Constitution save to avoid 1 exhaustion level, and a temporary portal vanishes after 1d6 + 6 travelers have crossed in either direction.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Chapter 2: Sigil — Portal Quirks (dnd5e-planescape#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: these portals can impose delay, bodily strain, or a limited number of crossings; dial: select the complication and its severity; in-world reason: unstable or specialized portal energy exacts a cost.

rules.statement: In Sigil, effects that try to banish someone treat Sigil as that target’s home plane. Interplanar travel effects cannot enter or leave the city, and teleportation into or out of it fails, though teleportation within the city works normally.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Chapter 2: Sigil — Alterations to Magic (dnd5e-planescape#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: block travel across Sigil’s boundary while permitting local teleportation; dial: allow narrow exceptions; in-world reason: the Lady of Pain controls access to the city.

rules.statement: Within Sigil, effects that summon creatures or objects from other planes instead draw them from inside the city if possible; otherwise they fail. An effect that calls a specific target from outside Sigil fails automatically.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Chapter 2: Sigil — Alterations to Magic (dnd5e-planescape#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: redirect a general summons locally or make it fail; dial: specific outside targets always fail; in-world reason: Sigil’s boundary prevents outside entities from being called in.

rules.statement: Extradimensional spaces, demiplanes, and pocket dimensions function in Sigil, but they are subject to the city’s magical restrictions as if they were part of Sigil.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Chapter 2: Sigil — Alterations to Magic (dnd5e-planescape#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow pocket spaces but apply the local boundary rules to them; dial: decide whether a space counts as part of the restricted region; in-world reason: the city’s influence extends into these spaces.

rules.statement: The Lady of Pain can block an individual creature from entering or leaving through a portal, and during severe faction conflict she can disable every portal in Sigil. When all portals stop, supplies cannot enter and refuse and unburied dead accumulate.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Chapter 2: Sigil — Locking the Cage (dnd5e-planescape#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the Lady may deny an individual’s passage; dial: citywide shutdown is reserved for major strife; in-world reason: isolation forces the factions to resolve their conflict.

rules.statement: A creature that attacks, casts a spell at, or otherwise targets the Lady with a hostile or prying effect immediately drops to 1 hit point. If it persists, she sends it to the Mazes on the next blink.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Chapter 2: Sigil — Interfering with the Lady (dnd5e-planescape#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: hostile or intrusive actions trigger immediate incapacitation; dial: continued defiance adds imprisonment; in-world reason: the Lady protects herself and Sigil by overwhelming intruders.

rules.statement: The Mazes are demiplanar prisons that swallow chosen creatures instantly. Prisoners need no food, drink, or sleep, and no magic lets them escape or communicate with planes beyond; any escape portal, if one exists, cannot be found by magical detection.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Chapter 2: Sigil — The Mazes (dnd5e-planescape#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: imprisonment isolates the target indefinitely without bodily needs; dial: an exit may exist but is extraordinarily hard to locate; in-world reason: the prison is made to contain threats to the city.

rules.statement: Contracts ratified on gold are enforced by maruts and truth-seeking kolyaruts; those who break them are tracked down and banished to a teleportation circle in the hall.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: High Courts — Hall of Concordance [Page 43] (dnd5e-planescape#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: breach triggers pursuit and banishment; dial: the contract’s terms and the severity of enforcement; reason: the inevitables exist to make dealings orderly.

rules.statement: Prison cells are adapted to their inmates: fire elementals are kept in freezing cells, while giants wear magic collars that weaken them and shrink them to a smaller stature. Especially dangerous prisoners can be held in isolated demiplanes saturated with antimagic.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Prison — Cells [Page 44] (dnd5e-planescape#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: confinement is tailored to the prisoner; dial: the restraint’s strength and the degree of suppression or reduction; reason: the prison must hold beings with very different capabilities.

rules.statement: The Silent King’s throne grants authority over the undead who serve him, but only a living creature can occupy it, and death is the only way to leave its grip. The undead remain bound to serve until the king is killed or decays away.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Undersigil — Dead Nations [Page 54] (dnd5e-planescape#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: occupancy binds the living ruler to the throne and the undead to their ruler; dial: which undead are subject and how authority is expressed; reason: rulership comes with a lethal, inescapable obligation.

rules.statement: The Loop is a closed tunnel fed by hidden, one-way portals, and its space and time do not follow ordinary rules. Travelers can encounter their own traces there; escape may take seconds inside but years outside, or release them in the distant past or future.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Undersigil — The Loop [Page 54] (dnd5e-planescape#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: entry routes feed a trapped circular space with irregular time; dial: whether escape is possible and how far time displacement reaches; reason: the place is a dangerous maze used to imprison threats.

rules.statement: The Great Foundry’s magical sculptors can shape objects from minimal raw material, making sturdy, delicate tools without coal or flame; one example elsewhere in the ward describes reshaping nearby material.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Lower Ward — Great Foundry [Page 47] (dnd5e-planescape#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: material is reshaped into useful craft; dial: the quantity and complexity achievable; reason: skilled makers turn scarce resources into tools for the city.

rules.statement: When the Athar destroy magic items made by priests of gods they reject, the released magic is gathered by the Luminous Arbor and concentrated in its fruit, which powers their priests.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Lower Ward — Shattered Temple, Luminous Arbor [Page 49] (dnd5e-planescape#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: destroyed items’ released magic accumulates in the tree and fruit; dial: how much power is captured and what a priest can draw from it; reason: their rites convert disputed divine relics into a usable source.

rules.statement: The Planar Energy Cooperative monitors magical flows for anomalies, and its mages can combine their power to siphon magic from whole worlds to weaken dangerous artifacts or stop catastrophic spellcasting. The group is small, and this requires sustained intense concentration.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Market Ward — Planar Energy Cooperative [Page 53] (dnd5e-planescape#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: group effort can drain magic at world scale for containment; dial: range, duration, and how much magic is diverted; reason: few mages can maintain the concentration, so they send others to handle threats.

rules.statement: The Ditch’s corrosive water can leave creatures washed ashore hours later unrecognizable, smoothing away their physical features; rare portals to the River Oceanus briefly make the water clean and sweet instead.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Lower Ward — The Ditch [Page 46] (dnd5e-planescape#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: exposure alters a body over hours; dial: the severity and reversibility of the change; reason: toxic runoff and planar influence make the water hazardous, while an occasional portal temporarily changes its nature.

rules.statement: The chaos mass in the Face of Gith continually changes its substance and form, and some patrons can mentally shape it into objects, creatures, or sensory displays. It is rumored to form a portal to Limbo, but the required key changes constantly.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Lower Ward — Face of Gith [Page 47] (dnd5e-planescape#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: mental influence reshapes the unstable mass; dial: the forms, complexity, and whether a portal can be made; reason: primordial chaos is mutable and its portal key is unpredictable.

rules.statement: When a location in the Outlands embodies an Outer Plane too strongly, that plane takes the location and its inhabitants, expanding its own realm and restoring balance to the Outlands.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Life in the Outlands — Cosmic Realignment, page 59 (dnd5e-planescape#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: trigger on excessive planar alignment; dial: define how much alignment qualifies; the in-world cost is losing the location and its inhabitants to that plane.

rules.statement: Automata’s portal can be used from either side, but a creature must first receive clearance for gate travel from an authorized modron.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Automata — Gate, page 60 (dnd5e-planescape#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require official clearance; dial: choose the approving authority and its criteria; the in-world cost is restricted access.

rules.statement: In Bedlam, creatures within 1,000 feet of the gate are deafened by its constant winds. The winds can also dominate longstanding residents and compel them to commit evil acts.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Bedlam — Regional Effects, page 63 (dnd5e-planescape#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated 1,000-foot boundary and ongoing exposure; dial: decide how often the compulsion takes hold; the in-world cost is impaired hearing and coerced behavior.

rules.statement: In Curst, creatures’ speed is reduced by 5 feet, and attempts to leave by teleportation or extradimensional or interplanar travel fail unless they use the town’s gate. The burgomaster can use an action to suppress either effect for any number of creatures for 1 hour.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Curst — Regional Effects, pages 64–65 (dnd5e-planescape#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: both restrictions apply in Curst; dial: the burgomaster chooses whom to exempt and which restriction to suppress; the in-world cost is curtailed movement and escape.

rules.statement: A pacifying aura extends 300 feet from Ecstasy’s Bone Plinth. A creature that starts its turn within it is targeted by a calm emotions effect with save DC 15; a creature that succeeds cannot be affected by the aura again for 24 hours.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Ecstasy — Aura of Tranquility, page 66 (dnd5e-planescape#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the aura at 300 feet, DC 15, with 24-hour immunity after a successful save; dial: adjust radius, difficulty, or immunity duration; the in-world cost is suppressed hostility.

rules.statement: Faunel’s gate pool has the effects of an awaken spell: beasts that drink from it gain speech, and saplings raised on its water eventually uproot as wooden guardians. Creatures that submerge themselves in the pool travel to the Beastlands.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Faunel — Gate, page 70 (dnd5e-planescape#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: drinking grants the stated effects and submerging transports the creature; dial: set the duration and limits of the granted traits; the in-world cost is exposure to a transformative, one-way threshold.

rules.statement: A creature that submerges itself in Ecstasy’s reflective pool emerges in Elysium’s innermost layer.
locators: Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse: Ecstasy — Gate, page 66 (dnd5e-planescape#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: submerging transports the creature to the named destination; dial: decide whether passage is one-way and who can use it; the in-world cost is leaving the Outlands.
