rules.statement: Your ranged radiant bolt is a proficient spell attack with a 30-foot range, using Dexterity for attack and damage and a damage die that scales with your Martial Arts die. When you take the Attack action and use it, you may spend 1 ki to make two such attacks as a bonus action; with Extra Attack, it can replace any attack in that action.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Radiant Sun Bolt (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bolt uses a defined range and scaling die; the bonus pair costs ki and requires the Attack action.

rules.statement: Immediately after taking the Attack action on your turn, spend 2 ki to cast a short-range cone of flame as a bonus action. Each further ki point raises its spell level by 1, up to a total ki spend of half your monk level.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Searing Arc Strike (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a minimum ki cost and level-based spending cap bound the strengthened area effect.

rules.statement: As an action, create and throw a radiant orb to a point within 150 feet; creatures in its 20-foot-radius burst save against taking 2d6 radiant damage, except those behind opaque total cover. Spend up to 3 ki to add 2d6 damage per point.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Searing Sunburst (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the burst has fixed range and radius, cover blocks it, and added damage is capped at 3 ki.

rules.statement: While your light is active, it illuminates brightly for 30 feet and dimly for a further 30 feet; a bonus action turns it off or on. When a creature hits you with a melee attack while it shines, you can use your reaction to deal radiant damage equal to 5 plus your Wisdom modifier.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Sun Shield (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the light’s reach is fixed and the retaliatory effect requires both an active light and a reaction.

rules.statement: When you use Channel Divinity, you may use an action to frighten chosen visible creatures within 30 feet that fail a Wisdom save for 1 minute. Each affected creature can repeat the save at the end of its turns to end the condition.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Oath of Conquest — Channel Divinity: Conquering Presence (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect is limited by sight, range, a failed save, and a one-minute duration, with repeated chances to end it.

rules.statement: When you make an attack roll, you may use Channel Divinity after seeing the roll but before its outcome is declared to add 10 to it.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Oath of Conquest — Channel Divinity: Guided Strike (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the fixed accuracy boost spends a limited divine resource and must be chosen before the result is known.

rules.statement: While you are not incapacitated, frightened creatures within 10 feet of you have speed 0 and take psychic damage equal to half your paladin level when they start their turn there; at 18th level the aura reaches 30 feet. When a creature hits you, it also takes psychic damage equal to your Charisma modifier, minimum 1, if you are not incapacitated.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Aura of Conquest; Scornful Rebuke (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the aura only affects creatures already frightened and is blocked by total cover; retaliation requires a hit and an active, capable paladin.

rules.statement: When a creature within 10 feet takes damage, you may use your reaction to take that damage instead; accompanying effects do not transfer, and the damage cannot be reduced. At 18th level the range increases to 30 feet.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Oath of Redemption — Aura of the Guardian (dnd5e-xanathar#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: protection redirects damage at the paladin’s expense, consumes a reaction, and does not transfer other effects or permit reduction.

rules.statement: From 3rd level, you can use Help as a bonus action. When helping an ally attack, you can assist from as far as 30 feet away instead of 5 feet, provided the target can see or hear you.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: [Passage opening; heading missing] (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enabled at 3rd level; dial: assistance range; the target must perceive your aid.

rules.statement: From 9th level, after at least 1 minute observing or interacting with a creature outside combat, choose two traits from Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and class levels; the GM tells you whether the creature is equal, better, or worse than you in those traits. At the GM’s discretion, you might also learn a piece of its history or a personality trait.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Insightful Manipulator (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: comparison of two chosen traits after a minute; dial: whether personal history or personality is revealed, at GM discretion.

rules.statement: From 13th level, when an attack targets you and a creature within 5 feet is giving you cover against it, you can use your reaction to redirect that attack to that creature.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Misdirection (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: redirect one attack; dial: none; it requires a nearby creature whose cover protects you and consumes your reaction.

rules.statement: From 17th level, telepathy and other mind-reading cannot read your thoughts unless you permit it. You can instead present false thoughts by winning a contested Charisma (Deception) check against the reader’s Wisdom (Insight) check.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Soul of Deceit (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: thoughts are unreadable; dial: false thoughts require winning the opposed check, while allowing access is your choice.

rules.statement: Magic that tests whether you are telling the truth reports you as truthful if you choose, and magic cannot compel you to tell the truth.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Soul of Deceit (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: both magical truth detection and compulsion are defeated; dial: the truthful result is optional, with the in-world limit that the feature applies to magic.

rules.statement: From 3rd level, when an enemy ends its turn within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to move up to half your speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Scout — Skirmisher (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: movement up to half speed; dial: none; it triggers only at an enemy’s turn end and uses your reaction.

rules.statement: From 9th level, your walking speed increases by 10 feet; the increase also applies to climbing and swimming speeds if you have them.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Scout — Superior Mobility (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: +10 feet to applicable speeds; dial: only speeds you already possess benefit.

rules.statement: From 13th level, you have advantage on initiative rolls. The first creature you hit in the first combat round grants advantage on attack rolls against it until the start of your next turn.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Scout — Ambush Master (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: initiative benefit and a brief shared attack advantage; dial: the target must be the first one you hit in the first round.

rules.statement: From 17th level, after taking the Attack action, you can make one extra attack as a bonus action. That attack can use Sneak Attack even if you already used Sneak Attack this turn, but you cannot apply Sneak Attack to the same target more than once in a turn.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Scout — Sudden Strike (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one bonus-action attack with a conditional extra Sneak Attack; dial: once per target per turn remains the limit.

rules.statement: From 9th level, you can use an action to contest a creature’s Wisdom (Insight) with your Charisma (Persuasion), if it can hear you and you share a language. If a hostile target loses, it has disadvantage attacking anyone but you and cannot make opportunity attacks against other targets for 1 minute; the effect ends early if an ally attacks it or affects it with a spell, or if you get more than 60 feet away.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Swashbuckler — Panache (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the hostile target is drawn toward you for up to 1 minute; dial: opposed check and early-ending conditions constrain the effect.

rules.statement: If a nonhostile creature loses the Panache contest, it is charmed for 1 minute and regards you as a friendly acquaintance. The charm ends immediately if you or your companions do anything harmful to it.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Swashbuckler — Panache (dnd5e-xanathar#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: friendly-acquaintance attitude for 1 minute; dial: the contested check and any harmful act by your group ends it.

rules.statement: When hit by an attack or when failing a saving throw, a war mage can spend a reaction to gain +2 AC against that attack or +4 on that saving throw. After using this defense, the mage cannot cast spells other than cantrips until the end of their next turn.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 60, Arcane Deflection (dnd5e-xanathar#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a brief defensive boost; dial: the spellcasting lockout lasts through the next turn, reflecting the effort diverted into defense.

rules.statement: At 6th level, a war mage can hold power surges up to a maximum equal to their Intelligence modifier, with a minimum capacity of one. After a long rest, the reserve resets to one; ending a spell successfully with dispel magic or counterspell adds one, and finishing a short rest with none also restores one. Once per turn when a wizard spell damages a creature or object, the mage can spend one surge to add force damage equal to half their wizard level.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 61, Power Surge (dnd5e-xanathar#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: surges are a limited stored resource with explicit recovery and capacity; dial: each use consumes one surge, fueled by foiled magic or rest.

rules.statement: While concentrating on a spell, a war mage gains +2 AC and +2 on all saving throws.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 61, Durable Magic (dnd5e-xanathar#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: protection persists only during concentration; dial: it rewards maintaining the spell, with concentration as its limiting condition.

rules.statement: When using Arcane Deflection, a 14th-level war mage can also deal force damage equal to half their wizard level to as many as three chosen creatures they can see within 60 feet.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 61, Deflecting Shroud (dnd5e-xanathar#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the defensive response can strike back; dial: it is limited to three visible targets within 60 feet and occurs only when the defense is used.

rules.statement: A life-event result can grant a continuing companion who performs mundane tasks during travel, but the companion leaves if neglected, abused, or put in danger.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 71, Boons (dnd5e-xanathar#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the companion's service is ongoing; dial: care and safety are required to retain the bond.

rules.statement: A past adventure can leave a character poisoned: they recover, but the next saving throw they make against poison is at disadvantage.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 71, Adventures (dnd5e-xanathar#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a resolved past hazard can impose a later penalty; dial: it applies only to the next poison save.

rules.statement: A past adventure may yield a magical item, with the specific common item chosen by the DM.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 71, Adventures (dnd5e-xanathar#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the item is an acquired reward; dial: the DM selects the item, with no further use or upkeep limits stated.

rules.statement: A character who succeeds at casting a discovered spell scroll has accomplished that past event; a separate past event may leave them temporarily invisible.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 71, Arcane Matters (dnd5e-xanathar#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: these are recorded as prior events rather than ongoing abilities; dial: invisibility lasts only for an unspecified time.

rules.statement: After a diviner reads a character's fortune, roll twice on the life-event table, but do not apply either result; the DM selects one as a portent that may or may not come true.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 71, Arcane Matters (dnd5e-xanathar#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the reading supplies a possible future event; dial: the DM chooses between two results and the prediction is not guaranteed.

rules.statement: When an ally you can see within 30 feet rolls a 1 on an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you may spend your reaction to let them reroll; they must keep the new result. Afterward, you cannot use your own Lucky trait until the end of your next turn.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 75, Bountiful Luck (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a reaction and temporary lockout of your own luck limit how often you can rescue an ally.

rules.statement: You may spend a use of your breath weapon to roar, making creatures you choose within 30 feet save against DC 8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier or become frightened of you for 1 minute. A creature that cannot hear or see you succeeds automatically; a frightened target that takes damage may repeat the save, ending the effect on a success.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 75, Dragon Fear (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: this trades a breath-weapon use for a limited-duration fear effect that can be broken by a successful save.

rules.statement: After you take damage, you may use your reaction to become invisible until the end of your next turn or until you attack, deal damage, or force a creature to save; use this again only after a short or long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 75, Fade Away (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: invisibility is brief and ends upon hostile action, with a rest-based use limit.

rules.statement: You may cast misty step once without spending a spell slot, regaining this use after a short or long rest; it uses Intelligence as your spellcasting ability. The magic briefly routes your movement through the Feywild.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 75, Fey Teleportation (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a single spell-free use per rest gives a bounded shortcut through another realm.

rules.statement: When you roll fire damage for a spell you cast, you may reroll any damage die showing 1, but must use the new result. When you cast a spell that deals fire damage, you may wreath yourself in harmless flames until the end of your next turn; they shed bright light for 30 feet and dim light for another 30 feet, and a creature within 5 feet that hits you with a melee attack takes 1d4 fire damage.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Pages 75–76, Flames of Phlegethos (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the flame aura lasts only briefly and damages attackers, while the damage-die reroll cannot be rejected.

rules.statement: When you take the Dodge action in combat, you may spend one Hit Die, roll it, add your Constitution modifier, and regain that many hit points, to a minimum of 1.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 75, Dwarven Fortitude (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: healing requires both a defensive action and expenditure of a Hit Die.

rules.statement: Once per short or long rest, when you hit with a simple or martial weapon attack, you may roll one of the weapon’s damage dice an additional time and add that damage. Immediately after using Relentless Endurance, you may spend your reaction to make one weapon attack.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 76, Orcish Fury (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the extra damage is limited by rests, and the follow-up attack costs a reaction and depends on using a separate survival trait.

rules.statement: When a creature you can see hits you with an attack roll, you may use your reaction to force it to reroll; it must use the new roll. You can do this again after rolling initiative or finishing a short or long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 76, Second Chance (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the defensive reroll is limited to once per combat or rest interval and consumes your reaction.

rules.statement: When you finish a long rest after sleeping in medium or heavy armor, you regain only one quarter of your spent Hit Dice, with a minimum of one die; the rest does not reduce exhaustion.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 79, Sleeping in Armor (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: heavier armor imposes a recovery penalty because it makes restful sleep difficult.

rules.statement: For every consecutive 24-hour period without a long rest, make a Constitution save, starting at DC 10 and increasing the DC by 5 each additional period; failure causes one exhaustion level. The DC returns to 10 when you finish a long rest.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 79, Going Without a Long Rest (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: staying awake accumulates escalating exhaustion risk until a long rest resets the pressure.

rules.statement: As part of a long rest, a proficient user of alchemist’s supplies can make one dose of acid, alchemist’s fire, antitoxin, oil, perfume, or soap, subtracting half the item’s value from carried raw materials; raw materials weigh 1 pound per 50 gp spent.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Page 80, Alchemical Crafting (dnd5e-xanathar#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: production takes a long rest and consumes valued raw materials carried by the crafter.

rules.statement: A complex trap can trigger repeatedly, with separate active elements scheduled on initiative counts 20, 10, or both. Count 20 is the usual quick response; count 10 suits an effect that builds up, and using both represents an exceptionally rapid threat.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Initiative, p. 123 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use count 20; dial: choose count 10 or both; in-world, the mechanism’s timing determines how quickly it can strike.

rules.statement: A constant hazard affects a creature that ends its turn in its area. As a guideline, use the active element’s save DC or attack bonus but deal half its damage; leave some areas safe so creatures can take refuge.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Constant Elements, p. 122 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the hazard at turn end for half damage; dial: adjust coverage or damage; in-world, exposure to the ongoing danger is limited by where a creature stands.

rules.statement: A trap’s effects can change over time or in response to interference: damage may rise each round, effects may vary, or disabling one part may worsen another. Changes can follow a schedule or be selected randomly each round.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Dynamic Elements, pp. 122–123 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use a schedule; dial: vary the effects or make them reactive; in-world, the trap’s operation changes as it runs or is disrupted.

rules.statement: Defeating a complex trap generally takes three successful checks or actions against each element. Successes can first reduce its DC or attack bonus, then halve its damage, and finally shut it down; for a nonattacking element, each success reduces its effectiveness by one-third.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Defeating Complex Traps, p. 124 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require three successes per element; dial: choose intermediate reductions; in-world, overcoming a mechanism takes sustained work rather than one attempt.

rules.statement: After a character succeeds against a trap element, another character cannot attempt the same check against that element until the successful character’s next turn ends. Multiple characters therefore cannot rapidly stack attempts against one part.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Defeating Complex Traps, p. 124 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enforce the one-turn interval; dial: change it if desired; in-world, access or interference prevents successive workers from acting immediately.

rules.statement: In the rolling-sphere trap, the sphere starts at 22 damage and gains 11 damage after each turn. At 55 damage or more, it acts on both initiative counts 20 and 10; stopping it or disrupting a return portal can neutralize the trap, and each successful rune-disruption check reduces its damage by 11.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Sphere of Crushing Doom, p. 121 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: increase damage by 11 each turn and accelerate at 55; dial: alter the progression; in-world, continued movement builds speed, while failing portals slow the sphere.

rules.statement: A character can make an unspecified allied contact into a one-use source of aid, but can hold no more than 1 plus their Charisma modifier (minimum 1) of these contacts. Using a contact’s help or hindrance consumes that use; carousing again is needed to regain that contact’s willingness to help or hinder.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Carousing, pp. 128–129 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: capacity is 1 plus Charisma modifier, minimum 1, and each use is spent; dial: contacts can instead be named and tracked individually; in-world, aid depends on limited social goodwill.

rules.statement: Carousing for a workweek costs 10 gp for lower-class company, 50 gp for middle-class company, or 250 gp and access to nobility for upper-class company. A successful result can create allied contacts: one on a check total of 11–15, two on 16–20, and three on 21 or higher; a total of 1–5 creates a hostile contact.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Carousing, pp. 127–128 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: pay the stated class-based cost for a workweek; dial: choose which social circles are available; in-world, money and access buy opportunities to form relationships.

rules.statement: When crafting nonmagical gear, the character needs suitable tools, proficiency, equipment, and materials worth half the item’s selling cost. Divide the item’s cost by 50 to determine workweeks; collaborators divide that time among themselves, and a workweek can finish multiple items whose combined cost is at most 50 gp.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Crafting an Item, p. 129 (dnd5e-xanathar#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use half-cost materials and one workweek per 50 gp; dial: judge appropriate tools and collaboration limits; in-world, production is constrained by materials, skill, equipment, and labor.

rules.statement: Making a magic item requires its recipe, an adventure to obtain an exotic ingredient, and either suitable tool proficiency or Arcana proficiency. The rarity sets the work and coin cost: common 1 workweek and 50 gp, uncommon 2 and 200 gp, rare 10 and 2,000 gp, very rare 25 and 20,000 gp, legendary 50 and 100,000 gp; consumables take half the time and cost.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Crafting Magic Items, p. 130 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require both a formula and an adventure-earned exotic material; dial: halve work and expense for consumables; the scarce material and labor are the in-world cost.

rules.statement: For ordinary magic-item crafting, each five workweeks spent has a 10% chance of a complication. Healing potions use a separate route requiring herbalism-kit proficiency: healing takes 1 day and 25 gp, greater 1 workweek and 100 gp, superior 3 workweeks and 1,000 gp, and supreme 4 workweeks and 10,000 gp.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Crafting Complications and Brewing Potions of Healing, pp. 130–131 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: complications can interrupt long crafting; dial: use the listed potion-specific schedule; rare inputs, time, and mishaps constrain production.

rules.statement: A spellcaster can make a spell scroll only for a spell they know or have prepared, and must have Arcana proficiency and provide its material components. Time and cost rise with spell level, from 1 day and 15 gp for a cantrip to 48 workweeks and 250,000 gp for a 9th-level spell; a cantrip scroll functions as though cast by a 1st-level caster.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Scribing a Spell Scroll, p. 134 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: restrict scroll production to accessible spells and required expertise; dial: set time and cost by spell level; components, training, and prolonged labor are the price.

rules.statement: A scroll made from a spell of a given level can instead become a random spell of that same level if a crafting mishap occurs; each workweek of scroll-making carries a 10% chance of a complication.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Scribe a Scroll Complications, p. 134 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a complication may change the intended result; dial: 10% per workweek; unreliable preparation is the risk of the process.

rules.statement: After spending 1 workweek and 25 gp to seek a buyer for one magic item, the seller makes a Persuasion check: a result of 1–10 offers half the base price, 11–20 the full price, and 21 or higher 150%. Consumables have half the listed base price, and the seller may refuse an offer but loses the time spent.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Selling a Magic Item, p. 134 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: offers depend on the seller’s negotiation result; dial: the seller may decline; time and exposure to complications are the cost of finding a market.

rules.statement: Religious service at a compatible temple takes 1 workweek and no fee; a Religion or Persuasion check total of 11–20 grants one favor, while 21 or more grants two. A favor can secure temple assistance, social or political backing, half-price cleric spellcasting, or a DM-chosen omen, vision, or minor miracle; unused favors are capped at 1 plus the character’s Charisma modifier, minimum one.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Religious Service, pp. 132–133 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: favors come from service to an aligned temple; dial: the DM determines supernatural aid; limited favor capacity and temple obligations constrain the benefit.

rules.statement: A character can research a declared person, place, or thing by spending 1 workweek and at least 50 gp with library or sage access. The check gains +1 per 100 gp spent beyond the initial 100 gp, up to +6, and especially strong research resources grant advantage; results may yield up to three true pieces of lore.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Research, pp. 133–134 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: research returns limited facts about a chosen subject; dial: spending and research access improve the check; time, money, and unreliable sources limit certainty.

rules.statement: A character relaxing for 1 week while maintaining at least a modest lifestyle gains advantage on saves to recover from long-lasting disease or poison. At the week’s end, the character may end one effect preventing hit-point recovery or restore one reduced ability score, unless the cause is an ongoing magical effect.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Relaxation, p. 132 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: rest can remove one qualifying hindrance or restore one ability score; dial: ongoing magical causes are excluded; a week and modest living costs are required.

rules.statement: One use of perfume gives the wearer advantage for 1 hour on Charisma checks directed at humanoids of challenge rating 1 or lower, and those affected do not realize magic influenced them.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Common Magic Items: Perfume of Bewitching, p. 139 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the advantage applies only to a narrow target group and lasts an hour; dial: none stated; a single-use dose is the limit.

rules.statement: A hat can spend one of its 3 charges to summon a bat, frog, or rat, which appears in the hat, is not under the user’s control, and vanishes after 1 hour or at 0 hit points. The hat regains all spent charges at dawn.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Common Magic Items: Hat of Vermin, p. 138 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the creature is an ordinary, uncontrolled animal; dial: three charges return at dawn; brief duration and lack of command limit its usefulness.

rules.statement: An instrument can expend 1 of its 3 charges while being played to write a message of up to six words on a visible nonmagical surface within 30 feet, in a language the user knows. Bards may add seven words and make it visible in nonmagical darkness; the writing fades after 24 hours unless dispelled sooner, and charges return at dawn.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Common Magic Items: Instrument of Scribing, p. 139 (dnd5e-xanathar#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the message is brief, temporary, and limited to a visible nonmagical surface; dial: bards get more words and optional visibility; charges limit repeated use.

rules.statement: A charged staff can produce one of ten specified bird calls audible within 60 feet by spending one of its 10 charges as an action. It recovers 1d6 + 4 charges at dawn; spending the final charge creates a 1-in-20 chance that it is destroyed.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Staff of Birdcalls (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the finite charges, daily recovery, and small breakage risk; the staff’s limited supply constrains repeated use.

rules.statement: A charged staff can make a harmless, nonmagical flower grow from soil within 5 feet or from itself, spending one charge as an action; it normally produces a mild-scented daisy. It has 10 charges, regains 1d6 + 4 at dawn, and has a 1-in-20 chance of being lost as petals when its last charge is spent.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Staff of Flowers (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the charge limit and modest renewal; the effect is restricted to harmless ordinary plant growth.

rules.statement: After a short rest spent setting up to six phrases of at most six words each and a condition for each, an attuned doll speaks a phrase when its condition occurs within 5 feet of it. The phrases are erased when the user’s attunement ends, and old phrases can be replaced during setup.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Talking Doll (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the small phrase capacity, proximity trigger, setup time, and attunement dependency; the doll cannot react beyond its programmed conditions.

rules.statement: Alcoholic nonmagical drinks consumed from this tankard do not cause inebriation, but it does not protect against magical liquids or harmful substances such as poison.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Tankard of Sobriety (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: block only ordinary alcohol’s intoxicating effect; magical drinks and other hazards remain effective.

rules.statement: The arrow cannot be broken unless it is in an antimagic field.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Unbreakable Arrow (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: prevent breakage in ordinary conditions, with antimagic as the explicit exception.

rules.statement: Speaking the command word while grasping the cane and using a bonus action transforms it into an ordinary longsword, which is no longer magical.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Veteran’s Cane (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the command-word and bonus-action activation; the transformation trades away the item’s magic.

rules.statement: A creature hit by this ammunition must succeed on a DC 10 Strength saving throw or fall prone.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Walloping Ammunition (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated DC and hit-triggered save; the forced fall is limited to a failed save.

rules.statement: A wand with 3 charges can produce orchestral music audible within 60 feet by spending one charge and waving it as an action; the music stops when the waving stops. It regains all charges at dawn, but spending the last charge carries a 1-in-20 chance of destruction.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Wand of Conducting [Page 141] (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the charge economy and dawn recharge; continued sound requires continued waving.

rules.statement: A 7-charge wand can create a harmless, torch-bright burst of colored light at a visible point within 60 feet, with a crackling sound audible within 300 feet, by spending one charge as an action; the light lasts one second. It regains 1d6 + 1 charges at dawn, and spending its last charge has a 1-in-20 chance of destroying it.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Wand of Pyrotechnics [Page 141] (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the finite charges and limited sensory effect; the brief flash and low destruction chance constrain use.

rules.statement: A wand with 3 charges can target a visible humanoid within 30 feet as an action; the target makes a DC 10 Charisma save or is forced to scowl for 1 minute. It recovers all charges at dawn, and spending the last charge gives a 1-in-20 chance that it transforms into the other expression-altering wand.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Wand of Scowls [Page 141] (dnd5e-xanathar#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the charge limit, save, and one-minute duration; the final-charge transformation is an uncommon consequence.

rules.statement: A 5th-level casting animates up to five corpses into controlled creatures that defend themselves unless given an order; they follow an order until its task is complete and become inanimate when the spell ends. Casting with a slot of 6th level or higher animates two more corpses per slot level above 5th.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Chapter 3, Animate Objects (opening passage; page marker absent) (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control lasts only for the spell and is limited by the number of corpses; dial: higher slots raise that limit at the cost of stronger resources.

rules.statement: A nature ward covers an outdoor or underground area from a 30-foot cube up to a 90-foot cube for 24 hours; repeating the casting in the same area daily for a year makes it last until dispelled. It can hold several separately removable effects, protect designated friends or password-speakers from those effects, and animate up to four trees that cannot leave the area.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Druid Grove, page 155 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ward is temporary and its effects can be dispelled one at a time; dial: daily year-long upkeep makes it permanent, while its boundary and immunity rules constrain its reach.

rules.statement: A summoned greater mount is controlled by its summoner, can communicate telepathically while within 1 mile, and shares spells that target only the summoner while they are mounted together. Only one mount bonded by this spell or its lesser counterpart can exist at a time; dismissing it temporarily preserves the bond, while releasing it ends the bond permanently.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Find Greater Steed, page 157 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one bonded mount at a time, with temporary disappearance and resummoning available; dial: the bond’s utility is balanced by its slot limit and permanent release.

rules.statement: A touched willing creature gains the ability to exhale a chosen damage type—acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison—in a 15-foot cone as an action, for up to 1 minute while the caster concentrates. The cone deals 3d6 damage, increasing by 1d6 for each spell-slot level above 2nd.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Dragon’s Breath, page 155 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the borrowed attack requires a willing recipient and concentration; dial: stronger slots increase damage at the cost of the caster’s higher-level resource.

rules.statement: A 9th-level casting can transform up to ten chosen creatures into beasts; unwilling targets can resist with a successful Wisdom save. Each transformed creature uses the beast’s statistics but keeps its hit points, alignment, and personality, and reverts when its temporary hit points are gone, it dies, or the spell ends.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Mass Polymorph, page 162 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation is temporary and can be resisted by unwilling targets; dial: affecting up to ten creatures is paid for with a 9th-level casting and substantial limits on their actions and equipment.

rules.statement: A 5th-level casting summons a devil of challenge rating 6 or lower for up to 1 hour while concentration lasts. Commands it accepts depend on its desires; otherwise the caster must win a contested social check, and one failed check makes it immune to further verbal commands for the spell’s duration. A true-name talisman permits a qualifying devil to be summoned and commanded without those checks.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Infernal Calling, page 159 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the summoned devil remains independently motivated and may resist commands; dial: a talisman removes that negotiation cost, while ending concentration can leave a command-immune devil free to act for 3d6 minutes.

rules.statement: A 2nd-level casting marks one creature with a divinatory link for up to 1 hour; on a failed Wisdom save, the caster always knows its location while both are on the same plane, and invisibility or hiding does not conceal it from the caster.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Mind Spike, page 163 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the tracking link requires a failed save and ends across planes or when concentration ends; dial: its duration trades certainty of location for sustained concentration.

rules.statement: A 3rd-level casting lets the caster take 4d8 necrotic damage so a chosen visible creature regains twice that amount in hit points. Higher slots add 1d8 to the damage rolled, and therefore to the healing calculated from it.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Life Transference, page 161 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: healing is purchased with the caster’s own health at twice the damage suffered; dial: higher slots raise both the benefit and the bodily cost.

rules.statement: A 9th-level casting creates a fortress that lasts 7 days, then sinks away safely with its occupants; casting it at the same spot once every 7 days for a year makes it permanent. Furnishings, food, and other created objects turn to dust if removed from the fortress.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Mighty Fortress, pages 162–163 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the fortress and its contents are bound to a place and normally last only 7 days; dial: repeated weekly casting for a year makes the structure permanent.

rules.statement: A 9th-level casting can turn up to ten visible creatures into beasts; each target keeps its hit points, alignment, and personality but uses the chosen beast’s statistics and cannot use equipment or actions requiring speech or hands. The change ends when its temporary hit points run out, it dies, or the spell ends.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: Mass Polymorph, page 162 (dnd5e-xanathar#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: this high-cost, concentration-based transformation is temporary and suppresses capabilities tied to the former body; dial: broader use affects more targets but risks loss of the altered form when its temporary hit points are depleted.

rules.statement: While concentrated on the spell, up to 1 minute, shadows heavily obscure you, change bright light within 10 feet to dim light and dim light to darkness, and give you resistance to radiant damage. A creature within 10 feet that hits you with an attack takes 2d8 necrotic damage.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: SHADOW OF MOIL, p. 166 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the defensive and retaliatory effects share one concentration limit; dial: shorten the duration or reduce the damage if obscuring and resistance together are too strong.

rules.statement: You can reshape or animate water in a visible area no larger than a 5-foot cube, change its color or opacity, or freeze it if no creature is in it. Movement is limited to 5 feet and cannot deal damage; non-instantaneous changes last 1 hour, and only two such effects can remain active at once, dismissible with an action.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: SHAPE WATER, p. 166 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: small, visible water effects are temporary and capped at two; dial: enlarge the area or allow forceful movement at the cost of greater power.

rules.statement: A prepared, nearly invisible 5-foot-radius rope circle triggers when a Small, Medium, or Large creature enters it; on a failed Dexterity save, the creature is hoisted upside down and restrained. The target can retry its save at each turn’s end, or someone can use an action to succeed on an Arcana check against the caster’s save DC to end the restraint; the consumed rope sets a trap lasting 8 hours.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: SNARE, p. 166 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the trap has a narrow trigger, a size limit, and multiple escape routes; dial: change its duration or the difficulty of escape.

rules.statement: When a visible humanoid within 60 feet dies, you can use a reaction and a silver cage worth at least 100 gp to trap its soul for up to 8 hours. You may exploit the soul up to six times to regain 2d8 hit points, ask a truthful brief question, gain advantage on one imminent roll, or observe a place it saw in life for up to 10 minutes; while trapped, the dead humanoid cannot be revived, and the soul is released after the sixth use or when the spell or cage ends.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: SOUL CAGE, p. 166 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the soul offers several limited benefits but blocks revival; dial: change the use count, duration, or price of keeping the soul.

rules.statement: A summoned demon of challenge rating 5 or lower acts on its own initiative and can be commanded verbally each turn, but at each of its turns’ ends it saves against continued control; success ends your control. If concentration ends early, an uncontrolled demon with hit points remains for 1d6 rounds. A blood circle can prevent it crossing, harming, or targeting anything within the circle, and consumes the blood when the spell ends.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: SUMMON GREATER DEMON, p. 168 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control is tested repeatedly and may fail, with a costly and dangerous aftermath; dial: make control more reliable only by increasing the binding cost or risk.

rules.statement: A temple formed within a cube up to 120 feet per side lasts 24 hours and blocks physical passage and ethereal travel through its exterior. Chosen creature types must save to enter; on a failure they are barred for 24 hours, and on success they suffer a d4 penalty to attacks, checks, and saves inside. Divination sensors cannot appear inside and its occupants cannot be targeted by divination; healing spells of 1st level or higher restore extra hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier, minimum 1. Recasting in the same spot daily for a year makes the temple permanent.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: TEMPLE OF THE GODS, pp. 168–169 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a large, costly-to-cast sanctuary provides strong but localized defenses for one day; dial: vary its size, duration, exclusions, or healing benefit.

rules.statement: You animate one unattached, uncarried Tiny nonmagical object for 8 hours, creating a controlled servant with 10 hit points; at 0 hit points it reverts to its original form and excess damage carries over. As a bonus action, you can mentally direct it within 120 feet, and higher-level slots animate two additional objects per level above 3rd.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: TINY SERVANT, pp. 169–170 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each servant is temporary, fragile, and requires direction; dial: increase its durability or autonomy at the cost of upkeep or control.

rules.statement: You can transmute nonmagical stone in an area up to a 40-foot cube into mud for the spell’s duration, making movement through it cost four times as much and potentially restraining creatures that fail saves. Alternatively, mud or quicksand no deeper than 10 feet becomes soft stone for the duration; creatures may be trapped, and breaking them free requires a DC 20 Strength check or damage to the stone, which has AC 15 and 25 hit points.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: TRANSMUTE ROCK, pp. 170–171 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the alteration is limited to nonmagical material in a fixed area and can trap creatures; dial: change the area, duration, or escape difficulty.

rules.statement: A 5-foot-radius water sphere can restrain up to four Medium or smaller creatures or one Large creature; a target that fails a Strength save is restrained, while a successful save ejects it. As an action, you can move the sphere up to 30 feet in a straight line, carrying restrained creatures; when it ends, they fall prone and the water vanishes.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: WATERY SPHERE, p. 172 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the sphere has a strict capacity, a repeated escape chance, and requires an action to move; dial: alter capacity, mobility, or how easily occupants escape.

rules.statement: A 20-foot-radius storm sphere lasts up to 1 minute with concentration; it is difficult terrain, and creatures inside when it appears or ending their turn there take 2d6 bludgeoning damage on a failed Strength save. Each turn, you can use a bonus action to attack one creature within 60 feet of its center with lightning for 4d6 damage on a hit; listening checks within 30 feet have disadvantage.
locators: Xanathar's Guide to Everything: STORM SPHERE, p. 167 (dnd5e-xanathar#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a persistent area combines movement hindrance, recurring damage, and an optional attack but requires concentration; dial: adjust the radius, duration, or damage.
